i highly recommend dr. goldman. early this year (2020), he performed cataract surgery on both my eyes. the experience was pleasant and with excellent results. for 70 years my driver's license restricted me to driving only with corrective lenses. (yes, i'm 85.). i had substantial correction for astigmatism and nearsightedness. i now have 20/30 vision in one 20/25 in the other. i passed the eye exam at mvd and no longer have a restricted license. i will get a prescription for 20/20 vision in both eyes and for reading, but i may never buy glasses. so far, i see up close and my computer using $20 readers from walgreens. 

i was terrified at the prospect of eye surgery. fifteen months earlier, i canceled cataract surgery at the last minute.  dr. g patiently and with graciousness allowed me to try again. he and his staff had to work me up once again. they were very professional in doing so; they didn't give me a hard time, though i felt they had every right to do so. 

surgery took place at a beautiful new facility just east of pima road and north of via de ventura.  the staff there is different from dr. g's office staff and care for the patients of several doctors. nonetheless, i was made to feel as if they were dr. g's exclusive staff. 

i was guided to a bed separated from other beds by a curtain. a nurse prepped me by installing a port (hope that's correct because my memory of what happens next begins to grow dim due to partial retrograde amnesia - like having a colonoscopy where you're awake but later don't remember being awake). 

i didn't have to change into hospital garb; i even kept my shoes on. they had me lie on a freshly made gurney (not a hospital bed) and gave me a light blanket. i remember meeting the anesthesiologist, who was kind and comforting as i confessed my terror. my next memory is dr. g taping a cup-like device over my eye. he was all done!!  wtf?

i have absolutely no recollection of the surgery.  if asked. i will say i was out; however, dr. g insists i was conscious and talking during the procedure. just like during a colonoscopy.  it was like magic. if i was anxious during the procedure, i have no recollection of it. i assure you i was anything but brave going into it. years ago, my sister told me that when she had cataract surgery she was so far in nana land she felt no anxiety. that helped me. but what assuaged my fear the most was dr. g's competence (he'd been my doctor for several years), the attendant staff and the clean surroundings.

having survived the first surgery, i returned for the second two weeks later - this time without the anxiety of the first. 

i'm not a rookie to surgery. i've had six coronary by-passes, eight coronary stents, a pacemaker, back surgery and surgery for testicular cancer. i was more apprehensive about this procedure than any of the others. there's something about the eyes that scares the you-know-what out of me.  

fear not, however. if you choose dr. g, you'll be in excellent hands. better than a tranquilizer.

i'm plagued with constant sinus problems usually triggered by fragrance.  i no longer wear jewelry, i wear colorful masks with charcoal filters around my neck so at least i can pull it up and have a chance to get away from the  offending toxic cloud before i get that punched-in-the-face feeling.

after a couple of weeks of going through my usual arsenal of treatments, it was time to see a doc.  last time i went to another brand of convenient care.  it was fine. insurance changes and i think maybe acquisition of the other place led me to cvs.

i made an online appointment which is really just a hold my place in line kind of thing.  grabbed my mask and was prepared to dash through a very smelly store to get to the clinic and had my saline rinse in the car to wash out all the chemicals when i was finally out.

there was nearly no wait.  i checked in at the kiosk and it was about 3 minutes.  the nurse practitioner was awesome.  new her stuff and very familiar with my problem.  turns out the sinus issue that i thought was stuck in my forehead had actually caused an ear infection.  when she looked inside my ears as part of the routine exam and came away with the "yikes!" look i almost died laughing.  it couldn't have been any worse if there was  a dead bug in there.

she explained i had an ear infection and i said "so i'm getting both antibiotics and steroids today, huh?" and she laughed and said "yeah, pretty much"

i've been battling this so long i know the drill.  i hate steroids but when you need them you need them.  i'm just grateful to not get hassled when things get mission critical.

we also had a good discussion about antibiotics because i hate them too and the side effects can really suck.  so far no side effects so if the infection goes away and i continue with no problems.. awesome!

the store was cleaner than the average cfs.  the patient room was immaculate.  i wasn't pushed to their pharmacy.  i was asked "what pharmacy would you like me to send this to?"  i really appreciated that!

overall really an a+ experience and exceeded my expectations.
address: 3290 South Fort Apache Rd  CVS Pharmacy

i have a number of autoimmune disorders and take a very heavy-duty immunosuppressant plus another daily, weaker med that does the same thing. so when i get sick, i get significantly sicker than your average patient. i went to the minute clinic last week with a severely swollen and sore throat, low-grade fever, evidence of infection in my sinuses, cough and inflamed lymph nodes. saw a nurse practitioner who took a strep culture and gave me lidocaine for the throat. i have no issue with her treatment, as i feel waiting for results was reasonable.

however, the next day (which is now five days after i initially got sick), i was significantly worse. at this point, my tonsils were swollen so badly, i was worried about it affecting my breathing and i called to see if she could prescribe something while we waited for the strep test. it was a different np this day and she refused to even speak with me and, as it was relayed to me, was "annoyed" i hadn't gone through "proper channels" to ask my question. 

later that day, the strep culture came back negative. the nurse still refused to speak with me, told me through her lpn that it was a virus that just needed to "run its course" and wouldn't listen when i tried to explain that my immune system isn't going to be able to fight it without some medical intervention.

the following day, now day 6, i was still worse, but now i was having chest pain and difficulty breathing. at this point, i went to urgent care and saw an actual doctor who immediately recognized i needed help. he diagnosed me with strep (and told me that a huge percentage of strep cultures give a false negative because they aren't collected properly) that was rapidly developing into pneumonia, plus a bad case of pink eye. 

it's been almost a week now that i've been on antibiotics, steroids and eye drops and i'm slowly recovering. a lot of this could have been avoided, had the provider at cvs actually listened to me and taken my illness seriously. i understand a viral infection won't respond to antibiotics, but the nurse didn't even offer a steroid. she didn't show any care or concern at all. i definitely won't be going back to any minute clinic, as i felt the level of care was very poor.

review:
my pcp recommended dr. jane wolford, who now works with this eye center, but based on his knowledge of her back when she had her own private practice.

i was incredibly disappointed with my experiences, though i suspect they have more to do with the support staff than with dr. wolford herself.

it started when i was first called back into the exam area, where one of the technicians began one of those automatic diagnostics of my prescription. the tech asked me if i was okay with being dilated - which, i figured they needed to ask permission because i would incur an additional charge for dilation. i agreed to pay for dilation, and the tech went ahead and dilated my eyes *before seeing the doctor.*

a short while later, i was in the room, meeting with dr. wolford. one of the reasons she was recommended to me specifically was for her experience with aging eyes. i am over 40 and really having difficulty with my extreme close up vision. i was hoping to specifically address this concern with the doctor.

however - she couldn't address my close-up vision because i had been dilated. dilation makes it so that your eyes can't see close up.

lo and behold, the easiest option was to make a second appointment.

hellooooooo, insurance fraud anyone?? if they had simply waited to dilate my eyes until after seeing the doctor, i could have gotten everything done in one visit. 

okay, no big deal, so i get a second visit, right? 

wrong. at my second visit, guess what? their entire computer system for the entire center had been attacked by a virus and was inaccessible. all the notes from my previous visit weren't available. 

the doctor saw me anyway, did another exam on me, and within 2 seconds declared that i didn't need bifocals (in other words, sorry, you're stuck with your crappy close up vision because old age sucks) and and and ... 

why was i even there?!? why couldn't they have called me that morning to alert me that their system was down and if they couldn't access records, they wouldn't be able to provide me with a quality visit? or if they didn't have access to their appointment information, why not explain to me during check-in that it would be best for me to reschedule for another day? or, why not wait to dilate your patients until after the doctor checks their dang vision???

anyway, after seeing the doctor i try taking my new prescription to the in-house optical center, only to find out that they can't use my current frames, i would need to either pick new frames or go back to the original practice that sold me my frames.

and of course, i got billed for that second visit.

maybe these are all things that are circumstantial, and mostly out of the doctor's control ... but i was so annoyed by the whole thing, i'll be looking for yet another place nearby to get my eyes fixed (this place was the third in longmont that i've tried, and i have yet to get glasses that actually correct my vision).

p.s. i went just now to see the info page on dr. wolford over at the eye center's website - she has a little video there on how she can test for dry eyes. i have always thought that i have dry eyes, but i've never been tested for it. maybe if i don't actually have dry eyes, i might be a candidate for lasik? in any case, i wasn't offered any sort of testing that wolford describes on their website.
fac_name: Eye Care Center of Northern Colorado

physicians here are ok, and depending on your specific condition(s) some are better than others. doctors here give a lot of lip service about how much clinical knowledge they have about specific conditions but understanding may be on a superficial level. doctors here tend to bulk conditions together as well as the associated treatments, sometimes grouping conditions together and making statements that "this and that condition is the same as this condition", when in fact they are nothing alike. doctor's here also look at the patient in pieces rather than a whole system and there are times when you may communicate your source of pain very explicitly, because you of course know your body the best, only to have it dismissed by the doctor as something else or originating elsewhere. after testing only later to be told that you were correct and that you were accurately describing the pain and its location. lol.

lots of pushing shots, which are incredibly painful during and post procedure-- these shots don't have any long term studies on long term effects. shots containing steroids and injected close to the structures of the spine may have the potential to cause additional tissue weakness, osteoporosis or early onset osteoarthritis at the location and/or surrounding location. this can be especially common in those with certain bone and connective tissue disorders/conditions. depending on one's drug metabolism, type of disorder or condition, etc shots may not be as effective for everyone. ime after a round of very painful shots, the side effects that appeared hours later and lasted two weeks were unmanageable. in my case the shots offered no relief relief at all and (in my opinion) turned out to be a waste of money..

other options include pt which always has potential to worsen certain conditions and cause additional damage or injury if the therapist doesn't have a clue about your condition and lumps you in with all the other folks with the same diagnosis code on their order. next option may be actual pain management using medications. of course certain medications require you to sign a guilty plea, i mean contact that can come off as incredibly limiting and sadistic-- which can make normal folks feel like they're doing something wrong by trying to seek relief from their pain with medications that actually work for them. the contract is in place to cover the practices butt mostly and to deter doctor shopping and drug seeking behavior from the folks who need legitimate pain control. the contract is no big deal as long as you follow the guidelines, don't mind peeing in a cup at every visit and being billed for the urine screening.

the contract also requires you to choose one pharmacy and to only use that specific pharmacy; you'll also spend a lot of time over the phone making calls and over explaining, with a mouth full of cotton wedges, to the dentist that just pulled all four of your wisdom teeth that you can't take that script for percocet because you signed a pain contract. then you'll need to power through the dentist's look of distain and explain to that same dentist that she/he needs to call your pain management doctor to let them know that they need to prescribe the medication for your dental extractions. while under the contract you cannot receive opioids from anywhere else, not the er, not the dentist, etc. outside prescribing doctors need to coordinate with your doctor at national spine & pain and s&p will decide if you need the prescription and they will be the one to prescribe it to you. so, lots of anxiety inducing complications and extra steps may occur with the contract if you decide to go that route.

shots and prescribing medications about sums up this practice. if you're looking for services like bracing, the office staff nor doctors offer any assistance with evaluating/choosing bracing, sizing nor ordering of braces, joint splits, etc. physicians aren't all too interested in assisting patients with these requests-- i guess you can't blame them since fluoroscopy assisted procedures involving x-rays, long probes and pricey lidocaine/steroid shots do make a whole lot more money for them than helping a patient fit and choose a joint stabilization device.

updating my review. i have seen a doctor here for a while now (not listing for privacy reasons) who is really great at what they do, and their ma is also outstanding. they have had a sub ma once who was also great. the interactions i have had with the lab, front desk and np's have also been positive.

then there was a nice old couple who had a cold or flu who she scolded for not wearing and carrying face masks as they were leaving.

i haven't taken the time to write a review in a while, but i thought i should share my experience here.

the location was very convenient and the clinic is clean and modern. i came at 9:58am on a saturday and the front desk was ready to see me. justin in the front is great, handed me a simple questionnaire and had me wear a mask when he realized i had flu-like symptoms which i appreciate. he also made sure to let me know (which i already did) that they'll need to contact the office who handles my specific insurance from guam, which i really appreciated. most of my stars are for justin. 

the nurse who took me back was a local girl, really sweet. i didn't get her name but she's very nice, pregnant and works on saturdays. the equipment in the office seems very high-tech and modern. i felt very comfortable while my vitals were taken and i was waiting to see the doctor. 

the only reason i dropped the review from 5 stars to 4 is because of my experience with dr. ohri. she was pleasant, but a bit short with me in that she didn't let me explain all my symptoms before interrupting me a few times and saying she thinks it's the flu. maybe she's just that good, or maybe she's different if you have a scheduled appointment instead of walking in, but i would've appreciated a doctor who'd listen to me before cutting me off - even if she knew what my issue was. 

they did a flu swab and dr. ohri made sure to let me know it'd take a while which i appreciated. it came back and she was right, it was the flu. i'd never doubt her diagnostic skills, but like i said it would've been nice if she had listened to me all the way through. by the end, she did ask me if i had any questions which is maybe where i should've shared my other symptoms, so maybe that's my fault. i was just so irked at how ready she seemed to get me out of there that i couldn't wait to leave either. like i said - maybe it's different if you have a scheduled appointment, but in a clinic that regularly sees urgent care patients, i expected more.

er is never going to be a good experience and in the midst of the coronavirus pandemic, it's for sure going to add to the overall lack of cohesion.
last night, i was in an accident. & i felt terrible, nauseous, sore, i had the chills and had trouble keeping my balance.
fremont er is a mess! they were making a half ass attempt to separate potential pandemic sufferers from those who had to go there on account of other injuries.
they do not have enough beds and in typical nurses gallows humor, the staff could be heard frequently joking about coronavirus and the clear toll it was taking on their lack of planning and inefficient operation. one staffer knocked over a hazmat bin & laughter it off. my doctor probably possesses medical knowledge but is no healer and her lack of interpersonal skills with me and the other patients  i observed was dismal and lacking. because they are out of beds, they placed myself in others on chairs or standing in hallways while staff whizzed by with large instruments/machines/beds and ran into at least 3 waiting patients just by my count. literally knocking these patients to the ground. clearly, these guys are understaffed abs overwhelmed. i was very cold and suffering muscle spasms from the accident i was in, i requested a blanket especially since i was pretty sure i'd be waiting for hours when i told the nurse i was unusually cold, she accused me of having drug or alcohol withdrawals in a mocking and dismissive tone. that really pissed me off. while i understand that opioid abuse is a thing, i sure as he'll wasn't in effing er because of that. my doctor finally saw me 3 hours later, took a a cursory look, wrote me some random prescriptions and shooed me away. despite my lack of mobility and my symptoms, she asked a couple questions and absented them herself and cut me off. clearly she was stressed to the gills and in over her head in the er environment.
kaiser needs to beef up their infrastructure in fremont. staff needs to be supported. they need serious leadership. they deserve better. staff needs to learn the art of empathy even in the everyday struggle of craziness that is an er. we deserve better.

i've been going to arc far west for the past two years just for annual physicals because they take my insurance. the service has been eh-- nothing great/nothing awful. this past december i had some test results come back which they shared over the phone. i asked some additional questions but they told me they couldn't specify the strain of the virus. next they referred me over to obgyn for further testing & to ask more specific questions i had because the regular nurse didn't have the expertise. the obgyn denied that referral & refused to talk to me further until i had an appointment, so i called back to the other nurses who refused to answer my questions which left me sol with no information. 

since then i've found a new doctor at st. davids that listens to my concerns. she's awesome. offers me treatment options. and actually communicates with me when i have questions. 

last night when i called up arc to get their exact words on what my chart said about the tests in december because it's relevant to my current health status, i found to my disgust that it wasn't that they didn't know the exact strain. it was just that they couldn't tell me over the *phone* though i could get hard copies of the charts...which no even mentioned. very frustrating. if you have other options that your insurance will cover, i'd look into them.

details02/02/2020
my stonington experience started with the detox. 9 days. they use ativan for alcohol detox. they tapered me too fast which resulted in an er visit and 7 days in a psychiatric hospital where i was given valium to taper more appropriately. 

i spent about 20 hours at the rehab in groton after the detox. the withdrawal from the ativan hit at 11pm, and i didn't get seen by the psychiatrist until almost 10am. i didn't sleep for 40 hours straight between the detox, the 20 hours at the rehab and getting a bed at the hospital. i spoke to 3 people in trails corner about my condition and got no help whatsoever. when i finally had sat through a 15 minute class on handwashing and walked over to the other building i talked to the clinician who finally listened to me and thought a man in severe withdrawal and suicidal thoughts might need help. i then saw the psychiatrist who called the ambulance. 

concerning the environment at the rehab dormitory:
-there are no actual clinical staff available.
-each room has about 12 bunk beds and 1 bathroom. 
-the windows are almost all frosted like a shower door so you get light, but you can't see outside. 
-there is no visitation except for court ordered dcf visits 
-you can only get stuff dropped off between 10am and 2pm m-f.
-drugs are sold and used. 
-the staff is indifferent at best.
-it took 6 days to get them to send my belongings to the hospital.
-they failed to send my medications that i had brought there.
-they assigned me to a top bunk. i am 6'3" 230lbs, late 40's with back issues. i asked to be given a bottom bunk within 20 minutes of being there and was told i needed a doctor's order to change the bed. 
-no hygienic products are provided. 
-no electronic devices are allowed, including mp3 players.
-there is no comfortable or quiet place to sit; either lay in bed or sit on plastic chairs with a tv mounted 10 feet up on the wall. 
-the gym was not open. 

i was only there for 20 hours. i can't imagine what 45 days are like. the dorm is more like a minimum security prison than a treatment facility. 

i have no thoughts about the groups and classes since i ended up in the er instead.

review: first and foremost, i understand and agree that for the majority of us the risk from covid-19 virus is very low.  i agree there is no need to panic.  however, this morning while making breakfast and lunches i spilled my coffee over what a doctor from lake forest hospital said. (i didn't catch the doctors name, however i'm sure it will be easy for the hospital to figure out who was answering questions on the radio.)  a woman called in  and was saying she isn't sure if she should take her family and young children on a plane to florida ( i think) for spring break because of the virus. the doctor told her that flying on a plane is perfectly safe....(next is what made me spill my coffee.)  the doctor stated that the air filtration systems on planes are much better than people think, and they remove the virus, so there is no reason to worry about catching the virus on the plane. a doctor said that.  you don't need to be a doctor to understand at this point that this virus is not being spread in the air.  it is being spread person to person, person to surface, and surface to  person.  lake forest hospital and its parent northwestern need to get a hold of this doctor and reprimand him for giving false information.  again, i understand for most of us, including a young family the risk is low.  however, stating that on the radio when there are possible seniors and others at risk listening is dangerous.  an elderly person with chronic condition may hear that and say "well, if a doctor associated with northwestern says its ok to fly because of the planes air filtration systems, then it must be safe.  i'm sure northwestern will reply to this with its usual legal speak of possible miscommunication by the doctor.  unacceptable, statements like that doctor made put peoples lives at risk, especially elderly with chronic conditions.  the is no air filtration system on any plane that can remove the covid -19 virus.  shame on lake forest hospital and northwestern

awful awful. we were there monday the 3rd and wednesday the 5th of february. there was no one there when we walked in. blood and x-rays were taken. it took over 3 hours to get a diagnosis which was low magnesium. my husband also mentioned he had chills. the diagnosis for that was a virus.  wednesday we were back in the er again. my husband couldn't stop shaking. again they did exactly the same tests and x-rays they did monday. why the same exact tests were done is beyond me. could it be that we have very good insurance. diagnosis, a virus. i asked the dr. if that is a catch all that they use when they don't know what is wrong and he said yes.  hopefully we will not have to visit an er again. if so we will be using the spartanburg medical center. it certainly can't be any worse. today is friday the 7th. our gp just called to let my husband know he has a strep infection.
this is something that should have been detected on our  first er visit.
the minute clinic at cvs could have diagnosed this immediately. like i said they knew we had good insurance.

this urgent care is well prepared for the covid-19 outbreak, and has procedure masks for all patients to wear. you can also register your appointment time so you don't have to wait in the waiting room long, and can more easily maintain social distancing. you can also wait in your car and they will text you when they are ready to see you. ashley answered my questions concerning their isolation procedures over the phone, a nurse took my vitals, and dr toth answered my questions and adequately alleviated my concerns. i went in to check on a respiratory infection and to rule out walking pneumonia but i neither needed a prescription or a chest x-ray. he was able to tell from my vitals and appearance that i was doing fine and how to prevent spreading anything as long as i didn't cough or sneeze on anyone. i would visit this clinic again, as they were friendly, professional and were taking reasonable measures to prevent the spread of the coronavirus. anyone with a fever can be tested at the next door providence hospital facilities that are designed for that. you need to have a fever (100 or above) and/or recently traveled to/from the affected area.

i don't know if it was the timing of my visit, coinciding with this coronavirus hysteria, but to tell you honestly they could've done much better to instill some confidence in me. instead, i got the vibe that they were scared as hell. i understand the wait time and that it's longer during flu season, and that the walk ins don't get priority over online registrations. but when i'm sitting there for 2 hours with a child who has dangerously high fever and those who come after me don't exhibit life threatening symptoms get admitted way before me, that i don't understand. there should also be a priority to how bad the situation is. i had to walk up to the counter and complain for them to take the vitals. and even after that and seeing how high her fever was, we still waited another 45 min to be taken into the room. when i go to a medical establishment i expect for the professionals to give me some sort of reassurance. what i got was a treatment like my child had a plague or something, talking to my daughter from 6 feet distance, by the book. people, we need to show more compassion for other human beings and not treat them like they're a walking virus. if that's what you're afraid of, you shouldn't be in a medical field. yes the place was clean, yes there was coffee and water (shouldn't that be the standard?) even before i was seated to wait i was charged the fee. wait, but the doctor hasn't even seen me, and i don't know if i want to wait! no one asked. i don't want to sound unthankful, they told me what i already knew all along, gave me the prescription and off i went. but i'll think twice before i go there next time.

they do not have tests for covid-19.  nor did they have any information. i asked where i could find out and the front desk said they don't have any information and if i wanted to pay to see a dr that's all they can do.  for a medical facility i would expect more information.  not helpful at all!

what a wonderful experience.  i had been feeling off for the past two weeks, with general fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and migraines.  i've never received an iv treatment before, so i very much went into this appointment with a "what could it hurt" attitude.  i was so pleasantly surprised with the experience and results! 

it was incredibly easy to book a same-day appointment online.  when i arrived, kara, the np, explained their offerings and listened to what i was hoping to get out of the treatment.  together, we decided on the fatigue fighter, with toradol added.  the administration of the iv was excellent--fast and painless.  the overall experience was relaxing--reclining chairs, cucumber water, and eye masks.  i also had the opportunity to chat with debbie, the owner, which was wonderful.  it's always cool to hear about a person's motivations for starting a business and it was evident that she cares about helping people feel better.  and it did help me feel more energized and focused!  i look forward to returning in a couple weeks.

avoid this facility at all costs and get medical care in la if you can. when my father was in the hospital due to complications from cancer, the doctors assigned to him rotated in and out, didn't communicate well with each other and wouldn't meet with us to give a care recommendation (standard procedure at other hospitals). it was highly confusing and detrimental to my father's care. one doctor even took me to task when i disagreed with the recommendation of discharging my father (who had a rare form of leukemia and was too sick to leave) and pushed back. this doctor told me that if my attitude didn't change, my dad wouldn't get good care. the hospital administrator was listening to the conversation and didn't say or do anything. apparently, they don't support families who advocate for their parents and this doctor never heard of the hippocratic oath. the majority of the nurses don't practice good hygiene, which is dangerous to patients. just a few examples: one dropped a needle on the floor, picked it up and tried to reuse it on my father (whose immune system was so weak that he was in protective isolation, i.e, visitors were required to wear gowns, gloves and masks). another nurse didn't wash her hands -- and didn't put on gloves when she touched my father. i had to constantly ask them to wash their hands and wear gloves -- and was given attitude about it. and there were other patients with infectious diseases on the floor. my father wasn't moved regularly or given a proper bed for a long-term stay so he ended up with multiple bed sores. he also contracted a staph infection/mrsa (not a surprise given lack of proper hygiene at the hospital). our family had to take shifts sleeping in his room/icu because we were afraid to leave him unattended. who knows what else would have happened if we weren't there 24/7? after nearly a month of sub-par care, a more compassionate and competent doctor was assigned to my father. this doctor immediately understood my father's medical needs, realized the hospital couldn't support them, and signed off on a transfer. the minute we reached the other facility in la, the quality of care vastly improved -- along with the caliber of the doctors and nurses. the rooms were clean and all the of staff practiced high standards of hygiene. in hindsight, i should have sued the hospital for malpractice on behalf of my father. i've moved on but feel compelled to warn others to avoid this hospital of horrors.

this experience is absurd in so many ways! i am reminded why dr tran is no longer the best option for compassionate, quality care. i have observed his office staff, nurses, and assistants as rude and incompetent. it was nice dr tran (for a  little while anyways!)

i was so happy that i received a facial and laser therapy last week, and it was such a positive experience!!! my skin is glowing and i received many compliments on my skin texture, tone, and how clean it looked!! the aesthetician who gave me a facial took out blackheads and gave me a facial massage and mask with light therapy.  the nurse who did the skin laser was very detailed and thorough lightened the sunspots on my face. i enjoyed meeting with marie the manager who is very friendly, kind, and knowledgeable, and i could tell she really enjoyed seeing people happy and with better skin!!! i really liked how the spa felt relaxing and luxurious and i bought a package so that i could go back!!! so happy!!!

i would not recommend this pharmacy.  i used this pharmacy for over a year and finally had to leave.  they will not call when they tell you they will.  they tell you they are ordering your medication and it takes over a week and having to call and reorder several times.  when they choose, they will not answer the phone because "they are busy".  i had to leave my house and drive there to ask a question about my medication.  i would show them i was still on hold and they would just shrug their shoulders and say "we are busy".  they will not even answer the phone for insurance companies.  my insurance called and they would put her on hold then hang up several times.

my experience here was not good.  i brought in my 13 year old son for a sore throat after checking in online.  at the front desk, we were greeted by an extremely unpleasant receptionist.  as a matter of fact, she was so unfriendly that i considered mentioning something about it to the nurse when she called us back, but then decided just to let it pass.  as there was only one patient ahead of us, we were quickly called back into an exam room and were told that the nurse practitioner would be in shortly to see us.  after waiting forty-five minutes in the exam room, i finally stepped out of the room to make sure we weren't forgotten about.  when the nurse practitioner eventually came into the room, the first thing i noticed was that she was wearing a face mask.  i'm 43 years old and have never seen a care provider, whether it was a primary care physician or a specialist, walk into an exam room and complete an exam for something as simple as a sore throat, wearing a face mask.  i understand that the coronavirus is currently a large concern, but the check-in paperwork we completed clearly stated that the patient had not visited china or been in contact with anybody who had recently visited china.  the nurses in the office  weren't wearing face masks, only this nurse practitioner.  between the unfriendly receptionist, the unacceptable 45-minute wait in the exam room, and the face mask, i will not be returning or recommending this place.

i saw one of the doctors and went over the information i was experiencing. the doctor checked me out. was very friendly, but didn't end up communicating to her staff what was communicated to me. i have crohn's disease and had been experiencing issues with it. she ordered blood work and asked me to get a cat scan as well as ordering my two prescriptions. neither prescription was sent over to the pharmacy for two days. finally on the second day after multiple calls with sanitas, the pharmacy says i only have one prescription. so now. i've got to make another appointment, still have gone without the medication and will need to pay another co-pay somewhere else. to get the medication i already went to the doctor for.

i have been a patient of dr. bieley going on 9 years.  when i first started with dr. bieley, thyroid, adrenal, and female hormones were abnormal.  i was in severe adrenal fatigue  & bordering thyroid and adrenal crisis and i had nutritional imbalances.  i was irritable, anxious, hair falling out.  my mood was all over the place.  my thyroid antibodies were off the chart.  my joints hurt all the time.  when i first met with him, he was knowledgeable, caring and patient.  we had an in-depth conversation that lasted a few hours.  i felt like i was heard for the first time.  he said it would take a long time to get everything back to normal because my problems didn't happen over night.  today, i am calm.  i can think clearly.  my mood is stable and i have energy to get through the day.  i'm not saying that i'm back to perfect health but i am a better than when i first met him and he started to treat me.  we have a partnership with my health.  i highly recommend that you work with him to heal your body.

my son got sick on vacation, went to the hospital in panama city where dr. rubina saw him for 20 minutes and tried to transfer him to another hospital because a lab result came back abnormal... other labs were not considered and the medical necessity to have him taken by ambulance was not needed.  

when we arrived back home, the doctors took all of the lab work into consideration and sent us home.  he is fine and simply had a virus.

did not and would not feel comfortable with her care.

tiffany is amazing! words cannot express how thankful i am that she has been there for me the past year. it is evident how devoted she is to her patients and how she genuinely cares about them as people. she is always so level headed, calm and reassuring, especially during these crazy and anxiety provoking times. when she was working in coronado, i always left her office feeling more calm than i felt when i walked in. i am so excited to continue working with her and i am so proud of her for her new endeavor! not to mention, i try and recommend her to all my friends because she is simply the best!!

no appointments after 4pm and no actual help. can't get a mask that fits after my old one was discontinued. new head gear broke because it doesn't fit... not their problem. have to wait a month to get a new one. tried 3 times (each time taking time off work because of their hours) to have a mask fitting to get a mask that works. hate full face mask but told no other option. guess i wear my 2 year old one til it breaks.

well westmed has done it again. i called in the morning asking them, if they can do some blood work, that i had a prescription for. i was told yes, i can go to purchase location or westchester ave. 
so at 2:00pm i show up to a locked down westmed, due to the corona virus. i pass screening go upstairs in this now ghost town, hand over the script and am told, we can't do it, has to be authorized by my primary doctor. however my primary dr has retired and i have appointment with my new dr in 7 days. sorry we can't help you. now, i have just had bi lateral knee surgery and need to go back in for a small procedure which requires anesthesia. we are so sorry. can you imagine a patient that they have my full medical history, they can't do a simple blood test? i'm 6 weeks post op and they tell me go someplace else. so i left went to greenwich hospital lab. within 10 min blood work was done no past history no referrals just very nice people. 
i wish westmed owners only have westmed and their staff to treat them in a medical emergency.
great skincare service consisting of thorough cleansing, neck and shoulder massage, and mask. my 50-year-old skin glowed afterward. i would go here every month if it was closer to my house.

the one star is for the coffee/food service staff, and one security guard in the morning. 

after being "transferred" from another hospital to pch i check my daughter in having a fractured tibia. she had x-rays done at the first hospital and the doctor there rushed us out saying how my daughter needed to be seen by a child specialist and pch is the best, they stated they contacted them and they had a bed for her. i declined the ambulance transfer since i would be covering this cost out of pocket. once at pch it was apparent every sick child in the valley was there. i put a mask on my daughter and we took a seat. 
once called up for triage about 45min later i informed the nurse that my daughter had a does of morphine at the other hospital and i was concerned that she was not being monitored closely. he stated her vitals we normal, she was fine. i then told him we were sent from another hospital, they told us there was a room for us and my daughter was really uncomfortable since she has a broken leg. he told me they always tell people this we had to wait. 
okay i understand couple 3 hours in the er naturally, 6 i repeat 6 hours later! mind you, my baby was freezing, she broke her leg at cheer i was not prepared for a cold all night stay in the er, i asked repeatedly for a blanket, we slept snuggled on a couch thing they have, and i watched her breathing all night because i was afraid of shock. 
once called back the nurse was sweet, i was completely out of it, no sleep, stress, worry, the list goes on... doctor came in to say her leg was broke, um duh, he was going to get her more medicine, and ct scan, 4 more hours later a new doctor comes in all i want to do at this point is leave but we came here for a damn ct scan so thats what i asked for, 2 more hours later i made an appointment banner children's specialist. 
i informed them i was going somewhere else for her surgery since it obviously was not nearly as emergent as the other hospital made it. at that point nurses became indignant when i asked for the records i provided when i got their. they literally lost my x-rays. in fact the nurse told me "i can call back and make a complaint if i don't like the way i am being treated". those people were just starting their 12 hr shift and were getting paid to be rude to a worried mother. good job. unfortunately, this was my first experience with pch and i will not be returning. i will pay my bill and pretend they don't exist. if your child has an emergency please call the ambulance because walking into this place is a joke.

if i could give less than 1 star i would. i came in with my sister, who is pregnant, because her husband had gotten us a gift certificate. when we arrived they told me i sounded "stuffed up," despite never having met me, and then told me that that is apparently their screening process to prevent the staff from being infected with coronavirus.

they couldn't process the gift certificate despite my brother in law being present and my sister's name being on the certificate, but even after we offered to just pay, as we were being escorted back, we were stopped by the same woman who asked if i was stopped up, who now decided they could not serve my sister due to her pregnancy. my sister had called in advance just a few hours before and was told a cryofacial was totally fine.

after this experience i said i was no longer interested in a treatment. we walked away and the "manager" followed tearfully and informed us they might have to close due to staff issues. like i care. they might have to close due to utter incompetence. after meeting them i am very glad none of the people there were entrusted with spraying frozen liquid nitrogen, or whatever cryotherapy is, on my face. 

go if you like bad customer service.

had the absolutely worst experience there ever. sunny the assistant came in and assisted me but was handling me without gloves on. when i asked what was on her wrist because they looked like scars she said that they were warts that she got from a patient. which was mind boggling that she said this so casually as she was handling me without gloves. secondly, she did a biopsy on my blue mole and cut so much of the flesh off, the wound still hasn't healed over a month later and the cut looks completely mutilated. i've had this procedure done before and they made a clean cut and it healed in no time but sunny did a botched job. i would not recommend anyone see sunny. she broke medical protocol for not having gloves on especially with such a contagious virus as hpv on her wrist and she has no idea how to properly take a biopsy.

awful. triangle womens center is utterly disorganized and unprofessional bordering on incompetent. every time i was there they had booked 15 patients for the same appointment times with 2 only doctors. i sat in the waiting room for an hour and 15 minutes minimum before going in. none of the records are computerized but written down on a piece of printer paper each time. this means they never knew my medical history and would ask me about it every time. i would go in for prenatal exams and they wouldn't even know what week i was in. on the days i got to see the doctor instead of the midwife she would rush in and rush out in 4 minutes. i called after her on her way out the door one time and to ask her to wait because i had questions and she stood in the open door while i listed my personal medical questions and then gave it a sweeping "nope. all normal." and ran out. whenever i got bloodwork done i would have to hunt them down for the results. it would take multiple calls before they could connect me to someone who knew the results. i finally decided to transfer to a different practice to have my baby and the new practice needed my medical records from twc. they have my medical release form and even still, it has taken me over a month to get them to send my records. every time i call, someone tells me they will let someone know and then nothing happens. a couple of times i have even been hung up on by irritable women at the front desk! i honestly don't know how they are still in practice. i am not a "yelper". i have never written a yelp review before, but my experience with twc was so incredibly bad that i felt it was important to try and warn others.  do not go to them!

brought our toddler here after a 6 day stomach virus.
our pediatrician suggested pm peds because they're open late and have iv. from the moment i walked in i have felt relaxed and cared for. friendly and attentive reception, very clean waiting area. beautiful murals for the kids and tvs with disney jr. in every room to keep kids distracted. the doctor was attentive, a great listener and knowledgeable. also, they offered me water, coffee, tea or snacks. i mean...5 stars plus 10. so at least 15.

this was my first time to visit a next level urgent care. i will be encouraging friends and family to use this clinic.
the check-in was easy and fast. i waited only a few minutes to see np dubose. she diagnosed my throat and nose problem as a virus but prescribed an antibiotic because i was starting to show signs of a bacterial infection. and the little anti-cough pills she prescribed have stopped my cough before my ribs had a chance to get sore. like arnold says "i.b.b."

absolutely the worst possible phone service.  even before the coronavirus panic, the wait times were intolerable.  now it is torture to try to get through. and all i want to do is find out if i accidentally left my cell phone at a doctor's office. after 20 minutes on hold, the voice told me i had to leave a call back number.  yeah, right.

i'm not typically a reviewer but when i saw their rating i was shocked, just goes to show not enough of us share the good.  i've been coming here for years with good reason. the front desk staff is courteous and efficient and demonstrate real interest in their clients. the massage therapists and esthetician's have always been great. i've been going to robert for years, he's responsive and just an excellent therapist all around, he keeps me moving  the facility is clean and right now we are in what i suspect is the early part of the covid-19 pandemic and they are using excellent precautions to take care of their clients, staff and facility.

i was getting ready to give a bad score like everyone else but one of the nurse practitioners changed my mind.
i originally received consultation from traci ngan le, i was very disappointed with her bedside manner, she talks down to you and makes you feel dumb. i had low libido, erectile dysfunction, low energy etc. i suspected low testosterone, so we tested twice and both times my results came back low, however she suggested that it was most likely a psychological problem and was reluctant to test me again or treat me. i convinced her to test me one more time, she ends up ordering the wrong type of test. lucky for me my next visit was with nurse practitioner daniel, he reviewed my case, asked a lot of questions, explained things much more clearly and ordered the correct test for me. on top of that he told me i did not have to wait a month to come back ( a month between appointments is common here) he offered to call me and discuss my results as soon as them came in. sure enough my testosterone came back low and he prescribed me treatment. i just began treatment recently and i already feel a difference, i am so grateful to nurse practitioner daniel for listening and helping me, i'm starting to feel like my old self again. the staff have been awesome every time i've visited, but the star of this show is definitely nurse practitioner daniel.  according to my personal experience and many of the reviews on here, this is a very sub par consult, and other than daniels excellent quality of service, i would have to agree with the other negative reviews.

i had my first kidney stone experience ever and was in so much pain i decided to call the ambulance to help take me straight to the emergency. worst mistake of my life...
3:00pm: the austin ems ambulance is a joke taking more than 30 minutes to arrive to pick me up, two heavy built male medical ems staff took me into the vehicle and started interviewing and collecting my information, taking their sweet time parking at one place not driving me to the hospital for another 30 minutes. i have to beg for pain meds and they gave a shot for it but poorly directed the needle causing me unbearable pain i literally scream from so much pain!
4:30pm: the ambulance arrived at st david's south austin er walk-in, to my surprise i did not immediately get to see the doctor but had to wait in line to be checked in! omg, the torturous wait and the unbearable pain. i asked if i can have a bed to wait, no, sitting hurts me so much i cried the whole time waiting...
5:30pm: i had to go the bathroom and they called my name finally but i was in too much in pain to run out so i crawled out slowly and they told me i have to wait again because they skipped me! why did they not check the bathroom???
5:50pm: they called my name i thought i was finally saved, but a nurse took me inside a chair just to collect my insurance info and gave me a name tag, then sent me back out to wait some more. i begged for more pain meds as the old pain meds worn out, no, they cannot give me any meds until i see a doctor...at this time i'm heavily considering laying on the floor due to so much pain. i threw up 3 times in the bathroom and was heavily dehydrated, i begged a nurse for some water, he said he will go get me some, he never came back...i had to drink some water from the bathroom sink to stay alive. i continued crying in pain waiting and no tears came out since i'm so dehydrated....
6:50pm: they called my name again i thought i was finally saved again, but this time they took me to a chair to put iv on me to draw my blood and get urine test only. the nurse lady was so incompetent she had to poke me twice to find my vein, the first time she was probing with the large needle giving me excruciating pain while watching how incompetent she was. she continued to probe me the second time i felt like i should just die already, blood splatters everywhere and i saw old blood stain under the chair...still refused to give me water but agreed to give me pain meds finally. i beg for a bed, no, they have no bed available and i have to continue to wait in the waiting area. i got fever chills after all the blood drawn and beg for a blanket, no, they can't give me blanket to prevent contamination...no water, no blankets, no ability to lay down, no time frame to see doctor, constant excruciating pain, i was ready to just die...
7:30pm: finally got a bed, right out in the hallway with a number on the hallway wall. still not allow me to drink any water, a new nurse came to take more blood samples from me, poking and probing at my small veins at multiple places half jokingly complained my vein was so tiny (i'm so dehydrated of course my vein is tiny!!!). gave me ct scans, and concluded i got kidney stone...
10:00pm: gave me some prescription drugs, made me signed a bunch of forms to pay medical bills when it comes and dismissed me...

i've never been treated so badly in my life! 5.5 hours of torture! austin ems and this er sees me as nothing but a number and an object to poke at and probe without feelings...gravely disappointed at the american health system, and to say we are fully prepared for covid19, what a joke!
fac_name: St David's South Austin Medical Center

review: fitchoice foods is delicious and convenient. my favorite is the chicken and the breakfast burrito. i have been ordering from them for years! it's nice not having to worry about making my meals and you can't beat the price for what you get. plus the owners are super nice.

set up my appointment today, quick and easy. filled all necessary documents online, greeted promptly , everything's perfect and efficient, the front desk quick check-in, vital check up, pn came and performed a thorough check and got my test result back in 10 mins. the minus one star was when i was ready to go, i asked the front desk (not the same one who checked me in) if i can get a couple of masks to bring home because of my cough, she said "no, sorry the masks are for our patients only!

hmm.. i asked for a couple of masks not a box of masks! i guess once you check out of their system you are no longer their patients.

covid-19 denier.

i had a strange experience with the pharmacist at neergard on 5th ave, brooklyn. our dog has severe epilepsy and needs daily medication. any interruption would put her immediately in very high danger. we are trying to take reasonable precautions in the event of a severe coronavirus epidemic in nyc. after discussion with our vet, he prescribed us a 3-months supply, so we wouldn't run out. friday evening (2/28), i went to fill this at neergard on 5th ave. they were only willing to fill 1 month. when i asked why, they said i needed to talk to the pharmacist, which i then did. he asked me why i wanted a 3-months supply, and i explained. he then said that my concern about the virus was just hysteria, that there were maybe 2 cases in the us, and that the whole thing would be over "next week". i asked him on what he was basing this. he didn't answer, and instead asked what i was basing my concern on (i mentioned the cdc). he also stated that the stock market was manipulated, and that one really should look at the 900 point gain in the last 2 hours of trading on friday.

i'm going to use a different pharmacy in the future.

i am a new patient for dr. chamberlain and i called to make an appointment as i seem to have a stomach virus. i was told she could see me in 4 weeks! you have a doctor so when you get sick you can see them and making you wait for weeks is ridiculous.. i will be better by then! i was told that once i established myself with her then we could make other arrangements but from what i can see in her reviews she's two weeks out or later which is still ridiculous. let's be honest you should be able to see your doctor within a couple days of calling them so your illness can be addressed and taken care of. having to wait more than 5 days is totally absurd. they said i could see a nurse practitioner but it was still going to be more than a week and i have found that most nurse practitioners are not up to the task. at this point it looks like i will be like many other reviewers and we'll be trying to find a new doctor who actually wants to treat patients in a timely manner

i was so looking forward to loving this gym. 

things didn't start well when i told the person at the desk i was new and presented my yelp "check in for a free session".... and she wouldn't accept it. 

so fyi they don't honor the yelp deal they have listed on here. 

so i paid $25 to drop in since i was there and had been driving most of the day and didn't want to deal with figuring out a plan b 

i took a group class in the afternoon. the class itself was decent. the music was almost prohibitively loud. the exercises at the different stations were good, and varied. it was a big group, but i didn't see the instructor correct anyone's form even once which is not awesome. 

especially not awesome was that a state of emergency was just declared here for corona virus, and the teacher was telling us to shake hands, high 5 each other very frequently. i'm not prone to hysteria about corona and not a germophobe (clearly, was at a gym, which at baseline are very dirty places), but some precautions are just reasonable and easy to take. like wear a seatbelt. like don't touch the sweaty people in your gym class. we were already sharing equipment, no reason we couldn't have mostly maintained the cdc recommended 6' of personal space.

i love doc stover!  i met doc a few years back and have recommend him to so many of my family and friends and they feel the same way.

it starts with his approach.  he doesn't try to mask the issue for short term relief, but treats for long  term health.  some may not value that, but i do!

next, he has been there and done that.  after i heard his past, i became more confident that i was in the right place for treatment... i.e. getting adjusted. 

last, he's a good guy, he cares!

i bee doing this cleans for 5 years now i do it twice a year. and when your on the cleans you know your on it. i recently just bought it again it's been two weeks and nothing the product is definitely not the same and i'm saddened to even say this because i'm such an advocate of dr sebi and his work but whoever is running it now is cutting down the product i guess the powers that be got their hands when they need to be at. it's a sham but i won't be ordering from there no more.

i've taken my daughter here for quite some time now and it's been ok or subpar to say the least. but, i am now changing pediatricians after this last straw. i took my daughter in who's 8 because she seemed to have strep. doctor dee told me she doesn't have strep, she probably has rsv (a respiratory virus that has been sending kids to the hospital at times). she then said she won't test for it because it's uncomfortable for kids (it's a q-tip up the nose and yes it is uncomfortable, but not dire). i asked if she could please test for it. keep in mind this all happened in front of my kiddo. she said, "why? if she doesn't have rsv, she has something else." i'm pregnant and need to know this info even if the treatment doesn't change. i still need to know. that's why we pay to get our kiddos seen by a professional. she proceeded to ask why and was hesitant and then finally had the nurse do the test. my daughter tested negative and doc sent the nurse in to tell me. the unprofessional-ism in this place is nuts.

i had my first ever facial today (at 37 y.o.) with larissa. after having break-outs and unusually dry skin the past few months, i finally looked into facials, and was excited to find luxury skin just minutes from my home and they had sunday hours! larissa was so sweet, easy to talk to, and spent time consulting with me before my facial to learn my areas of concern and decide which type of facial to do. after discussing my dry skin, hormonal break-outs, and persistent black heads on my nose, larissa recommended a dermal infusion with vitamin c to hydrate my skin.   the dermal infusion machine is like a little vacuum that sucks all the gunk out of your pores, while exfoliating you're skin and infusing it with a serum. larissa then did a rose scented jelly mask and gave me a hand, shoulder and scalp massage while the mask dried!! my skin is super soft, glowy and clear!
thank you for my amazing first facial, larissa! i feel like a new woman:). i can't wait to start using my new skincare products. i highly recommend larissa, and i will for sure be back for more luxurious skin treatments soon!

i visited this clinic on sunday, my symptoms started getting worse on thurs and i tried to do what i could at home to prevent having to go see a  doctor.  of course i got worse over the weekend so i decided to go to medpost. i was feeling really bad. the staff was pleasant but the dr. i saw was asian, if you've been there before you know who im speaking of. he walked in and greeted me and then asked where did work. couldn't understand why he asked that question; and then he handed me the hand sanitizer after shaking hand first.  little does he know i carry my own. finally asked what was the problem, checked my upper respiratory and concluded i was fine, was told  i had a virus after telling him my ear was hurting, sinus congestion and laryngitis. i only got a rx for a cough and was told to get claritin. the next day i was feeling even worse so i called that morning to see if i could get in as a work-in and thankfully i did. my dr. examined me and told me my ear that was hurting was red, throat was red and a lot was going on in my sinuses. mind you i had just saw this urgent care dr. the day before.  my dr. placed me on antibiotics, allegra d and something for my cough. thank god i decided to go see my primary dr. i paid for services not rendered at that place. i'll think twice before going there again.
fac_name: MedPost Urgent Care of La Quinta

review:
this place needs to be shut down. 
they either need their staff to be retrained completely or a complete new staff. 
i work in the healthcare industry and what i saw was just appalling. they call me up to the window for my lab work, the lady was talking to i guess one of the nurses, who had gloves on. which i thought was a little worrisome because you shouldn't have gloves on unless you're with a patient..what's more was that she was touching her hair, the papers on the desk, everything. 
i got that same lady when i got called back for my bloodwork...she was wearing gloves. i waited to see if she would atleast change them before we started, she didn't. so i kindly asked her, since i didn't see her change her gloves, if she would. she looked at me like i just insulted her. she left the room, and proceeded to talk baldy about me to the other employee right outside the door. classy. 
when she came back in, she put on new gloves and then said "i had just changed them before i brought you in but i'll change them again" 
so you touched a door handle that everyone uses to get in and out of the waiting room, and who knows what else before you sat me down with those same gloves to draw blood from me? what?

complete lack of basic infection control which is 101, in any healthcare profession. 

i'm sorry, but with the flu and the corona virus going around i'm not taking any chances just because you're lazy. 
not happening.
i have to go here for my physical bloodwork but i will not be returning and i don't think it should even be up and running.

highly recommended- checked in online, was seen very quickly & was impressed by the quality of care and efficiency. being as unwell as i was, i appreciated the experience. i was coughing so they gave me a face mask and followed up with me a few days later to see how i was doing. 
it's a shame they can't be primary care!

the staff, today, was rude. dr. kapoor is amazing. she cared for my husband and family growing up, and then our son. i called concerned about a fever today. i'm sure they're overwhelmed,  though maybe contact them after the pandemic, and i'm sure you'll get great care then.

i was referred by a friend couple months ago for my blackhead and other skins problems.  after seeing rebecca couple times, my skin becomes cleaner and brighter.  the place is clean and the rebecca is very friendly.  she always make my visits pleasant and relaxing.  rebecca takes her time to cater my skincare routines, explains every steps about the the products she used on my face and how it would help to calm my skin. unlike other facial treatments i had experienced before, rebecca also spends times on massaging my face before putting mask on, to help absorbing products she puts on my face! i really enjoy my each visit and  will continue to visit her!

i've never reviewed a hospital before, but this is honestly the best one i've ever been to. 
the entire staff is so nice from the security to the doctors. i had to bring my son here for a cold and since he's little, they were able to get us in immediately to check him out. i didn't switch my insurance over from texas to missouri at the time and even coming uninsured it was no problem. they checked him out and gave him pedialyte and some extras to take home. they allow you to bring kids & babies back in to get their nose suctioned for (i think) 7 days after 24/7 at the hospital or you can go to an urgent care if it's closer to you with an appointment.  there's also a lot of hand sanitizer stations and masks available to make you feel more comfortable in this season. 
i recommend coming to this hospital over any other one in the area if you're able to.

doctors are suppose to treat you even when you are sick but no even the corona virus has them refusing mildly ill patients.  i just watched them turn away multiple patients because of flu or cold symptoms.  this is absurd i am going to blast and smear this practice everywhere they failed to follow their oath.  not to mention that snotty girl at the front desk needs knocked down off her high horse.  do not work in a doctors office unless you use manners and empathy. that is something she truly lacks and gulf coast is about to lose a lot of patients.

after years of having health  issues and seeing many doctors that just wanted to give me pills to mask my symptoms i started  searching on my own to find answers. this is how i came across dr gersh. it was actually easier to get an appointment then i thought.  she has an amazing practice to look at the whole body and find solutions to fix it instead of just fill you up with prescription drugs.  she took her time to educate me about my options and listened to my concerns.  i finally have hope that i can soon feel better. they have all the tools i need  to get my health and my life back.  she has a fantastic and friendly staff that includes the front desk.   i  recommend integrative medical group for anyone that feels that the current health system has failed them and wants to see positive results . 
( written by kitti goodman, dave's wife)

in the midst of the covid-19 pandemic, they require you to sign in on a touchpad teeming with germs. crowded waiting room. long wait time. rats. i may have to go back to beaumont! this review applies specifically to the lab.

i schedule an appointment for dr maska 2 months  ago . they ask me which kind of insurance i have and they scheduled. i have severe pain but waited until now.  just the day of the appointment i received a mail that dr. can not accept me because they don't accept blue shield ppo , and they cancelled it.    if they said me from the beginning i could call another dr , and not wait 2 months with this pain..

a little background, my parents are visiting me from northern china. they have been here way before the coronavirus situation. they planned to leave next week, but the flight was canceled. both of them are retired, so there is no need to rush back, especially given both of them have existing health problems. however, my father's medication is going to run out. so, i am searching for a doctor within his travel medical insurance's network, who is still accepting new patients.
i called the doctor's office on 3:24pm of feb 6th, 2020 with hope to get an appointment with the doctor to see my farther and prescribe the meds he is currently on. after the receptionist picked up the phone, i explained to her about my father's situation. however, the first few questions she asked was "when did your father come to us?" "where did you farther come from?". i had to tell her repeatly "he is not sick, just need to see a doctor to continue his current medication for his heart." at the end, the receptionist told me "we don't take patient from china". 
i am still shocked and angered by how i was treated by a medical professional/health care provider. first, a health care provider should not be so scared of a virus. not to mention it is a virus outbreak happening in another continent! how are you going to treat your patient with all different situations? second, a health care provider should not ask all of those questions even when it is not remotely relevant, a health care provide cannot reject a patient for his/her race.
of course, i am not saying the doctor is unprofessional and racist since i never got a chance to see him/her. but, as a health provider, this is extremely unprofessional and racist. so, i urge all of you who is considering seeing this doctor, think twice before you call. even you are a patient, think twice about how they really think about you. 

如果可以的话，我会给0星。先讲一下事情的背景，我爸爸妈妈从山东省来美国看我。两人过来是一月初，当时还没有coronavirus。他们本来计划下周回国，但是他们的航班取消了。因为他们两人都退休了，家里没有什么特别的事情需要他们回国，再加上我爸爸妈妈两人都不是特别健康，所以我就打算让他们在这里和我待到情况稳定之后再回去。我爸爸心脏不好，在国内时也是一直吃处方药的，他的药很快就要吃完了，所以我就在他们的旅行保险下面查找医生，希望可以找到一个接收新病人的医生，看看他现在吃的药和国内的处方，在这里可以开相同的处方药直到他们回国。
2020年2月6号下午3:24的时候，我打给了这个医生的办公室。我给前台介绍了详细的背景情况，可以前台前两个问题就是"你爸爸什么时候来美国的？""你爸爸是从哪里来的？"后来我一听不对劲，很坚定的重复了三次"我爸爸没有生病，只是需要看个医生，希望可以在这里拿到处方继续吃他治疗心脏病的药。"前台听后，告诉我"我们不接受中国病人。"一直到现在，我还仍然觉得很生气。生气的原因有两个，第一，作为医务人员，怎么可以会被吓成这个样子，怎么帮病人看病呢？第二，作为医生，怎么可以随便问和病情不想关的问题，怎么可以因为种族而拒绝病人？更何况，他们很有可能拒绝了和自己同样种族的病人。
当然，我并不是说这位医生不够专业或者有种族歧视，毕竟我没有机会见到他/她。但是前台代表了整个办公室，所以这个办公室作为一个整体，我认为特别不专业也特别歧视。如果你在考虑预约这个办公室，请三思。如果你现在是这个医生办公室的病人，也请考虑一下你是怎样被对待的。

bottom line.  i would not recommend marque urgent care for any type of medical need.  in my honest opinion, they are not qualified and charge way too much for the service that they do offer.  i can honestly only give them a one star out of necessity to post the review.

you know, no ones really ever thrilled about being in an er. there are classically long waits, sick people coughing all over you, and no one ever brings you that martini you ordered. i can't say that for most people a trip to the er will be a pleasurable experience, but i think if you take into account what to expect from such a visit and adjust your parameters, you can still end up with a 4-5 star experience. 

as coronavirus is running rampant in wa right now, i really wasn't inclined to visit a doctor when my clumsy self fell running and my finger turned 50 shades of purple..yah not at all sultry or enticing as an ombre of grey. i taped and generally avoided until i couldn't any longer and checked myself into the er with an xray of my translocated finger break..so apparently a purple finger is not a sign its healing normally just fyi.

the ladies at the front were positively peachy and got me checked in and even gave me the mask i requested to avoid the dreaded beer virus (cv). i really loved the new construction of the building with modern aesthetics, the checkin desk being separate from the waiting space and the door that begins your journey into the next waiting space.

i actually didn't hang out in the waiting room too long and an rn nabbed me to triage. he checked out my radiograph i came prepared with and laughed at my attempt to convince myself i was totally fine. they moved me after vitals to a nice patient room with a tv playing relaxing music and showing gorgeous scenery photography, i actually quite enjoyed that touch. the room was modern, clean, and had rather nice cabinetry. 

radiology popped in after hardly any wait to snap a few more photos of my mangled paw and then came the long wait for the physician. i  waited about 40 mins or so for her to pop in, say yah..that's a pretty complicated break.. then another 25 mins or so as she stepped out to see if there was anything she could do for me.

with that being said, "city of roses" and kimball did to me what i judged for my entire life to be impossible, he helped me to effectively get rid of the anxiety attacks that were consuming my life for 20 years or more.

the session was relaxing, but, honestly, i didn't think it would do anything. after we finished, as mentioned by others, kimball gave me the mp3s of the session to listen to them at home. 
after a week listening to the tapes (well, i wasn't actually listening, but rather sleeping with the tracks in the background) i was absolutely shocked. it was like i had carried a one-hundred-pounds-backpack my whole life and the therapy helped me to get rid of it. 

still skeptical, i waited three and a half months before i was convinced i should write this review. 
after our session, i read that hypnotherapy works through the connection your hypnotist makes with your subconscious. there's no magic, we are simply unaware of it unless we talk about it just like we are unaware of our noses and eyes. i believe it now! 
whatever kimball did that day has changed me from the inside. 
i sleep better, have more self-control, can now focus more at work, and have had no anxiety whatsoever ever since i had the session (heck, i am writing this during the coronavirus outbreak, so nothing will test the hypnosis efficacy more than this). 

please, do yourself a favor and go see kimball. he will change your life. 

p.s: he is also an amazing piano player.

i am extremely happy that i had the surgery, and i am glad i chose the la jolla nvision team and dr. parikh. i would also like to give a special shout out to john, the director of the clinic, for helping make the arrangements for my surgery.

so i made a reservation online for 8pm, but when i arrived i was told they didn't have one. i was told i would have gotten a confirmation email. well last time i came for a different reservation and the same thing happened, i got a confirmation email 2 days later. however, i am here now and they are open to walk ins, but i was clearly yet rudely told the wait is about an hour but it's shift change now. ok so i know healthcare doesn't just stop at shift change, but i get it slows things down a bit. look if i had gotten sick during business hours i wouldn't be here. this is my second time here and the second time i have had a bad experience. so moving forward my paperwork wasn't even completed for 2 hours, it is like they hold your id hostage so you don't leave. i got up and asked for it to be told they were almost done. so i am still sitting here. freezing, shivering, aching, sweating, wearing my mask in the almost empty waiting room aside from one other person. not sure what the wait is. i have seen one person go in and 2 people go out in 2 hours. so efficiency and courtesy are not top priorities here despite the healing ministry mission. it is like antarctica in here, the woman at the desk has spent a good bit of time on personal calls, i hear some inappropriate gossip coming from the back. trying to be patient but i feel terrible and i can tell the urgency of this urgent care is lacking.
