review:
i would give it a zero if i could. i am family nurse practitioner and work in the medical field. i decided to bring my son here because he had foot pain. i usually go to west med medical but decided to give this a try. i walked into a flooded waiting area with no available seats- which i think it's a disgrace since everyone waiting has some kind of orthopedic complaint. i waited patiently for over an hour to be told by front desk that my "insurance was canceled" although i gave my insurance information the day before for eligibility.  probably for the best...i called west med and they are accommodating me today. 

as a hispanic provider, i get infuriated when i see medical providers/businesses over booking just for their profit margins and worst the demographics they serve are predominantly hispanics and blacks. shame on you!! patients with orthopedic issues should not be standing in your waiting area!! patients should not be waiting over an hour in the waiting room and then another hour in the treatment room!! patients should only be confirmed for appts once they are screened and found eligible. and lastly...it's flu season ...put some hand sanitizer/kleenex for public use since your waiting area is inoculating whatever current strain of virus we currently have.

i don't know what happened over the years but my last 2 facials at bw orange was the worst.  this review is for both of those experiences b/c coincidently, i had the same lady.

 both visits, everything felt rushed-- what happened to relaxation and slow fluid movements?  

i don't think my girl knew how to properly give a facial. it literally felt like she was just putting stuff on my face, rubbing here and there and then abrasively rubbing off with a wash towel.  she didn't do any massage techniques on my face nor did she move in an upward circular motion.  she kept pulling my face downward which is a huge no no in my book. 

bw used to use a soft sponge or cloth to wash cleansers & masks off but on this visit and my last visit months ago this girl used a wet towel to rub off everything.  it felt so rough and abrasive on my skin-- i straight up hated it.  every skincare enthusiast knows you're not suppose to tug your skin or rub your face with a towel. 

i don't know if this is common sense but why would you give me an aggressive scalp massage and then use those same fingers that touched my greasy oily hair, proceed to massage my face immediately after?  i felt so disgusted and gross the entire time- i just wanted to go home and shower to wash all the filth off. 

this is not the bw that i know and have been coming to for years.   it's very disappointing. the quality has gone down and i think it's time for me to find a real esthetician who knows how to properly massage my face.

don't count on any help here for the coronavirus! you cannot get a person on the phone,  period,  and there are no options on the automated line to allow you to try to find out what to do if you are showing symptoms.  this is how the virus has become a pandemic!!!

this is not good practice. i smoke and received steroids for my lungs and a inhaler. did bloodwork but no x-ray ordered for a 30 yr. smoker when i called to get a order the next day, they said she would call me but surprise did not. then when i called and asked on monday the nurse said i had to make a appointment and pay my deductible again. i have read other post where people die from her not ordering them. if you need a real doctor stick to a good ol usa dr. that will help you live even if you dont want to pay two co pays for the right treatment the first time. now i now why their office is always empty.

we just switched 18 of our monthly prescriptions from another cvs to this store which is closer to our home. what a disaster. with the exception of one pharmacist; dr. patel and one pharmacy assistant named jay this is a very poorly run pharmacy. i learned today that the pharmacy manager is on medical leave and has been for some time. the store manager told me that it is unclear when the pharmacy manager will return. in the meantime we often arrive at the counter to find that they don't know where our prescriptions are. our prescriptions are filled incorrectly. we are told incorrect information as to when our prescriptions can be refilled. we are not offered assistance should we have questions about our prescriptions. and the latest insult was today. we asked for alcohol wipes which diabetes use daily. the pharmacist could not find any in the store. the store manager said that they were out due to the current coronavirus outbreak. for pete sake these wipe are the size of my thumb nail. the store manager had no idea what an alcohol wipe which a diabetes must use every time he or she sticks him or herself even was and that the pharmacy was out of them was ridiculous. i am a cancer patient and my husband has both parkinson's disease and diabetes along with several other serious medical problems. the pharmacist is an important member of our health care team. going to this cvs has become borderline dangerous to our health. the store manager is unresponsive. he is kicking the problem upstairs.....gave me the email address of the regional manager. i feel he should own the problem until it is fixed. he won't.....don't use this pharmacy. and by the way there were 8 people in line behind us today while they searched for our missing prescriptions....they never found the prescription and had to fill it again....sad. and finally the people who check you out at the counter look like they would rather be any place but working at that cvs.

i am quite disappointed that in light of the coronavirus outbreak and extra measures- the hospital has ignorantly placed a sign at the entrance asking people if they have any symptoms or have been to wuhan, china. the virus is global and we have a reported 1200 cases in the us with thousands around the world. i could easily come from italy or germany and have contracted the virus. let's not feed the xenophobia anymore. this is no longer a "chinese" concern but a world concern. they also ask that if you have a cough to wear a mask. but right after i walked through i stood in line with a visitor at starbucks that was coughing! get smarter people- this is not the first global health crisis and definitely not the last!

this was my first time getting a facial and massage envy was the perfect place to do it at! i scheduled a 60 minute appointment with raina and after we finished our session, i knew it would not be my last facial!

when checking in, i took a quick survey on a tablet, indicating what type of skin i have, any regimen i follow, and any concerns i have regarding my skin. i arrived a bit early, so i was shown to the tranquility room, where there are complementary tea and foot massagers to accompany my wait. raina came to take me to our room right on time and she walked me through exactly what our appointment was going to entail.
it was so relaxing and she made sure to let me know what we were doing at each step and answered all my questions. raina is super knowledgeable, as she used to specialize in dermatology, and gave me some helpful recommendations specific to my skin. 

from start to finish, the experience was so relaxing. it ended with a face mask complimented by hand and arm massages. i left the room glowing! my face has never looked so dewy nor has it felt this soft.

when i left, raina gave me two samples of serum that she had used on my skin during the facial! it was such a pleasant first experience, i will definitely be back!

i would like to detail my experience using vons.com to order groceries for delivery. i've been using a service for almost two and a half years now, and the service has certainly changed from what it was a year ago at least in los angeles where i live. when i go to your website i'm told that my default store is in san diego, i live in los angeles so i have to change which store i'm using most during most of the time. i've had many issues with ordering products.
 
1 example: i used to order hansen's root beer and it was $4.09 for a six-pack, always the same price.  then something changed on your website and i was charged $4.09 for one can of soda... and i had to speak with three different people over the course of an hour to get a refund for that! your employees were refusing to help at the beginning. i had to speak to a manager. lost an hour of my life dealing with that vons generated issue. 
 
your website does not register the "#" symbols when entering delivery instructions. my door code has the # symbol in it, but your delivery people would never see that because your website doesn't register the symbol.

 i ordered delivery, you should deliver it to my door. i don't have the ability to carry five cases of soda up to the fourth floor, that's why i order delivery, i've been told by your customer service that doordash is only used if i select the one hour delivery window, which is not true, i've had a delivery between scheduled between noon and 2 p.m. and i got a phone call at 2:30pm saying that my order would be delivered by doordash in an hour and a half. so my order was two hours late for a 2 hour delivery window.  i call the customer service line and are met with people who say they can't/will not help. they act as though all this problems are my fault. and after the delivery you go through your groceries and find a bunch of stuff that you didn't order, even though you select "no substitutions" on the website, the people at the store do whatever they want. 
 
i wish it was easier to order something online, and then get that product and not have to spend 48 minutes on the phone dealing with issues. or being forced to schedule a "return item pick up" and have to take a full day off work just to get a refund, absolute terrible experience my last 5 orders.

please do not bring your loved ones to this rehab facility. we had a terrible experience here. my dad was recovering from pneumonia and needed to get stronger yet he got worse and had to be rehospitalized. the nurses were very inattentive and pt rarely got him out of bed even to sit in a chair. the nurses seemed overworked and complained about their paperwork and other parts of their job. they hardly seemed interested in his well being, he didn't eat, was left in bed all day and got a urinary infection and staph infection in his blood because the nurse left an iv needle in him which was discovered after we rushed him to the er. as though it wasn't bad enough, most of the nurses called in sick and there was even less attention during the holiday week, as though it wasn't bad enough already to not be with his family for the holidays, receiving terrible absentee care on top of that. the doctor was terrible and instead of finding out what the pain was or ordering tests, he just gave him oxycontin.

i would give zero stars. please choose another facility for your loved ones.

i was referred to katherine by my attorney after being rear ended and then pushed into another car. she didn't order an mri right away which has made a delay in treatment . i had to ask for it and for xrays. it took a week from seeing her to even get the order for xrays. i go into her office 3 weeks after my initial appointment and she hadn't called to get the xrays, so i still have no clue what they said or if she even requested them yet. she was more concerned with getting my previous medical records than seeing if i've been injured worse through the accident by ordering an mri. she was very unprepared

worst doctor i've ever been to. insulted me and rambled on about nothing pertaining to me or my health. you rarely ever get to see him as he always has medical students conducting the visits for him. when i did get to see him, it was hard to understand what he was saying and was making some stupid joke about the corona virus.

so far, so good.  new to the area and needed a pain specialist to do my yearly (or so) back pain shots.  went to see dr. alvarez.  got in quickly and he spent a thorough time talking with me and ordering all new tests which impressed me.  now waiting for insurance to ok everything and will be getting my shots soon.  the office staff is friendly and i've liked everything so far and i'm really picky about my doctors.

i've been to this urgent care a handful of times over the years and have been disappointed each time. i live very close so i keep hoping that the next visit will be better, but i visited for the final time today. the first time i went here, i was laughed at for needing a chest x-ray following a virus and was told that i needed to give it more time. after begging for the picture, i was given the x-ray and sent on my way as i was "fine". got a call 2 days later that my radiologist report showed pneumonia. i revisited this place tonight (a couple of years after my first experience) 2 hours before the closing time and was met with an open sign that was turned off. i was the only patient, probably because the sign was off and no one else bothered to try the door. i felt the entire time as if i was inconveniencing them and am pretty sure that the strep swab that was taken from me wasn't even run as the doctor returned with my 'negative result' about 3 minutes after they swabbed my throat. i came with good reason (my daughter has tested positive for strep this week and i have a history of strep throat cases), but because my family is also currently getting over the flu, i was told that i was just fine and needed to wait another week with my fever and pain before following-up with my physician. he also would not be sending my swab out for a culture because he was confident in his diagnosis. normally, i greatly respect any diagnosis, but they were treating me like i had walked in complaining of a sneeze, and i left so embarrassed by the whole situation. probably not the best urgent care to choose; at least not on a saturday night when they don't want to be bothered.

i literally drove from san jose all the way to los banos trying to see my niece. my dad and sister were already there. when i get there, they didn't let me see my niece because of the coronavirus. i mean i understand and all but they let my family in and moreover they made that announcement five minutes ago when i came in(my dad called me about it). they really can't make an exception. all that driving for nothing and i can't even see my niece for like one minute.

look, i don't normally leave bad reviews. i assume someone just had a bad day. but at this location, it's been too much of a negative experience. if i could give zero stars, i would. zero compassion and total lack of concern from 4 separate doctors at this facility. never seen anything like this. my doctors in austin were kind, listened to my concerns and at least were open to new ideas in medicine. but the tools weren't available yet. there are new tools now, so i thought i would try again to get to the bottom of what's going on with me.

i waited over 3 months to see a urologist (at my pcp's insistence) for a chronic, a-typical urinary tract infection symptoms. he dismissed me within 1.5 minutes of speaking with me. after describing a few of my symptoms, he said i needed to keep things in perspective because many of his patients had cancer and/or didn't have long to live. i get that, but i'm your patient too. just because i'm not dying (yet), it doesn't mean i'm not worth helping. 

i'm a pretty gentle person, so for me to stand up to a doctor and not take no for an answer, it takes a lot. over a decade of doctors telling me my symptoms don't add up, i'm not taking no for an answer anymore. i'm determined to figure it out.

he referred me to an infectious disease specialist who suggested i just manage the uti symptoms with diet. i'd been so excited to finally maybe see someone that could help me. rather than explore my situation, i was again very quickly dismissed. she's very knowledgeable about nutrition, though. more than most doctors i've seen. but my other doctor in a different network is very concerned about trying to manage chronic kidney infection with diet alone and feels i should be treated to try to clear the infection. because what i possibly have can cause permanent kidney damage, just managing it with diet could be risky. and it's getting harder to manage, getting worse and worse each year.

went back to the urologist and he said he just focuses on surgeries and wouldn't revisit this with me. most other doctors i'm calling to see just keep ordering me to go back to the urologist. ha! i'm finding out urologists just do prostate/bladder cancer or vasectomies! who the hell do you go to for rare uti issues?!!

the endocrinologist there berated me immediately for  medications i took. not my fault i was prescribed this stuff, sorry lady. said i was being scammed and the doctor that prescribed it was just taking my money. uh, the money went to the pharmacy??? she demanded i get off all mediications immediately... even before i asked her to check my numbers first to be sure that was the right course of action, she still demanded i get off them. i tried to explain that without the progesterone, i would once again be on my period every day. she just said to get on the birth control pill again and stop the natural progesterone. there is no birth control pill with the levels of hormones i need, and because birth control pills are synthetic (made from horse urine), i don't do well on birth control pills. my obgyn was very concerned about the immediate orders i was given by this endo and advised me to disregard her orders.

i was later sent to the rheumatologist who was slightly more approachable, but he didn't seem at all interested in trying to help me figure out what's going on with my system. i was told lupus and other autoimmune disorders can cause kidney issues. so i was trying to get an answer for that. no real concern was expressed or offer for help. 

i don't know if they're just stressed and overworked, but just asking to have some tests run, they treat you like a street junky trying to get opioids. not a good place to be when you are already at the end of your rope dealing with frustrating, exhausting medical issues. i needed hope and i needed help. instead, i got confirmation that western medicine is broken, dysfunctional and doctors don't give a flip what happens to you. 

these doctors here at the main campus always seem like they're trying to keep a lid on their anger. not sure what's happening behind the scenes. but it's bad for patients. 

also, i've heard of the referral kickback game. didn't really think it was a "thing." but beware, doctors at this location may just keep referring patients to other doctors taking a kickback for referrals. doctor after doctor here wants to spend 1 minute with you and simply refer you to another doctor. i have been in a referral loop for a long time getting referred from one doctor to another. no doctor willing to sit with me to figure out what's happening with my kidneys or my immune system. seems to be no big deal to them. i wish i'd known all this before i accepted my pcp's referral. she was at the kelsey-seybold cinco ranch location and was also abrupt, rude and condescending. i now have a sick feeling in the pit of my stomach about going to a doctor in the future.

this is so average. they lost my paperwork and i waited for weeks more to start getting help and orders sent out. they are a bit unconscious as so many doctors offices are. i submitted to tests which i feel are currently barbaric and in time will be utterly eliminated. the doctor was a bit ham handed and weighty in his administration of said tests. it's funny how they always think tests arent that painful when they aren't the ones undergoing them!

based on my observations, his recommendations and the general vibe, i don't feel i'm going to be healed here. he didn't even bother ordering a new mri to see how i fare this year, and my insurance certainly would allow that. he is contacted to a lot of weird quacks doctors in pasadena under the same name of west coast neurology. i have experienced the others on the raymond ave building and they really suck.

what a nightmare. the only reason i'm putting two stars is because the ladies at the front and the two nurses were very nice. i went in for my first visit 3 weeks ago they told me i had an upper respiratory infection and that it was a "virus" and it will go away on its own i was skeptical because i wasn't coughing and i had no congestion in my nose just a sore throat i the asked the doctor we could still treat it with antibiotics just in case she said no. fast forward to today i've been sick for 3 weeks now woke up with my throat swollen shut so i went back to have it examined i was nicely explaining the situation to the pa ashley she turned to me and i kid you not said "well okay i don't need a speech" i mean isn't it your job as a medical practitioner to listen to your patient whether you like it or not and maybe show just a little bit of compassion or understanding ?!?! i'm in so much pain and to have someone basically say they don't care what i have to say was extremely insulting. this all could've been avoided if i would've just been prescribed antibiotics the first visit. again i was brushed off and told it was a virus and now they're saying it's a bacterial infection so basically no one has any clue what's going on. it seems their doctors need to go back to school. at this point i was so sick i just took the antibiotic prescription and got the heck out of there. the only reason i came here in the first place is because my primary care physician is out of the office for a month. what a joke.

i have never posted on yelp before and this my first review. this hospital is amazing!! went to loma linda  urgent care for my 6 month old son  having trouble breathing. after examination, started turning a little blue and doctor called an ambulance to take him to loma linda pediatric er. (note: if your child is sick, call 911 and get an ambulance. ambulance er visits get them to the front of the line immediately.) after in pediatric er having breathing treatments, he was diagnostic with rst, bronculitis, and one other virus i can't remember. the pediatric er is small, crowded , loud and will make you very irritated. hang in there. the staff know what they are doing and make quick decisions. once my son was diagnosed, they wanted to admit him to pediatric icu for his condition. i thought it was ridiculous that he would need that level of care because he was alert and giggling with his toys. i was wrong. after admission, he was on oxygen. then he got dehydrated from not eating and had to go on baby cpap machine. almost went to tube breathing on a ventilator but he improved slightly. he got a lot worse before he started to improve. the staff at the pediatric icu were amazing. very attentitive, very informative, and constantly checked in on him. children have died from these viruses and i believe that loma linda pediatric icu saved his life. please go to pediatric er and get admitted if your child is sick. remember to take an ambulance ride. worth the money to be at the front of the line.

i've never had a bad experience with a physician before i was seen by dr stephen newandee. he had poor bedside manner and was quick to make judgements about me. 

i went in for a gynecology referral and recurrent oral mucositis. i get frequent cankersores since i was a child. they worsened over last two years and one was even located on my tonsil (the md who saw me at the time said it was the worst cankersore she had seen).

i got four new cankersores and decided to see dr newandee. i don't generally see a md unless my symptoms were severe, and with 4 new cankersores, i was unable to eat, talk, or drink. i went in trying to find out an underlying reason for these recurrent cankersores and for symptom management. i tried to explain to him my history with cankersores and that they have been something chronic i've dealt with for many, many years--but he basically shut me up. he quickly brushed my symptoms off as nothing and told me 1) i have herpes 2) need sleep and water. that's. it. 

i was unwilling to accept those as the sole reasons. i, in turn, asked if it could be related to vitamin deficiency and wanted to know if a chemistry panel would provide insight. he ordered the chemistry lab but started ordering 999999 other unrelated labs (such as lipid panel that tests for cholesterol levels). when i asked if the additional labs were necessary (because i'm on a budget and don't know how much the extraneous labs would cost), he said "you want labs to find out why right?! do you want them or not?" when he asks that, how is a patient supposed to feel? i was shocked by his outburst. it was abrupt and very uncalled for. 

mind you, i wasnt trying to doubt his medical expertise and was only asking for clarification. it was the first question i asked during the whole visit, but he became aggressive for absolutely no reason. cholesterol level is clearly unrelated to vitamin/electrolyte levels, and that was the only reason why i asked for clarification. if he simply wanted a complete bloodwork on me to see i'm healthy, then fine. but he could have at least explained himself rather than get grumpy with me.

he repeatedly told me the more i do to my cankersores, the worst they'll get. yes, i already know they just need time to heal. they're similar to cold sores wherein they need to heal on their own, but at least there are products to help speed up recovery. when i asked for ointment, he told me "theres nothing" and "do whatever you want youll just make it worse." first of all, i'm not your 12 year old child. secondly, i still tried to be respectful towards him despite his rudeness, but he did not speak to me with respect. that honestly was the last straw. i'm not asking him to care or be passionate--those were thrown out the window 2 min into our visit--but the least i ask for is respect. 

i remained professional and asked him if i could leave at the end of the visit (he didn't say bye or at all indicate if he was done with me or not). he then said very curtly, "you have your referral and lab. what else do you want??"

these are just few instances when he was curt and rude to me. don't even get me started on how he repeatedly cut me off and how he approached the physical exam. he may be a good doctor based on other people's reviews, but i feel he had a serious prejudice against me because i was coming in for a "nothing" symptom. he should've at least tried to hear me out and explain the treatment better--rather than saying "sleep and fluids! sleep and fluids!" i'm not a doctor so need his expertise to better understand my condition. he didn't care to give me any of that and just wanted me out of his office as soon as possible.

i left the visit feeling terribly hurt by his condescending and dismissive words. no one should be speaking to me like that unless it's my parents. needless to say, i switched my pcp right after the visit. i deserve a better doctor and won't be coming back.

my wife had a very debilitating illness which came on somewhat suddenly just before christmas.  she is usually in very good health, but whatever she had knocked her flat.  she had visited dr. fang for a physical in the past, but never had the need to see her for anything else.    we got in to see her very quickly for an examination.
her bedside manner is exceptional.  she is patient, inquisitive and, most importantly, very thorough as she questions you.  we never felt rushed or ignored and she allowed my wife to explain her symptoms completely.  her initial diagnosis had a few scary possibilities, so she began ordering tests.  she was apologetic when explaining that she was going on vacation until after the new year and that the ucla system (like every other business during the holidays) would be running at reduced capacity.
understandably, at this point, we were even more concerned.  when facing systemic delays during a health scare, you're left with your mind racing to various awful outcomes and to be denied expediency at such a time is devastating.  and, of course, dr. internet is telling you bye-bye; you're toast.
dr, fang sensed our trepidation and with the help of pedro and christina in her office, scheduled all the tests, imaging and specialist visit in such short order that we were completely reassured.  in addition, she personally called us 3 times to discuss each set of test results and to continue her path to diagnosis while she was on vacation.
i can't stress just how reassuring knowing that your doctor was following up personally as opposed to justifiably handing your case off to a covering physician and letting us simmer until business resumed two weeks later.
i was somewhat reticent to post this review fearing that others would seek her out and increase her popularity to where we couldn't get in as soon as we wanted.  but when your health is on the line, you truly want someone like dr. fang and a system like ucla to have your back.

if your pet needs timely life saving medications to continue living, do not use this joke of an outfit!
my wife and i adopted a cat. ther cat was the single most loving and snuggly cat in the history of cats. last year, the cat developed a number of health problems that required medication.  he needed 3 compounded medications. our vet recommended these folks. at first everything was fine. the vet would call me to authorize the charge on my bank card for each medication. and it was delivered on time. 
then the problems started. it turns out, they created a separate account for each medication.  there was confusion ordering refills. my wife would call for a complete refill and only one would be delivered. i called in november to resolve the issue and was told by the person on the phone that the multiple accounts had been combined into one. 
nearly 2 months later, we received a bill for unpaid medications.  my wife called and left repeated messages but never received a call back. with an important medication nearly out of doses, she went to their website and found that there were still multiple accounts open for our one pet. she herself combined them online, paid off the outstanding balance on the bill that was sent to us, ordered more medication and because the meds were very low, she spent extra money to have the meds expedited with 2 day shipping. 
the day the medication was supposed to arrive, i received a phone call from someone at the pharmacy who insisted that we owed them money for an unpaid bill from last june. i explained to them that my wife had just paid off all of the outstanding bill that we had received. the caller said that they were able to see the payment for the refill that my wife had just made but that was all. i then said i would look over the bills with my wife when we got home from work and it they could please double check with their accounting person to confirm that there was an outstanding bill and not a mistake and to call me the next day. at home, my wife and i went over the last bill received, and sure enough there was nothing outstanding from june. 
the next day, a full day after the meds were supposed to arrive  the pharmacy called me back insisting that money was still owed. i explained that i looked at the invoice and there was nothing on the bill from june and it must be a mistake. i asked if there was a record of the last payments my wife made and they said that they could see the those and the payment from the refill. but nothing from june. i then asked why there was nothing on the last bill from june and i was told that there must have been a "misunderstanding" and i replied that it was not and that it was a mistake on their part. i then asked to have them email every single bill they had over the last year so i could go over it with my wife and they said they would, but before the call ended, they said that they were not going to sell to us until the bill was fully paid. 
when my wife and i got home, after the pharmacy had closed, not only was there no email of the bills sent to either of us, but the expedited  medications still had not arrived. 
the next morning, my wife spent nearly an hour on hold before she managed to reach someone who confirmed that even though they could not find a record or any proof of a missed payment, because accounting said so, they were not only refusing to sell to us in the future, they also were withholding the expedited medications we had already paid for at the beginning of the week. this being friday, with the pharmacy closed for the weekend, even if we paid off their mistake, the expedited meds would not arrive until the middle of next week. 
luckily for us, we have an amazing vet who managed to find us medication to last until the new pharmacy can compound it and ship it to us. 
my wife sent a scathing email to them with screenshots of the bill and her bank records showing that not only have we have been excellent customers, we would never use them again and almost magically, an hour later we both received phone calls saying that everything was cleared up and medications would be sent out right away. 
this is not a magazine or or newspaper subscription. this is medication. the pharmacy is willing to endanger the life of a beloved pet over a mistake that they made and only changed their tack when my wife told them to reverse the payment for the expedited meds because we would never do business with them again. 
i can't imagine going into business to help care for animals while being so amoral, greedy and cruel that they would be willing to hold a pets life ransom until we paid a bill that they could not show us or in any way prove it existed. the fact that they quickly reversed course is sad proof of their greed. 
if you value the life of your pet, never use these people.

i was moved by the review written by richard f. he said that he wanted to set the record straight regarding the negative reviews which have been written about this doctor. one reviewer complained this doctor made him wait beyond his appointment time. richard f said that was because the doctor was operating on him at that time,  and there were unforseen complications. therefore dr spoonamore had to spend more time on his surgery to make sure it was done right. i respect that integrity and would rather wait then have a doctor rush through surgery on another patient,  just to talk to me. though, in fairness, i do think the doctors staff could have told the waiting patient that the doctor was still in surgery, and have rescheduled that patient's appointment. in any event, richard f's review motivated me to set an appointment with dr spoonamore. my experience with dr spoonamore motivated me to write my own review.

i consulted with dr spoonamore in december 2019. i have ongoing siatica pain in my left leg which comes from spinal problems. i have protruding discs in the lumbar spine.  that can cause a great deal of pain. i have been treating this condition with epidural injections which do mask the pain temporarily. but i have to have an injection every 3 to 4 months to stay out of pain. i was looking for a more permanent solution. i was hoping i would be a candidate for non invasive surgery.

dr spoonamore sat with me for about 45 minutes, possibly longer,  with the cd of my mri results in front of us on his computer screen. he gave me a nuanced consultation about the kind of surgery i would need to remove the bulging discs and he advised against surgery.  unfortunately, dr spoonamore does not think that i am not a candidate for non invasive procedures because the location of the discs are too close to the spine.  so, according to him, i would need to have a fusion. that would mean they would have to go through bone and muscle to remove the discs.  dr spoonamore explained that would be a long and painful recovery. and, that i may not even be out of pain when recovery was complete, because he would not be able to remove all of the protruding discs in one operation. he said i may need a second surgery to remove the remaining discs.  

dr spoonamore recommended that i continue with quarterly injections if that is helping to mask the pain.  and, that i start up with physical therapy.  to give me hope, he said that stem cell therapy may be a viable option in the future. 

i asked dr spooamore if he felt an anti-inflamatory diet would help alleivate some of the pain. he responded that he is a spine suregon and not a nutritionist. i was a little taken aback by that comment. i thought it was curt. first, he had just given me discouraging news. i was grasping at whatever i could do to help myself. second, he states on a video on his website that he uses a multi disciplinary approach. therefore, i would have thought that he would have known more about alternative options such as an anti-inflamatory diet. in any event, i do not think he should have responded as he did to that question. 

overall, i was satisifed with the consultation. while i was disappointed with the diagnosis, i appreciated his honesty and integrity.  he could have given me a different recommendation in order to get my money. but he did not. he also took time to give me a through and nuanced explanation.
address: 1450 San Pablo St Ste 5400 USC Spine Ctr

2.  the security guard never looked up from his computer and mumbled for us to sit down - "they know you're here."  we were the only people in the er, so i'm thinking "who knows we're here?"
3.  three women were behind a desk and did not make eye contact with us - no concern for a young woman holding a crying baby.  they just talked to each other - nobody told us anything.
4.  five minutes becomes 10 minutes and nobody said anything to us.
5.  after about 10-12 minutes a door marked triage opens and some patient comes out.  the triage nurse asked us to come in.
6.  she did not wash her hands, use purell, or wear gloves.
7.  she had to do all the typing to get us into the system (i guess the other three women were busy not helping)
8.  after about 15 questions - she finally asked why we were here.  we told her he had been bitten by a dog.
9.  when she reached for his hand - he of course screamed - so she reached for an unsanitized teddy bear on her desk and gave that to him to quiet him down.
10.  she dabbed the wound clean (did not rinse it) and moved us through some double doors into another waiting room with about six chairs - again we were the only people there.
11.  about another 10-15 minutes later a nurse came in and confirmed the baby's name.  then she asked us if he had a fever?  no?  a cough?  no?  we told her he had a dog bite.  (i wonder why she hadn't read the triage report??)
12.  she asked my daughter a dozen questions which had nothing to do with the dog bite, including vaginal or c-section delivery?  i'm guessing that is a priority when treating a dog bite.
13.  another 10 - 15 minutes and a doctor came into the room.  and here's where i started to question this whole operation.  he never came closer than 10 feet from the baby - never looked at the wound, let alone cleaned it.  from 10 feet away he then described what he was going to do - he was going to order an x-ray and then give us some antibiotics - because he told us without antibiotics the risk of infection is very high.
14.  another 10-15 minutes and a guy from x-ray came and told us he had been instructed to an x-ray of the right hand.  "is this _____?"  good guess!

did you ever see the movie zootpia where she has to go to the dmv to get her license?  that's what this experience brought to my mind.  they were like the sloths but without the smile and the compassion.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=drhsktakrzc 

15.  another 30 minutes and the nurse came back asking us what was happening.  that is when i got a little frustrated and asked her why the doctor had not even looked at the wound?  why hadn't the wound been cleaned?  she seemed to think that the doctor had looked at the wound.
16.  i could go on and on...

finally the nurse came back with the prescription for the antibiotic - it was now 11 at night.  i asked her if she could call in the prescription so it would be ready when we got there.  "we don't provide that service."

this is a perfect example of an organization which is driven by procedure - and has absolutely no focus on patients.  no compassion, no coordination, no communication.  the system these people work in has crushed their humanity - and this is with an empty er.

all the while i'm thinking to myself - "omg imagine if there was a corona virus outbreak in sarasota and there were five or six puking sick people in the er waiting room?  this hospital is completely unprepared to handle anything like that."

come to find out two days later that there was a corona virus patient in the hospital that night - and i thought back to the people not washing their hands, etc. etc.  i pray that my grandson, my daughter and i were not infected.  

and hannah b. don't respond "i am so sorry to hear about your experience..."  if you gave a damn, you would go to the er yourself and see what your customers see - it isn't pretty.  if you did care, it would either be fixed, or you wouldn't be working there.

i went to this urgent care center for the first time today because i recently got a new insurance and my pcp's office was not able to verify it. my pcp was also booked for the day, so i wasn't too keen on waiting hours to be seen. 

i came in wearing a mask due to my symptoms of sore throat, hoarseness, and productive cough. immediately upon arrival, i was greeted by the friendly receptionist. i handed her the printout of my insurance cards and she was able to verify and register me quickly. 

within minutes of completing registration and paying my copay, i was taken into a room by the medical assistant, dennis, who read my description of my symptoms, took my vitals, and swabbed my nose and throat for strep and flu. 

then i sat in the room for 10-15 minutes, before i was seen by marina domatova, the pa. she was very friendly and informative. she asked me a few followup questions about my symptoms before examining my ears, throat, lymph nodes, and lungs. at the conclusion of my exam and discussion, she diagnosed me with strep throat and pharyngitis.

throughout the encounter, she took the time to listen to my concerns and explain things patiently. she made helpful recommendations such as 
-avoiding sharing drinks and food since strep throat is contagious for 7 days after the start of antibiotics
-avoid taking cough suppressants in general since they suppress the cough reflex and prevent your body from ridding the irritation in your throat.
-drinking warm fluids, breathing in humidified air, gargling with warm salt water to moisten and soothe the throat. 

i had a very pleasant visit and was surprised by how clean, neat, and new the facilities looked. the whole visit only took 45 minutes from start to finish! all the staff there were extremely professional and courteous, and i left with a comprehensive treatment plan. due to the ease of the appointment and the quality of care, i would definitely return to prohealth if i have another urgent medical concern and cannot be seen my primary care doctor.

i would not recommend coming here.  instead of presenting us with our options in terms of vaccines, pill prescriptions, mosquito repellant, water purifiers, etc, the nurse who was helping us merely overwhelmed us with a packet of information and told us what she was going to go prepare to give us.  
i am a registered nurse, so luckily i felt comfortable asking for further explanation and telling her no to some things.  my husband, however, if i was not there, would have gone through with everything unnecessarily just because he is not medically aware and it was so quickly pushed onto us.
the nurse told us that we are not to come in contact with fresh water and that we are not to eat any street food.  how is this practical?  we came across multiple waterfalls, bathed elephants in fresh water streams, and ate tons of street food.  take some azithro with you on your trip in case of emergency, but otherwise live a little!

the nurse was also very serious and adamant about keeping a paper book with proof of immunizations provided by passport health with us at all times, as each country we are going to will ask for immunization records.  we went to 5 countries, and none of them asked for this.

when the nurse came in with our vaccines, they had been drawn up in a different room.  how is this professional?  we were not able to see if she took the needle out of a new package, if she cleaned the vials, if the vials were new, etc. i also had to ask what she administered to my arm after she had already given me the vaccine.  let us know beforehand!

the ordering medical professional, whether it was an np or md, never was seen either.  i trust rns, as i am one, but this is yet another thing that did not seem professional.

by no means am i being your typical annoying medical professional nitpicking in another medical space, but this company needs to act more as a clinic, rather than a mere business.  the entire time we were there, we felt like we were in a jewelry store, being upsold and constantly having to say no to a sales pitch, while also being treated as customers rather than patients.

review:
update: i'm no stranger to surgeries and medical procedures, but so many of them have gone poorly for me, either by being painful or ineffective or mistakes being made. this was my first elective medical procedure and the only one that went smoothly and painlessly. the most painful part of this procedure was peeling the tape off my face to lift the eye shields up to put eye drops in. 

getting the valium was a big help to my anxiety and took away my restless/fidgety nature so i could lay still during the procedure. this team seemed liked a well oiled machine; they communicated concisely and calmly and it was incredibly comforting to know what was going on and how long it would take for each step. when i heard "18 seconds," i felt extremely relieved, not just because that step was extremely short, but also because i knew what to expect. the team had an awesome sense of humor and had me laughing for half the procedure. there was pressure, there was discomfort, but there wasn't any pain and i don't think the entire procedure took 5 minutes. i kept my eyes closed for a few hours after, but when i woke up and lifted the eye shields, i could see, perfectly, and that's amazing. 

my friend was able to sit in a waiting room and watch/record the procedure on a tv, which was so cool. i've watched the video like 5 times already and i just can't believe the coordination and care they're able to achieve.

i have 20/20 vision the day after the procedure, with no pain or dryness. to prepare for the surgery i took fish oil, lutein, and zeaxanthin, used preservative free eye drops generously as well as msm eyedrops daily and used a steam mask daily. i've been giving my eyes a full 30 seconds closed at the beginning of every hour to be sure i don't experience the dryness or discomfort that i've read some others do. i'm not sure if all the prepping i did contributed to how smoothly it went, but i know it went a long way toward making my eyes feel better regardless.

also, the state of massachusetts already has confirmed cases of coronavirus so i'm not sure what the difference is between refusing a customer from ny or a customer from ma- might as well refuse all customers at this point and not try to keep a business open. makes no sense!

this is a questionable, shady business. stay away! received damaged product and they refuse to take it back. the ingredients listed are more for dessert rather than supplements to boost your milk. i wished i spoke to my friends prior to ordering because they said the treats all tasted way too sweet and did not even taste good! milky mama has terrible customer service. if you want help boosting your milk supply check with a real lactation consultant that is not about making money but more about helping mothers.

my roommate is very resistant to health care. but was sick with a cough & was referred to primary medical & was given an appointment with lauren corrigan. np, & she is wonderful.  she made suggestions regarding his health

my husband, aged 91, had a medical emergency far from home as we were vacationing on south padre island. i reviewed his symptoms with our triage nurse at our primary care physician and was advised to take him to the er. corpus christi medical center - bay was the nearest facility, still 25 mi away on a dark and foggy night. the waiting room was full of people waiting wearing surgical masks....we took the last two seats and had barely sat down and we were called in. in rapid order my husband had an iv, xray, ct, dr's visit and meds ordered. armando, the nurse checked on us often. we can't say enough about dr trent martinez
and the care we received.

review:
i had never done acupuncture and acquired an acute virus last year. my health practitioner said good rest and building my immune system was all i could do. my friend referred me to erica and after one yes one treatment i was on the path to recovery. i could feel the life force coming back immediately. i was so impressed, i asked what other things could be targeted with acupuncture. i also had suffered from menstrual issues since puberty and erica discussed her expertise in women's health and hormone health. it's been almost a year and my body feels calibrated and as it should, an experience i had to discover. 
erica has a pure heart, extensive knowledge and takes a scientific, professional and compassionate approach in her practice. i am so pleased with the investment i have made in myself and my health. i have all good things to say about this experience.

i have been experiencing pain in my throat for over two weeks and home remedies have not been working so i decided to visit exer in west hills and was very excited because i've heard great reviews about their other locations. i will give them 2 stars because the front desk was very nice and the location was very clean. however, nurse was really rude and short and they weren't busy so i'm not sure what the rush was. the dr listened to me way better and he noticed that my left tonsil was swollen and i had fluid in my ear. they tested me for strep throat and he came back and said it was negative. which is great but that's where he left it. he told me it's just a virus and to get otc medicine. it's sad that my bill is probably going to be over $200 for them to tell me exactly what i've been doing. i went in because my symptoms have been going on for too long and not getting any better. i have been sick for close to 3 weeks and i don't know what to do. i typically don't leave reviews but i have never been so disappointed in the way i was dismissed. untreated for a big price. it's unfair.
went to dr firooz several years ago for a severe rheumatoid arthritis virus, she was a godsend. thank you dr firooz!

i had to be checked for conjunctivitis right during the middle of all of the coronavirus madness. although i was unable to reach them by phone i was able to make it same day appointment. when i arrived i was impressed by how clean and uncluttered it is but what really impressed me was the stellar staff. the receptionist was friendly professional and reassuring. next i was interviewed by a medical assistant. again she was friendly, relaxed and professional. finally i saw the rn. she quickly diagnosed me and again was friendly and professional. i was so impressed with the quality of the staff and especially how they conducted themselves despite being super busy that day. i actually felt as pampered as if i'd gone to a spa. i can't recommend them highly enough.

when i went to the take care clinic i had already been sick for about 10 days. it felt like the worst cold ever but just wouldn't go away. i just walked in and put my name in the queue and was able to get in about 30-40 minutes later. they gave me a strep throat culture and a flu culture and listened to my breathing and asked about my symptoms, etc. the physician's assistant could not have been nicer. she prescribed flonase, benzonatate, and doxycycline.  the flonase and the benzonatate were completely worthless but the doxycycline was exactly what i needed to kick the virus. after about 2 more days i finally could tell i was on my way up rather than down. i would return to the take care clinic.

my son almost died on me because his pediatrician kept telling me that he just had a virus when he was actually asthmatic.i showed the doctor a video where you could see his ribs and i told the doctor something is not right.i was at this kaiser twice in a week i was told he was fine he just got another virus.i took him to a different kaiser they rushed him to the hospital his oxygen level was 40 percent was at the hospital for 2 days.it was a female doctor at the loveland location

okay, this is my  second appointment with this group, my first appointment was at the main office on shadow lane and i was impressed, but a very different experience at this location. while everyone here was friendly, efficient and professional there was  one exception: the recepttionist -she was coughing andsneezing the whole time i was in the waiting room, other patients waiting there would look at her every time she coughed or sneezed and shake their heads,  i went to her to ask her if she was okay, and she shook her head no. , there she sat, coughing no and sneezing, in a doctors office, with a waiting room full  of potentially vulnerable people with the whole world in fear ofthe coronavirus  outbreak in  china. no anti- viralmask and zero situational  awareness, get a clue or stayhome!!! if you are sick during an epidemic

it was my first time there. i was told i would receive an hour for my regular facial. i got there 5 mins before my schedule time. 7 mins after my appointment time i was asked to fill out a short form online. my facialist then came out a few mins later to retrieve me but did not introduce herself. she used latex gloves for the facial and did minimal cleansing and facial massage. a few extractions and a mask and i was done in 45 mins. that's it. i didn't complain as it didnt feel the facialist was in the right energy to do it proper anyway. i left feeling disappointed. i hope this feedback will help improve tact and skillset.

review: publix truly makes the grocery shopping experience much more pleasurable. i was in the area for a few days and decided to stop by for some goodies to keep me stocked during my stay. the online deli ordering is phenomenal. they had my cuts ready for me upon arrival saving me plenty of time at the counter. the beverly store was pristinely maintained. plus, the customer service here is second to none so i was content during my visit. i found everything i needed and much more. it's great to take advantage of their bogo deals as they vary weekly. i scored some great steaks on sale so i also added the ingredients for the marínade and chimichurri it deserved. plenty of selection in the wine department kept me contemplating certain bottles. the bakery had some fresh rye bread for my breakfast toast which sealed the deal. it truly is a pleasure shopping at publix.

decided to try this urgent care after a poor experience at another one in the area. big mistake- i was the only one in the office and seen quickly which was the only upside of my appointment. the np came in, asked me what i was in for (bad cold and sinus pain), tapped my face and checked my throat (after i told her it didn't hurt). i tried explaining my other symptoms and she pretty much shooed me out of the office and told me to get over the counter meds that i said i had already been trying and they weren't not working. she didn't check my chest, ears or nose or even ask about how long i've been sick. this is not a thorough check- i understand viral illnesses are going around but you should give your patient a thorough visit before shooing them out. i'd even understand more if the office was busy but i was the only patient and can't help but feel like the np pushed me out didn't want to get my illness (while wearing a mask) - that's your job!

i have to applaud landauer medstar for their consistency. they will screw up anything they are given the chance to screw up. every time i order cpap supplies they screw up. they send a mask, but not tubing. or they send tubing but no mask. their employees apparently flunked the exam to get a job at mcdonald's. all of this could be avoided if they had a functional web site for ordering supplies, which they don't. instead, you are left dealing with a soviet-era call center that asks you for the same information three times over. landauer is so bad that many people pay out of pocket to use cpap.com just to avoid dealing with them. the sole reason they exist is that they are the cheapest possible provider to insurers, which basically sell patients down the river by using them. i sincerely hope there is an hmo executive out there whose mom needs cpap supplies so that he too can have the joy of dealing with landauer met. sadly, you have wasted your time by reading this review, since they have a local monopoly with your insurer. you are forced to use them. ha ha ha ha.

although the staff was extremely welcoming and friendly, i wasn't impressed by their service. i was on time for my appointment but still had to wait 30 mins after i completed the forms. they make you take 14 photos of your face for analysis. i'm not sure if you can decline, but i wish it was an option. i guess there's a machine that analyzes your skin before treatment, but it was still in use while i was waiting so my esthetician skipped it -- which was totally fine by me. i think i prefer a physical analysis of my skin from a knowledgeable esthetician rather than a fancy machine. 

the "acne facial" itself was okay for the price. it was basically just triple exfoliation, some minor extractions, a mask, high frequency and the led light. pretty basic. in my experience, extractions usually involve lightly breaking the skin then an extraction, but she mainly just did the pushing motion. it's been a few hours and the areas she worked on feel irritated but not "cleaned out." 

the least enjoyable part of my facial was how much the esthetician talked, but i think because it was my first time there, she probably felt the need to explain everything. i think it's fine to say a few things about the steps during the facial, but i didn't need an ingredient list and a detailed explanation of what each product does. i hated feeling like i needed to be attentive and responsive to everything she was saying because i didn't want to be rude, but i honestly just wanted to relax and not talk for an hour. she also up-sells the products she uses which also took away from the "relaxing" aspect of the service. 

lastly, they make you take a survey at the end of your service, but they also email you and text you again after to ask for more feedback. i found the whole process to be a bit overbearing, but i'm sure there are a lot of clients who could appreciate those details. 

if it's your first time there, you should definitely carve out at least 2 hours for your appointment. i arrived 2 and was out the door by 4, and that was without the machine analysis.

my kaiser doctor suspected i had sleep apnea, so i was sent to the sleep lab. they ran tests, and found i have sleep apnea. i liked how the test was a take home device. the negative about the experience was that i had to pay $170 for a cpap device. some people got up and left when they heard the price.

there's not much follow up after you leave. if you have problems like waking up with the equipment on, they tell you to get used to wearing the mask.

not impressed at all. i was avoiding going to the er or the doctors. this was the sickest i had ever been in my life, but i had no fever and figured it would pass as it most likely was a virus. i was forced by my employer to go to the doctor to avoid occurrences. i was vomiting constantly non-stop for days on end. i couldn't keep anything down. i laid in bed and went from the bed to the bathroom vomiting. i was then vomiting blood. (probably from the non-stop vomiting and dry heaving for 4 days straight) i went to urgent care and couldn't walk or stand long as i felt like i was going to pass out and was very short of breath. i had to sit down every few steps. they stated they couldn't help me and to go to the er as i was severely dehydrated. because every time i stood up, my blood pressure would drop.

i was given an i.v. for fluids. while i was receiving fluids, i heard the nurses complaining about the patients and that they "treat them and then street them" as the patients were a pain.

(he had renal failure) they took him in, they were unable to stop his bleeding, so they released him. he went to his practitioner and the practitioner was furious with geneva and had him go to f.f. thompson hospital where they were able to treat him and give him a blood transfusion.

do not go here!!!

this review is for anyone who is on the edge. for those who want to get this done, but scared, or doesn't trust the process. i'm currently a week post-op and here to tell you.. do it! 

i've always struggled with having a few more chins than i liked. thanks to the heredity "turkey neck" and..ok..some taco bell and tito's..i've always been self conscience of my chin(s), and who doesn't want to look better and more confident in their selfies!? when i saw an ad on instagram (my fbi agents listening to my woes again..), i thought it was to good to be true. i immediately sent an email over for more information. i did an at home consult, which was essentially me pinching my fat and answering a few questions. within 24 hours, linda gave me a call. gonna take a moment here to shout out to my girl linda- holy crap was she amazing! she answered all of my questions (and let me tell you, i had some weird ones...) and never judged and made sure i had all my questions answered. i probably called back 2-3 more times with additional weird questions and each time she answered and make me feel confident enough to book. i booked my procedure for 12/20. probably up until the night i was emailing more questions. this just goes to show how responsive linda and the entire team is..they made me feel so comfortable!

when i walked in on 12/20 i was greeted by my girl linda who immediately got up and greeted me with a hug- totaling reassuring me i came to the right people and the right place. when it was time i changed into my robe, and dr. yassanow and nurse anne were so awesome at reassuring me how simple and painless it was. after i got marked up anne gave me a cocktail of calming meds. dr. yassanow asked me what kind of music i liked and he put on some country for me (right before the procedure i changed my mind to backstreet boys- i appreciate you listening to that for me!). he then (using laymen's terms here..) put in the numbing stuff. just a quick pinch here and there- nothing painful, and absolutely tolerable. while we waited for it to kick in, anne chatted with me the whole time, taking my mind off everything instead of sitting with my own thoughts. and then it was cannula time...

so the question i kept asking was what does this feel like going in and out and how does it not hurt!? well here's the answer- it doesn't hurt at all. it feels like you have an electric toothbrush and you're lightly touching your face with it. it took only about 10 minutes, and i remember the last few i was singing the bsb song that was playing- shout out to my chill pills! 

after you're done they put a compression mask on you and you hang in post op for a few mins and then you're on your way! dr. yassanow called me that night to make sure i was doing ok, which i totally was. anne called me the next day to check up, as well. honestly, the worst part, and it's not even bad, is just wearing the face spanx (as i like to call them) as it can be uncomfortable- but i'm getting used to it. they give you pain pills, and i didn't need them. in my experience, there was no real pain. 

48 hours later i took my face spanx off and already saw such a noticeable difference!  (picture attached of the difference in just 48 houra week later, i still have a bit of swelling. although you only need to wear garment at night after first 48 hours, the more you wear it the better the results. i've probably only taken mine off 4 hours in the past week, and will continue to wear.  i'm so excited to go to my 3 month appointment and see what a difference! i also can't wait to get more work done!

i hope this helps you in making the decision to press on. thank you again to the entire team at elite for making this such a delightful process! you'll be seeing me soon! :)

this is for dr. timothy lane only. i have never left a review for a doctor but i guess there is a first time for everything. 
i went to the orthopedic institute today to see dr. lane for a second opinion on my knee. in the past i have seen two other doctors (sharkey and pritt) in this office and had excellent and timely care with them so i was expecting a similar experience with dr. lane. 
i cannot attest to his knowledge or advice. no one came in to explain why the doctor was so far behind and i had other things i'd rather do then sit longer waiting for a doctor who viewed his time worth more than mine.  while i was waiting i began to notice some things that disturbed me as a patient and a retired nurse. the room i was in bad need of a thorough cleaning. the floors were very dirty with grime in between the tiles and in the corners. it was apparent that someone had sat on the exam couch (paper was wrinkled) and it had not been changed. with the flu and coronavirus rampant, cleanliness should be top on the list for any doctors office. the medical assistant or nurse who took my blood pressure and temperature did not wash her hands before toughing me and i find that truly disturbing as all health professionals should know that the best way to prevent the spread of communicable illnesses is proper hand washing. i probably would have noticed more but after an hour and a half, i got up and left without seeing the doctor. if this were the only game in town i probably would have stayed, but it isn't and uf ortho doesn't make you wait.

obviously in the middle of the flu season you can expect to wait longer times in the waiting room. what makes it so bad is the receptionist that checks patients in is extremely rude and unprofessional. this and they will not give anyone masks, so adults and children are all in a small space coughing and spreading their germs. while i was waiting i went up to the receptionist to ask for a mask, and before i could even open my mouth to ask she shouted at me "just go sit down! they will get to you!". i was not going to complain about the wait or how slow they were. she was even ruder to other patients who were being respectful to her. she would just snap at them for no reason. would give customer service from her a 0 star. the people in the back were a little friendlier.

had a great experience here, picked up my cpap machine and was helped by danielle del lattore, she has great customer service skills, she went above and beyond explaining everything and answered all my questions.  2nd visit to pick up my heated tube and discuss my mask, malory helped me and she is really good when it comes to the product, a total "geek" when it came to explaining everything....she was also amazing.  i would give them 10  if i could.

words cannot begin to express how wonderful my experience was here!  i was warmly greeted by victoria and the reception area was clean and vibrant.  i appreciated that there were sterile masks; tissues and pens at the counter.  the registration process was smooth and fast.

i was seen in no time at all and i enjoyed watching hgtv in the waiting area.  rosa came to get me and she was super sweet just like victoria.  the place is huge!!! i reminded me of an upscale hospital floor yet nicer with a warm touch to it.

my wife and i took both of tori's classes today.  the first is an 8 hour class focused on the birthing process and the second is a 2 hour class focused on infant care.

the classes were packed with information.  not a single question went unanswered.  even timely questions such as how expecting parents should react to covid-19 were answered carefully and fully.

i cannot recommend these classes highly enough, and will certainly recommend them to expecting parents in my circle.

note also that tori is a celebrity in the labor and delivery world.  she is the author of one of the leading books on the subject - the joy of pregnancy.  our ob recommended her classes to us, i think, primarily because of her status in the community.

was well worth it.
laid up with a broken ankle. first time ordering groceries online. fast easy process. text message when they were on their way. courteous and professional delivery person.

i was diagnosed with add and prescribed adderall to help treat it.  caremark has gone out of their way to make me feel like 1.) a drug addict 2.) a crazy person.

the second month i had the script the local pharmacist told me i missed her ordering deadline and would have to wait for an additional week before she would place the order, it would be 5 days after that i'd be able to get it.  that means it would take 12 days for me to get my script and the pharmacist offered no alternate solution.

when i called around to see if anyone had adderall so i could transfer the script, the pharmacist all treated me like i was a drug addict that was going to come to rob them.  they refused to tell me anything and said i had to come in with a physical script.

the customer service phone line did nothing and called 4 pharmacies as a "courtesy"  but wouldn't tell me if any location was able to fill my prescription. 

my psychiatrist's office called and raised hell and got me script filled from another local pharmacy but the annoyance had already set in.

the next month i didn't realize that i had to have the prescription called in every month so the script lapsed.  i called up caremark who basically shrugged and told me they couldn't/wouldn't do anything.  my psychiatrist called in my script which took two days for caremark to "receive" the script.  

i called up caremark two days later to get a shipping estimate.  the first person i spoke to told me they were going to rush it and it would ship that day or tomorrow at the latest.

two days later and i call back again, this time the person told me it would take an additional 3 days for the script to be "processed" because "it is a controlled substance" and then it would take 3 - 5 days to ship.  that puts the script out 12 days again.

when i asked if there was anything that could be done to speed it up, they said that i could pay for next day air...again making it like they were doing me a favor.

next month, i call my psychiatrist and get them to submit the script early so this doesn't keep happening.  it sat in limbo for 10 days before i called up and caremark claimed that my insurance denied it and they were waiting on info from the psychiatrist.

i call my psychiatrist who flat-out tells me that caremark is lying.  my psychiatrist assures me they will get it figured out.  

the next day i call caremark again to see if it's all sorted.  this rep tells me that it still looks like it is on hold but they can see notes that the psychiatrist's office cleared up the issue.  not knowing what else to do she canceled my order to submit a new one and was going to put a "rush" on it.

after a few minutes, the rep realizes that because it is a controlled substance the new order was going to have to wait 5 days before it could be released (note: this was actually the first person to tell me about the 5 day cool off period, i just added it in in my earlier examples).  i got them to clarify that the order was now going to take even longer than it was before.  they reluctantly agree.

i end up having to pay for overnight shipping again and waiting 10 days to get my medicine.

my last order, submitted 12/27, was canceled because i switched insurance.  due to the 5 day cool off period on controlled substances, they won't be able to submit it to my insurance company and they can transfer me to my new insurance provider.

of the 5 refills i have gotten on this prescription, 4 have come late and i have had to pay next day air.  the customer service's attitude is to shrug and apologizes.  i have asked several people what would happen if this was medication for my heart?  or if this was a medication that was going to keep me alive?  would they still act like i was just trying to score?

review:
why 1? ( please read about the first corona infection below ) i checked in quickly around 11:15. the patient care associate didn't call me in until 2:00 pm. the poor rn was struggling to document her unfinished assessment when i whisked away to a different room and then the pa came in at past 3:00 pm.  she asked me a bunch of questions and her diagnosis was either i have cancer or severe infection.  she wrote a referral to see a specialist that will get me in the schedule in 2 weeks.

oh, furthermore, the first positive corvid 19 infection is from a physician traveling from iran with her husband who is also an er doctor. they were all whispering and said not to tell anything about it. figures. i blame dr. david l. reich for all this hush hush. he is no better than his predecessor. they do not care about the staff and in turn they do not care about the community.

they do not take credit cards, (receptionist said 'he doesn't have the swiper" or something like that. methinks he doesn't want to pay the low fees for processing credit cards) and for my first visit of $150, a nurse took my vitals, asked the usual questions including curiously, about my pregnancies, (my 'kids' are 34 and 39) and then donald came in. he was frowning, looking over my paperwork, did not make eye contact with me and was decidedly unfriendly, i was confused. he asked if i had any other issues- i said, yes, some congestion and coughing that i'm trying to mitigate with dust mask (and vit c)- he didn't bother to listen to my lungs or heart. glad others, with proper insurance companies, get treated so well but frankly, i want my money back. i will never go back and do not recommend. when he left the exam room where i was not examined, he tossed some sheets my way for blood testing without explaining what he was looking for, nor that i had to fast before the test (previous doc did not have me do that) he didn't ask one question about my diet or mental health. it was overall a humiliating, demeaning, frustrating experience.

no. at least, no for me. i had disappointing experience.
