review:
i took my friend to the er last thursday. she was in excruciating head pain and vomiting. we got there at 4:00 pm. it was very busy. the nurses and doctors are kind. however, no one saw her for two hours. by 7:00 she had an x-ray. no one addressed her migraine. no one addressed  her vomiting. her spouse came at 6:30pm . i went home at 7:00pm. by 12:00 am they finally gave her some pain meds and an i.v.  eight hours of suffering in the  er surrounded  by very sick people, many vomiting. my friend did not have the flu. the next day i was violently ill for 24 hrs. my doctor thought it was a virus but perhaps food poisoning. my husband and i ate the same food and he was fine. i think i got ill from  being in the er four hours even though i wore a mask ( which is probably useless in preventing flu virus from penetrating). 

i would  not recommend los robles hospital emergency room if you are sick. go to urgent care or stay home and wait it out. 

btw she's allergic to penicillin and they gave her an antibiotic very similar to penicillin. she had  to go to urgent care the next day to get a steroid shot to combat the  allergic reaction (hives) she had from the antibiotic they gave her in er.

also, i  suggest you investigate the  hospital's reporting of infections gotten in the hospital.

as you can tell if you look at how often i write reviews, i am extremely selective in my assessments. to cause me to write a review means you either hit a home run, or you struck out. unfortunately it's the latter with the emergency room of this hospital. we live within walking distance, and have lived in the community for 20 years +. in that time, we've used the hospital or the er just once or twice.  in other words, we're healthy, use regular doctors to meet our basic health needs, and are not the type of people who run to the er for a paper cut. additionally, we have truly excellent insurance supplied by our employers. 

with that as background, we visited the er at 1 am this week. my husband had been flat on his back with the flu/cold since returning from texas about 10 days ago. he was running a fever, coughing frequently, hadn't been able to eat, and was having trouble breathing. when we checked in we explained his symptoms and told them several times he'd been in international airports since coronavirus was starting to be talked about. when the er doctor sat down, he asked my husband "what's going on?" my husband very reasonably responded to that question by saying "i think i have the flu." the doctor shot back "i'll make the diagnosis." that sums up our experience in the er. they were generally detached, rude, and acted like we were bothering them by being there. the one exception was the truly friendly guy with the portable machine he rolled around to get a bit more info from patients such as religious preference. but the nurses and the doctor were awful. they didn't follow up with us about my husband being in houston airport (where the coronavirus was found), and when he complained about being lightheaded they initially ignored him and then reluctantly offered a wheelchair. they also debated between themselves as to whether they should offer an inhaler. once concluded, one trotted off to find the doctor. the other disappeared without telling us anything. a third employee sat staring at his phone, tapping away, and never said a word to us or looked our way even though we were perhaps 3 feet from him. i was standing the entire time and none offered me a chair.

as a community member, i don't feel los robles provided even minimally acceptable service. i looked on their website for a place to lodge complaints but there isn't one. interesting. additionally, there are more "1" ratings of this hospital on this site than "5" ratings. i'm not surprised by that.  i'm sure there will be an insipid follow up comment from jasmin o. saying "thank you for your comment, sorry we didn't meet your expectations" or something noncommittal like that. the fact that the hospital offers the same canned response to every poor review indicates to me that there is a lack of true caring.

everyone has bad days at work, i get that. but in certain industries, that can be dangerous. you don't want ticked off air traffic controllers, lackadaisical nuclear energy plant operators, or medical staff who lack compassion and don't really want to help patients. i expected more out of the er. we won't return; we'll go to an urgent care spot if needed in the future. which is too bad since los robles loses a future chance to over bill our very generous insurance company.

bottom line, i don't recommend anyone willingly going to this hospital's er based on our experience this week.

this place is a joke, never bringing my family to this circus ever again.

review:
rise prime wellness is absolutely amazing!!!! the staff is extremely friendly, knowledgeable and all-around awesome! they create an inviting atmosphere and we always feel welcome.
  
the process, itself, is so easy.  you change into a bathrobe in private 1-person rooms and step into the chamber room.  you have the option of keeping as much or as little clothing on.  you put on slippers and gloves, a head-band to cover your ears and a mask to protect your nose and lips.  when you disrobe to enter and exit the chamber, the female technician turns around to face a wall so absolute privacy is maintained.  you have your choice of music to help the 3 minutes of cold race by.

i started with rise prime wellness to help heal after shoulder surgery.  by using the chamber twice a week for 6 weeks or so, i was healed and back on the football field in 3 months, vs the 6 months plus the surgeon said it would take.  i am a true believer of the power of rise's full-body cryotherapy.  

if i had to describe rise prime wellness' full-body cryo chamber in 1 word, i would say "magical"! it is truly an amazing feat to let the cold heal a person: mind, body and spirit!

i am addicted and will continue to use rise prime wellness forever!

if i could give this place zero stars i would. the first time i went was when i broke my ankle. made us wait over four hours just to get an x-ray and we had to share a room with another patient. the next time was even worse. my girlfriend came in with abdominal pains and they made us wait three hours just to see a doctor. the doctor than told her she needed an ultrasound, which we waited two hours for and than another two for the results. after that they made her get a cat scan, which took up another two hours to get and another two for the results. than after all this doctor mchue came in for no more than thirty seconds to tell her nothing was wrong. they definitely just added procedures in order to rack up her hospital bill bordering on malpractice considering how much radiation a cat scan gives. after all this we had to wait another hour just so a nurse could come in for five seconds to take out her iv. when i went to complain to dr mchue, and told him we'd been at the hospital for almost 12 hours and we just need the iv to be taken out so we could go home, he rudely told me "people are dying." i understand that it's an emergency room but there were atleast ten people talking or sitting at their computers, one of which is capable of removing an iv, or dr mchue should've just done it himself when he came to see us. his attitude was not one any dr should have and it was clear he got stuck with the graveyard shift and was not happy about it. terrible terrible doctor. don't go unless you're literally dying because they will not help you. go to a different hospital if you can and definitely hope to god you don't get dr mchue, because i've never encountered a more rude or dismissive dr in my life. fuck this p

we had a less than favorable experience a few days ago at the lcom er. the er was a mess and seemed no better than what i'd expect harbor general to be like. we have very little experience in an er setting so maybe my expectations are unrealistic.

for starters, the was place filthy. the sheet on the triage nurse's intake bed was dirty.  people, we're in the middle of the corona virus problem! that thing should be changed after every patient. just so you know, i went back the next day almost 24 hours later to get some paperwork and that same dirty sheet was still on there with the same identifiable dirty shoe marks and stains. at the time of admittance, i was happy my husband was even being seen so i didn't make a fuss. in hindsight, i should have said something. 

most important however, was the lack of care he received by the attending physician dr. lu. he was impersonal and spoke very condescendingly to us. my husband was treated on a bed in the hallway the entire time hooked up to a heart a portable heart monitor!  here's a person with a heart condition and skyrocketing blood pressure, dizziness and whose been vomiting.  no blood work done, urine taken but not evaluated, and no fluids given.  and yes, i do feel entitled to decent care - i'm going to pay my bill! 

i think the main problem is too many people in our community use the er like a doctor's office with common ailments because they can't be turned away for lack of insurance or ability to pay. the staff are like robots with the barrage of problems that walk through the door. 

i'm sharing my experience because we are concerned at the level of healthcare available to us in our community during an emergency situation. is what we experienced an isolated event or is this the norm at our community er?

this is long but bare with me. this place stereotypes people with mental health history. this is strictly for their er doctors and er intake nurses (some). i have past heart problems which were corrected in high school. i was feeling close to the same way the first time i had my heart episode and went to the er in mid november. i went in for heart palpitations, shortness of breath, extreme lethargic about to pass out feeling, and weakness. when i was taken to the er by my boyfriend, because who wants to call an ambulance on their lunch break in their work parking garage and drawl that kind of attention to themselves, when i got there, the intake nurses literally did not fucking care i existed as a human. it took the nurses or security guards who help wheel people in and out to tell them to open the door and let me in. the er intake nurse didn't give rats a$$ that i couldn't breath well, didn't pay attention to my boyfriend who was literally handing her an emergency card i keep in my wallet of all my allergies and medical history. my boyfriend told them my symptoms, they didn't even think about hooking me up to a ekg until i was in the er exam room, which if i can remember correctly was about 15 to 20 minutes after i arrived. the nurses were ok that day and the nurse who put my iv in kept moving it because she couldn't get the blood out...ok we'll go somewhere else?! so much pain while feeling like i could pass out.

this is a review of dr. john giddens at fremont urgent care. 
i'd like to preface this by stating that i've never been very fond of doctors, am very skeptical of big pharma, and have always tried holistic/ alternative methods first whenever struck with ailments. 
after suffering a slip and fall at work back in april and treating severe back pain myself through eastern medicine without much avail (my employer refused to file a workman's compensation claim stating that his insurance rates would increase and that i would be inconvenienced with people monitoring my every move, etc.) i returned to work after 2 months of recovery, mainly because i was broke. i was working through the pain to the best of my abilities. (i was a bartender and tequila helped immensely!) i subsequently fainted from exhaustion at work the following october and my back pain returned with a vengeance. i then asked my employer file a workman's comp claim so that i could seek legitimate help from real doctors. he knew i didn't have health insurance and his initial reluctance to assist me at the onset of my injury was quelled by my demands. his insurance company contacted me and i was able to choose a facility close to home. 
i got very lucky with dr. john giddens as he was selected to be the primary physician assigned to my case. he singlehandedly changed my perspective on doctors. his intelligent yet laid back demeanor is so respectable and calming. he is thorough, compassionate, efficient and explanatory. he's been a doctor for over 4 decades which, with that amount of impressive tenure, could easily go to one's head, yet he's humble and devoted to his profession. i always pegged doctors as middlemen to the pharmaceutical industry; pill-pushers dispensing whatever they feel might mask an illness while meeting their fill quotas. dr. giddens broke that stereotype. he showed me that being a doctor isn't just about seeing patients and offering typical treatments, repeat, repeat, etc. he actually looks at every unique case, computes his hypotheses through examination, and tailors treatment modified to a person's particular physiology. it's really impressive. if dr. jane crusher and data from star trek the next generation had a baby, it would be dr. giddens. 
he's very good at what he does, and i should know. i'm a very difficult patient! i have tested his patience as an impatient patient plenty, yet he's always stayed kind, informative and even-keel. 
you'll be in good hands with dr. giddens. he's also been voted best doctor of fremont a few times so i'm not alone in this assessment.

i had picked up something nasty, either on a flight from dublin to london, a flight from london to vegas, or from one of the thousands of people who insisted on shaking hands during ces. whatever the cause, i was suffering, and it was lingering. i figured i should get looked at, in case it was something crazy (and this was a few weeks before the news of the coronavirus hit...)

the waiting room was pretty packed when i got there, with a handful of people wearing surgical masks. a sign at check-in asked those exhibiting cold or flu symptoms to don a mask, so i followed suit.

check-in was fast and painless, once i got past the forms. after turning in my completed documents, i sat in one of the chairs, trying not to cough too loudly or blow my nose too often, waiting for my name to get called.

it actually didn't take very long, given the number of people in line ahead of me. the intake nurse brought me back for vitals, and to ask all the necessary questions. she then sat me down in a room and told me the doctor would be right with me.

want to hear something crazy? i spent more time typing that paragraph above than the doctor spent on me. he listened to the rattle in my chest, asked me a couple of questions, then diagnosed bronchitis and a sinus infection. he told me to meet him at the lobby, and we were done.

i had to ask the nurse to ask the doctor if i was contagious. to his credit, he came back out to the front to answer my question (he called me "close contact contagious", meaning i shouldn't share drinks with or kiss people, but said i'd be fine in normal situations.)

it was an okay experience, but here i am, 24 days after my visit, still working to shake the cough. my husband says i need to get to my regular doctor. he's probably right. maybe i'll make that appointment soon.

ellie made sure that no plasma would run into my ears and that i had a tissue in hand just in case i feel anything rolling down my face. i liked how she informs me of how much plasma i have left. she also gave me a small ball to squeeze onto cause i was wincing in pain and my eyes were getting watery. that was my fault because i decided not to put on anesthetic cream beforehand thinking that i could handle it due to my high pain tolerance level. but i regret it deeply.... microneedling is something else....it's another beast of pain so i definitely learned my lesson the hard way. despite that, i'm glad sai made my first experience with microneedling worthwhile. she kept my concerns in mind and focused on those areas with good motion and speed. she also adjusted the setting and depth of the needles along my face because she knew which part was more sensitive than the other. i was really impressed!! after the whole session was over, she put on a moisturizing mask for me. the nurse practitioner also popped in to check if everything went smoothly and offered some advice for the after care. ellie also reminded me to wear sunscreen and recommend me some good ones to get. thank you everyone at wave for taking care of me, especially sai for making me feel at ease. the team effort and customer service here deserve a standing ovation. i can't wait to see my skin after the healing process. will be back to update!

so thankful i found dr. lissau!  i was in vegas for a weekend trip and came down with a harsh stomach virus.  i literally couldn't start throwing up.  what a way to vacation, right?  i finally decided to call the doctor to see if he could help.  dr. lissau was at my hotel room within the hour.  he was very kind and helpful.  he came with all the medicine needed to get me back on my feet.  he even left me with fizzy potassium water to help with aftercare.  after a shot of the nausea and an hour nap, i was back up and didn't miss seeing gwen steffani with my girlfriends the same night.  dr. lissau even called to check on me the next day.  first class service and worth every penny.

recently while traveling on business i fell ill due to a stomach virus. i have to admit i usually avoid going to the doctor and try to wait these things out but i had appointments to keep while in the parsippany area. luckily a colleague recommended dr. randy spector to me.
i was very impressed with their warm and friendly staff and the high level of treatment i received.
if i'm ever ill while i'm in the lake hiawatha parsippany area i would certainly recommend them to friends and family.

this is my second time here in one week and i must say april is amazing and so sweet. i was extremely sick from a stomach virus and the medicine caused major constipation. i decided to try a colonic for relief and let me express how this was the absolute best decision i've made in 2020!! april is very informational on the process and caring. she continuously asked if i was comfortable during the process. i left out feeling relieved and was back to my normal routine. she recommended that i try an additional session, which was today and i've been energized ever since. i recommend you check her out. she's great!!!
this place takes forever.  needed a tb skin test and wait was over 2 hours.  with corona virus concerns, there is no screening and separation of acutely ill patients.

i walked in to the hospital er yesterday 13feb2020 at about 1300hrs. waited about 10 min before being addressed by a receptionist. i was able to then present my paper showing i am severely neutropenic and should not be made to wait in the er to him. i was seen about 7-10 min later in one of the back rooms where my blood pressure, temperature, and heart rate was taken. i showed the lady in there the same note to which she replied, ok i'll put you in the system as urgent urgent. we spoke for a little. she was a nice lady. i then went and waited with my fiancé in a corner of the er because i shouldn't be around other sick people. it was about an hour before i spoke to a new receptionist asking her how much longer it would be for me while presenting her with my paper from my doctor. she told me 15 min, they're cleaning a room. and so i don't have to be in the er i can wait in my car and she'll come out and grab me if they come earlier. so, we walked to grab my car and pulled it to the er. we waited about 15min when i asked my fiancé to valet the car and we'll wait outside for a little, it shouldn't be much longer now. with my two bags for the extended stay i was expecting, seeing how i have to get a transfusion and a bone marrow transplant because i have aplastic anaemia. we waited outside for about 20 more minutes before i decided to go in and ask the receptionist again how long it would be, because it's cold outside. she stated she doesn't know. so i went back outside and waited almost another 20 minutes before deciding to leave. in total i waited roughly 2 hours. i went back in to talk to the receptionist. i calmly and professionally explained to her that she shouldn't give me a specific time even if it's an estimate. because she did that, my expectations were based off what she told me, we were waiting outside in the cold for longer than we should have if she had just told me i can't give you a time right now... i can't believe that i couldn't wait in any room regardless to if it was an er room or not. at this point if i get sick from all the people being in the er sick, coughing and sneezing when i first waited, that virus could kill me. hence why i am upset.

this place is the best. i was getting frustrated trying to find a good primary health provider through my insurance, united healthcare.  after a few failed attempts with places far away and no availability for months out, i finally found this place, right off the 101 and i got my first appointment within a week of contacting them. awesome. the building is huge, with many rooms. bigger than anywhere i've ever been. and it's clean and inviting. they even have a book exchange in the lobby and a whole separate waiting area for kids with disney movies playing!  it feels like they really care about the community.  you would think with a place this ginourmous the wait times would be insane. but no!  they have everything digital, check in & check out is super quick, they use these laptop type devices where you can just swipe your card and pay.  and all of your records are on your patient portal you can access online anytime. very modern and on top of things!  i'll admit the front desk folks are a bit underwhelming, but helpful enough. i'm sure they are very busy!  the nurses are fantastic.  super friendly and easy to talk to. i was pleased with my visits and i felt the practitioners were very knowledgeable and really cared about helping me rather than just prescribing tons of things to mask my symptoms. i had to do a blood draw and i was in and out of there within 15 min!  i think that's a new record!  they send text reminders for appointments and are great about refilling rx requests quickly. i am so grateful to have found them.

i went in today for a sick visit. i called while at work and they were able to fit me in right after work, which was great. when i got there they took me back to the room pretty quickly, but i was sitting in the room for quite some time and for someone who is sick it was extremely difficult. when the doctor finally came into the room she asked a few questions, one being "have you been around anyone with any illness recently?" to which i replied "i'm a teacher." many of my students have been out sick with the flu and other illnesses. when they took my temperature, it read 99.4, but they failed to ask if i had recently taken any medication to control my fever, which i had. after the exam they told me "it was probably just a virus" because my sore throat didn't have white spots so it couldn't be strep. i have had strep without presenting any white spots on my throat before. when i got home i took my temperature and it was at 102 and would not go down with medication! you can be sure i'll be calling back tomorrow for a second opinion as i do not believe that whatever i have is "just a virus".

i had a really good experience here.  i went in to be fitted with a mask for my new cpap machine. jonathon was very helpful. he spent a lot of time  showing me the options for my mask. he also answered all my other questions and gave me helpful tips. he was on time and i took the product home with me.

i brought my mother here at 7:30pm - she is experiencing severe pain and this will be the second er visit in a month. at initial glance, the er is filthy. food scraps on the floor, face masks discarded everywhere, and individuals are scattered in the hallways/sitting on the floor.

after the initial greeting, we sat in the waiting room for 2 hours before any service was administered (no iv, pain medications, evaluation or check-in from 7:30-9:30pm). the entire hospital's system (internet and internal systems) went down during this time for roughly an hour. it seemed to be the primary excuse when i politely asked for an update.

after the third hour, they removed her from an er room and placed her in a hallway chair (unable to sit because of the pain). this was pretty shocking.

we are now working on hour 7 and the only care has been two pain medications. pretty inadequate service overall. if there is a next time, we will be taking her elsewhere.
fac_name: St. Joseph's Hospital and Medical Center

review: brought in my young daughter who was experiencing a high fever. they tested for flu and it was negative so i was told it's a virus and was sent home. her fever did not break by the following morning so i went to a pediatric urgent care who correctly diagnosed her with strep. then i was given a $1700 bill for the ineffective medical care. the itemized bill showed it was a level 3 visit and listed a battery of lab tests (all from one flu swab). i called to have the charges verified through their audit nurse and of course they state the charges are correct. however, the doctor specifically told me he was only testing for flu because her lungs were clear meaning there was no sign of pneumonia and they couldn't have tested for strep bc they misdiagnosed her. what else could they have possibly tested for? and if the "flu" is a level 3 visit, what would you have charged me for an actual emergency?!
fac_name: Houston Methodist Sienna Plantation Emergency Care Center

review: i 've been extremely impressed, with  the high quality of care, as well as the high level of sensitivity we've experienced here.  i 'm retired now, but my work history as a neuro. monitoring tech at brigham and women's as well as mass general hospital, for 40 years--enables me to be a "critic" of sorts.  my adult son with down syndrome, had fever, horrible bronchial cough, and upset stomach for a day and one half.  being sunday (feb. 23, 2020)  i didn't have a lot of faith at what we might experience at the medical center.  when we checked in we were given masks, appropriately.  we were taken in at the time of our appointment, the medical assistant quickly acknowledging my son having fever, and documenting her findings for the physician.  prior to leaving the room, she attempted to make my son as comfortable as possible--how refreshing--patient care!!  the physician was timely, kind, and efficiently fantastic.  within one hour, we had a nebulizer treatment, blood work, further lab testing, as well as a chest x-ray--all which led to a diagnosis of influenza a, and pneumonia.  all needed rx's were called into our local pharmacy, which were all ready for pick-up when we arrived there perhaps 20 minutes later.  we were home, convalescing, within 2 1/2 hours of our appointment.  i can only offer the highest of accolades for the entire system, especially the amazingly awesome, superlative physician, who seemingly walks on water!

we were camping here in waco when my daughter spiked a high fever. she was complaining of her throat hurting and felt a bit nauseous. i found premier on google and liked that they had such high ratings. we went inside and it was very clean. they had a beverage station and a station with masks, tissue and hand sanitizer to help not spread germs. the staff and doctors were very friendly and we were in and out in less than an hour. would definitely recommend this urgent care.

i have been extremely sick for 2 days and knew i had the flu, so i called my doctor's office to see if they could call in a prescription for tamaflu for me. they said they dont do that, i would have to come in, and my regular doctor didnt have any openings so i had to see doctor dolan. fine. i will have my husband drive me and my 2 toddlers, who are all also sick but not as bad as me, to the appointment (because i am too sick to drive and we dont have a sitter).  so now we have 4 people sick with the flu in their waiting room. sounds great so far, right? way smarter than just calling in a prescription durning the middle of flu season, right? 

so the nurse calls me back, takes my vitals and swabs my nose for the flu virus. fine, whatever. then the doctor comes in and wants to know what i "want?". kind of weird thing to ask, but i tell her i think i have the flu and i would like tamaflu. she tells me i don't have a fever and i let her know i am taking dayquil religiously every 4 hours because i am very sick and it helps a little with the fevers. then she asks me how long i've had symptoms. i tell her and she says that's longer than 48 hours and they dont prescribe tamaflu after 48 hours. mind you, we are now at about 50 hours. i asked her why not, since i have read many times that tamaflu helps even if you start taking it after 48 hours. her answer was "it makes people nauseous". ok, i think that if that's your only concern you should let the patient make that decision. 

so after that conversation, dr. dolan says "your flu results will be done in a couple minutes". i told her i didnt see the point in waiting on the flu results because they wouldn't prescribe me medication anyway. all of the sudden she says that i might be a special case because i take steroids for an autoimmune disease that makes me more susceptible to pneumonia. 

at this point i'm wondering what's wrong with this woman. she goes on and on about how she wont give me tamaflu because it's been close 50 hours and it makes people nauseous, then literally her next sentence is telling me i'm a special case and i need to be on tamaflu.

anyway, she leaves for the lab results and guess what, i have flu type a. she gets my local pharmacy phone number to send over a prescription for tamaflu and i ask her for a prescription for cough medicine. she says they dont give prescriptions for that. fine. can you reccomend an over the counter cough medicine? "we reccomend a teaspoon of honey". i asked her to repeat herself because i was in disbelief. she repeated "a teaspoon of honey". listen lady, i already know you are a nut, but if you think i am getting up every 3 minutes in the night with coughing fits to eat a teaspoon of honey, not only will i not get any sleep but i will have diabetes by morning.

anyway, we head over to the pharmacy to pick up the tamaflu i had to suffer mind games at the hands of a doctor to get, and guess what. they didnt send my prescription to the pharmacy i specifically asked them too and gave them the number for. nope. they submitted it to my mail order pharmacy. so the kind people at the pharmacy called my doctor and told them to send over the prescription and cancel the order with the mail order pharmacy because my insurance wouldn't cover both. cool. except now i have to wait another half hour for my prescription. we wait a half hour, go back up, and they tell us my doctor cant seem to cancel my mail order prescription and they wont be able to do anything for me until the mail order is canceled. at this point i'm exhausted so we just leave.

as we get in the car to drive home my doctor's office calls to tell me what the pharmacy people already told me, that they sent the prescription to the wrong place and they were not able to fix it and i about lost my mind. they made a huge deal about how many hours i had been sick and didnt want to give me the medication, but then realized they should, but instead of sending it where they were supposed to, they sent it to mail order where it would take literally days to fill. i told them to cancel all the orders since "hours" seem to make a huge difference in efficacy. they had already wasted at least 2 additional hours at this point and i didnt even have the medicine yet. i just needed to rest and the stress was making me feel even worse.

done, right? nope, 2 hours later i get an email from the mail order pharmacy saying that my order will be delivered in 4 to 7 days. thanks dr. dolan and thanks to her super incompetent staff, i guess i will just wait and see if i get pneumonia.

oh, also, the staff at the doctor's office was apparently supposed to have me put on a mask so i wouldn't spread the flu virus to others in the waiting room with my horrible cough, and they didnt. doctor dolan told me that after she came into the examination room.

bye bye saint mary's! if this flu doesnt kill me i will be seeking care at another practice.

if the front desk staff is too panicked about the covid -19 that they don't want patients coming in then they should close the doors and go home without pay. went today to get checked out. either have a respiratory virus or the flu. no fever. i know everyone is freaking out about the covid-19 virus right now but as a health care worker myself i knew it was ok to go to a walk in because i did not have a fever. i got to the check in desk and the staff at the desk were so rude and unprofessional i walked out. as healthcare workers are jobs put us at risk for many things but we know that going into the medical field. if the front desk staff are going to be as crazy as the general public about viruses then maybe they should work elsewhere. my primary care doctor is karen brown, she is all the medical director of nemg outpatient offices. i will be sure to let her know about my experience at my next routine visit to her.

there not enough words to describe how happy i am with the work salma has done to my face. not sure if it's my hormones, wearing masks all day at the dental office , stress, etc , but my skin on my in the last 2 years started break out bad. my friend of 25 years said she has never seen my face like this. i went to the dermatologist and the doctor told me to buy an over the counter face wash . that didn't work. then, i decided to try this place . wow! i got a micro dermabrasion facial. the extractions are not fun but i tell myself remember the end affect. she then place this type of tens unit , which i think kills the bacteria. she gave me suggestions to home facial care. i am on my 2nd visit. even after the first visit , i noticed less bumps, scarring, and acne forming. i have referred many of my friends here.
i have had facials ( not microdermabrasion ) in los gatos, palo alto and willow glen. this one is worth the drive to fremont for me. amazing.

i've been a client of verde touch for over 4 years and originally found them serendipitously through a simple search on yelp when i was pregnant. verde happened to be very close to my home and i decided to give them a try. they've been a key part of my wellness practice and i'm grateful to david and his wonderful staff for keeping me relaxed, grounded and healthy throughout the years so i can simply be a better human :). they've revitalized me through ongoing massage during my pregnancy and well after, healed me through a horrible car accident and continues to surprise me with their craft approach to the art of massage. 

i value my well-being especially living in silicon valley where it's hectic and frequent many spas around the world.  nothing compares to verde when it comes to a nurturing, intentional, unpretentious and integrated massage experience.

here's my recap: 

massage - david is an exceptionally talented therapist himself while also spending many hours training each and every therapist 1 on 1 for quality and consistency. he allows each to infuse their own personality into their practice. i've seen a handful of therapist each with their own style with the signature 'verde touch' in mind. you really enter a state of bliss and ultimate relaxation. the tables are comfy and linens soft. 

for individual/couples massages are equally amazing (many options/promotions to find the right fit.

for prenatal - amazing recess belly and breast holes in the  table so you can lay face down and supported.

staff - david, the owner and heather, the ops manager are first class. in 4 years as a client, i don't think i've ever not received a confirmation email, text or some form of communication.  if there are any cancellations, there's always a contingency (ie new date or therapist proposed). their customer service is next level. it's exciting to see verde's success is creating more demand and increased hiring of diverse and talented massage therapists.

experience
where do i start? ok here goes...

ambiance - minimal, inviting, intimate, unassuming. i love it. there's a natural, deeply fragrant smell of the handmade, organic salve made in house, minimal greenery, plush furniture and wood accents that create a warm atmosphere. 

water - reverse osmosis citrus water is clean, pure, refreshing and sooo delicious.

organic massage salve - is used during the massage and infused with quality, young living essential oils of your choice (or my favorite, therapists choice).  i've used it as a hair mask, moisturize my toddler's skin, moisturize my lips and a plethora of other usages. it's made of organic coconut oil and beeswax and verde magic. they sell it and i have a tub laying around everywhere -  car, bedside, work.

location - los altos (cozy corner nook and upstairs location), hotel los gatos, and soon, downtown palo alto yay!. great locations and all unique in their own way and very accessible.

berries! yes, raspberries, every single time, there for you to enjoy. i munch on them often :)

automated booking app - lifesaver. i always forget to schedule and with the app, you can pre book immediately or even find sessions last minute. it's been wonderful for not only myself but for my friends and family (i.e. family coming from out of town). the ease of scheduling is amazing.

cost - reasonable considering all the personal care verde puts into supporting your well-being. there are so many promotions as well (birthday, try new therapists, etc).

david know's how to run a business so verde will always take care of you. 

hope you enjoy as much as i have - i think most of my friends are now verde believers :) to your wellness.

i brought my mother here for severe pain one afternoon as the doctors office was closed for the weekend and we didn't want to spend a whole day at the er.

after we paid the exorbitant fee, we waited 2+ hours in the waiting room which was now packed with people coughing & sneezing with zero available hand sanitizer, tissues or masks (which all of the foh staff were wearing, as if this was chernobyl.) one chair was even covered in dry blood, which should've been the first sign to hightail it out of there.

finally we get called in and go through the routine questions. as we wait for the doctor, michael vincent, i overhear him and the nurse discussing my mothers symptoms out in the open and practically diagnosing it as a lost cause... how *very* professional. he walks in with an irritated attitude and before he even asks us anything or examines my mother, he sharply tells us that there's nothing he can do. as i start to explain the situation, he practically cuts me off and screams at us, like children, that we should've just went to the er. then he begrudgingly checks her vitals, as he is still shaking his head and basically scolding me for bringing her there.

meanwhile, my mother, a legal immigrant and senior citizen, is now not only in the pain she came in with but also embarrassed and uncomfortable. thank you for that, dr. vincent. not sure if his dismissive demeanor is his normal or if he just had a particular problem with the color of our skin (or perhaps having to wait a second for me to translate to my mother) but it was incredibly inappropriate and unethical.

then, as we were leaving, they make me wait an additional 40 minutes for discharge papers and have the audacity to ask me to sign an ama form "because you're leaving against doctors advice." his "advice" was to go to the er, which we intended to do. so this was yet another sign of the shady ways in which this establishment operates. i did not sign it and went to the er, who promptly gave my mother the pain meds she needed, without any issue or discrimination, and we were on our way. something so minuscule and yet, so hard that this urgent care couldn't handle. let alone with care.

with a market as competitive as private urgent care centers, you would think that a manager or owner would care to respond or immediately return missed phone calls but that's also not the case here as it seems their manager is there only 8 hours a week and, conveniently, none of those are when you call.

drive an extra 5 minutes and spare yourself and your loved ones from a waste of time & money (and exposure to another illness in this waiting room) at this dumpster-fire of a place and go to literally any other urgent care or er that'll at least treat you with an ounce of respect.

i there at the end of january with high fever and severe cough.  masks were not available. no one asked if i traveled outside of us. i just came back from germany. it took 1 hour to check me in with full waiting room of people. i stood up and told them that this is very irresponsible due to the coronavirus. they laughed at me. i do not think that this was responsible urgent care.

i am so disappointed in the service and quality of assistance received when i switched insurance companies and needed to be reauthorized for my gammagard infusions.   the one person who had seemed competent was out of the office so for two weeks i got the runaround from at least 6 other people.  not one of them seemed to know what they were doing or talking about.   they would not let me speak to a supervisor but instead kept transferring me to people who had no idea why i was connected to them.  all told, i spent at least 5-6 hours on the phone over a 3 day period and still did not successfully solve the problems i was having in receiving authorizing and obtaining a medication shipment.   of course it comes at a critical time as i have a compromised immune system and the coronavirus is spreading (and my son is arriving from italy tomorrow to be home quarantined).    as soon as i can i will transfer to another infusion provider even though i like my nurse.

it seems like entertainment and costumer experience are their first priority. maybe more than anything else.

riverside staff is not friendly, both offices are somewhat - - scary. they want to give your kids some kind of experience, but to my kids (and me) it just brought fear, my daughter was terrified. in their offices you find lightening, forest sound effects (riverside), a skull dressed in a tuxedo, digital fireplace with sound and potions (redlands); it's like you're in a harry potter film set. dr. watson dresses in renaissance costume. some may find this amusing, i find it weird and eccentric.

one time i went, the nurse who took my baby's vitals was smelling cigarette. the same nurse later on gave my baby an oral vaccine while he was asleep and he chocked. became blue, and all. everyone got worried, dr. watson called me personally to apologize and follow up.

i gave it two stars only because dr. watson is very worried about customer appreciation of his practice (you'll notice the effort in the offices' decor and how he responds to a lot of the reviews posted here); and when my son was circumcised he did take the time to sit and talk to me. that went okay, in despite of him not wearing a mask during the procedure and didn't stop talking to me or the nurse while on top of - what it was supposed to be - a sterile camp (i'm a nurse). i could actually see his spit falling over it, and just hoped for the best.

booked on zocdoc for dr.shapiro. but turns out i met with a pa?? i was not notified prior or informed during my visit that i was not meeting with who i spent time looking at reviews and recommendations for! 

the pa, john i believe his name was saw me literally for two minutes. took a glimpse at the issue and said he'll prescribe something for it. absolutely no explanation, no questions to assess my condition. he stayed so far away from me like i had the coronavirus! now my prescription is wrong and the pharmacy only received one of the two!! 

the staff is also super unfriendly! my gps led me to a parking lot. so i called them and someone from brooklyn picked up. she just said it should be there. that's the address. she's never been there so can't tell me more. i asked if she can transfer me to the forest hills location and she said no!

terrible experience today. i saw a black female provider and she was the least empathetic, uncaring medical provider i've ever encountered. she genuinely acted mad i was there and told me no fewer than three times i shouldn't have come and it was her front desk staffs fault i was allowed in the door. she raised her voice and yelled at me, threw down her paperwork in frustration, argued with me, bad mouthed her staff, and let out these exasperated sighs. i came in for fever, difficulty breathing, painful ear with echoing, and persistent hacking cough. she then determined i needed a covid year but couldn't provide one. she told me to go home, and i told her i'm required to go to work, and she said i can't go against the cdc. well i'm navy, so without a note i can't stay home to self quarantine. she said they don't have covid tests and said to call 211 or go to the er. then she came back and said the er doesn't have covid tests and she'd tell me the number to call, which she didn't. i asked her for help with my ear which angered her and she yelled that i shouldn't even be there. so now i have no pain relief for my ear, no diagnosis, no work note, no quarantine paperwork for work, no idea how or where to get help, still am coughing, still can't breathe without coughing..... absolutely terrible experience.

i've had such a hard time finding a good chiropractor after my regular one retired.  i've tried at least a dozen over the past 10 years. dr dave is one of the best i've ever been to.  he is very knowledgeable and is eager to give you advise about your whole health.  there are no contracts or plans; just a flat fair treatment cost.  dave recently sent an email to his patients about some natural supplements that may help prevent you from contracting the corona virus.  he doesn't sell any of it but will recommend a site where you can find good quality products.  he's very thoughtful and caring and takes the time to get to know his patients and to figure out how to best treat them. i'm so glad i found him.

in the midst of corona virus, this is the only indoor place i will take my kiddos! we have been here so many times and never gotten sick. i saw the girl who works at the front desk clean the play food and wipe down surfaces multiple times. my kids also take great naps after because of all the fun things to do and stimulation. it's great!

i was extremely frustrated and felt very disrespected after my visit today to medexpress in jenison. the majority of my visit was great, the nurse and physician treated me kindly and diagnosed my symptoms. however, the front desk lady was extremely rude and treated me badly all because i traveled to spain. she made comments about me and in-front of me to her coworkers. comments such as "well looks like she gets to stay" (she was not happy they didn't turn me away because i traveled internationally) and "looks like we need hazmat suits". i felt bad enough for going in today but have been dealing with a sore throat (turned out to be uvulitis). she made me feel like i did something wrong and that i should be ashamed. really felt disrespected after hearing the comments she made about me. would not recommend going to medexpress in jenison right night if you have traveled internationally recently or if you have any symptoms that may be similar to the corona virus.

eeesh... so sad to have to downgrade their review. came in at 9am on a wednesday and still not called back for a simple mask fitting an hour later. not very friendly people this time around. i really wish they could talk their employees into smiling and eye contact once in a blue moon!

the healthcare providers here are nice enough but management-wise there is room for improvement. similar to another review here, after my physical last year i received notice that my tests -- which i hadn't completed -- came back normal. in addition, while the front/back office is computerized, the patient charts are not. some of the physician's assistants spend more time than others making sure they review what other pas/doctors have documented in the chart. 

there's truth to the saying "nobody knows your body like you do". all these years, even though i have asthma, i have kept myself out of the hospital. although i have been a patient at this practice nearly a year, it has taken me some time to adapt to the presence of so many physician's assistants, which at times has made it feel like i'm reinventing the wheel (especially when they don't spend enough time reviewing the chart before the visit begins). 

in general, i do wish there was more effort to accommodate patients with chronic conditions and/or disabilities who simply want to manage them proactively. as an example, i attempted after the 7.2 earthquake in july last year to put together an emergency kit -- which for where i live is supposed to consist of a month's worth of food, water, supplies and medications -- but i had trouble stocking it with my medications because there's no allowance for this. worse, my spouse and i have hit some major car trouble over the past year and since we live in a rural area without bus service (or even semi-affordable uber) there have been times i do not have transportation. the other problem is that this office has a strict policy of seeing the patient for medication refills vs. treatment. a typical situation is that my refill appointment is already scheduled so when i come down sick i have to choose between medication and treatment.

i have been told that my only option in such situations is a secondary office visit -- even if i've been in recently and/or don't have access to transportation. this is frustrating because prior to moving to this area my former primary care physician of over 20 years worked with me, not against me, in extenuating circumstances. i want to continue my track record of managing my asthma well enough, even through flu season, to remain out of the hospital. sadly, i feel that effort is not accommodated -- chiefly because this office does not allow for remote (phone/video) consultation. (if you're lucky, a nurse will call you back. if you're not, it's possible to leave multiple messages and/or for your calls to go straight to voicemail even during normal business hours.)

it is one thing to expect patients to show up regularly for care -- which is reasonable -- another to mandate that all patients, regardless of health risks, even in flu season, make what amounts to revolving-door use of the (sick) patient waiting room. given recent news of a public health emergency, my concern is that allowing patient calls to reach a voicemail system, where their best efforts to leave a message may go unreturned, will open up this practice to seeing patients who should have been evaluated, at least on a preliminary basis, by phone. instead, it is my impression that the office doesn't really track why the patient has scheduled an appointment. cdc guidelines in dealing with the emerging coronavirus threat, as an example, recommends that medical providers ask patients to "call ahead" to prepare for their arrival (to limit exposure to staff and other patients). if patient calls are unreturned, the staff doesn't note why the patient has made an appointment and there is no phone consultation option, staff may eventually be forced by the cdc to take time off work to self-quarantine thanks to reflexively advising patients to simply show up for an office visit regardless of the reason for their visit.

while i sympathize that doctor's offices are already subjected to more calls than they care to take, that doesn't mean patients who have successfully managed chronic health conditions for many years should be held to a rigid policy aimed at compelling every patient, regardless of health status or extenuating circumstance, to show up as per usual -- even in the midst of a county/state emergency declaration. during a recent period without my car -- spouse's car was at the dealer for more than a month for an airbag recall and an unrelated repair -- i was more than willing to schedule a follow up visit but had no way to get there. my requests for a callback kept going to voicemail until i got high desert medical group to connect me to the front office. when i explained my circumstances, i expected to be connected to a nurse. instead i was told that there was nothing that would be done unless i scheduled a second in-person visit. my pleas for a reasonable accommodation were flatly denied. this left me feeling patronized and confused. nobody ought to feel like that when seeking health "care".

dr robert krage, dc

interview
i fell for the full-page ad in the desert sun last january 2019. although i thought dcs should stick to spinal care, but here was a dc who seemed able to treat foot problems.  i have had morton's neuromas for 8 years, treated with alcohol injections which reduced them somewhat, but they still bothered me. dr. krage's initial consultation is like a pep rally to motivate one to "qualify" for his treatment plan based on willingness to follow through with the plan and reap the huge benefits - much like a timeshare presentation. he also videos your walking on a treadmill and tells you that you are doing it wrong and that is why you have 'hammer toes', which sounded dubious to me. still, i wanted to believe that he could help my discomfort so i continued. one of the tests he performed was to dig his thumb into the bottom of my heel until i yelled in pain. that, he said, was "plantar fasciitis".  really?? that was the only time i ever had pain in my heel!! the 2nd consultation requires the spouse or significant other to attend, presumably to acknowledge joint willingness to pay the high cash fee up front without dissent.   the contract he presents starts at over $15,000 but - of course - he mentions "discounts" (for no apparent reason) which brings it down to $7,000.  when $15,000 would be an "absolutely not!" answer, agreeing to $7,000 is not quite so bitter to swallow - with a big dose of hope!

treatments:
all treatments, whether laser for feet or backs, or stretching for those with spinal problems - are done by the hardworking, organized and caring 2 office attendants at a satellite office on fred waring in palm desert. (his main office is in corona.) for me these included lasers directed to the soles of my feet and strong percussion treatments before or after, 3 times per week for 32 sessions.  dr krage did just a few foot percussion treatments and took molds for the expensive, high quality orthotics that were made to order. otherwise i rarely saw him other than to say 'hello'.
when the 1st set of orthotics arrived i tried to use them in my shoes for the 2 hour periods, but could not sustain the daily schedule due to the discomfort. i never got to the 4 hour or 6 hour daily sessions, and never picked up my 2nd custom set of orthotics -- which were supposed to be even more severe in pushing up my metatarsal arches.

results:
i can't attest to how laser treatments may or may not have helped the other patients in this office, most of whom received the treatments on their lumbar backs, but for my morton's neuromas, i found no benefit whatsoever. i regret ever being so optimistic that dr krage's  full-page splashy ad convinced me that an amazing new treatment would do more for the painful lumps in the balls of my feet than my podiatrist could do.   if i had researched yelp.com sooner, and searched for his san diego connection to a similar treatment claim in another krage office in previous years. i would have run the other way.
even recently in the coachella valley, dr krage was fined for "false advertising" in 2014.  at $7000 per patient, a $300 fine is easy to pay!  https://search.dca.ca.gov/details/8500/dc/24734/7cfefa3ed5e1338723892475e4bcfe7d 
dr krage does not take any insurance as payments -- most likely, because his treatments are not approved by any medical or government authority. i completely wasted $7000, plus a lot of time.
 
also, robert krage dc may be related to john krage dc of san diego since robert is linked to a san diego chiropractic office years ago on the internet. 
the following is noteworthy from the california board of chiropractors webpage of professional violations.
krage, john-san diego dc 14672 12/30/2013     gross negligence; repeated negligence acts; false advertising; excessive treatment; dishonesty; use of laser for purposes other than those approved by the us food and drug administration (fda)  https://www.chiro.ca.gov/about_us/summer_2014.pdf

and decades ago there was another john krage in san diego with the same ads and the same "happy feet" logo. that dc is retired or deceased but is probably the father with 2 sons who followed his  business model.

review:
on 2/17/20 i had the unfortunate privilege in bringing my dad to this er.  his car broke down near spartan stadium, so he decided to walk to his home, 4+ miles away (nearly 80 years young).  when he was less than a block from home, he decided to rest on the curb but fell forward and hit his forehead on the cement. he made it home and that's when my mother called detailing his incident.  at 5:00 i left my home in tracy and arrived in san jose just 1 hour later.  we got to the er by 6:15p, where the staff immediately took us back to take my father's vitals, ekg and schedule a ct scan. all was quick until it came to the scan.  it took almost another hour before he was called for the scan.  after the scan, we were told to wait in the hallway for an xray.  well two hours later we were asked what we were waiting for after i had asked a nurse on the status of the xray tech is, as we have been waiting.  he came back 30 min later and said my dad did not meed an xray and walked us to the front where a nurse asked what he has had done so far.  them she said, ok wait n the waiting room and we'll call you when the dr. is available.  now 10p and they finally called us back.  doc said all looks good but he'll need stitches (really!).  11:45p all stitched up and good to go!  almost 6 hours of mass hysteria with zero communication from staff who appear to be very disorganized when shuffling patients around!  i can only imagine how many sick elderly re being left in hallways laying in gurneys until someone remembers them! i saw a few of them last night.  
ways to improve:
1).  separate those with viruses into a different area than those with other emergencies.   this is what ucsf does.  goes quickly.  

2).  communication is key!!! keep the patient up to speed every step of the way.  we understand your busy but remember that the patient is already in some sort of discomfort and shouldn't be worrying if they have been overlooked!

attentive, patient and caring, i felt like a patient instead of a number here. i came in with a high temperature and a severe cough and with all the scares of corona virus, i was concerned.  however doctor yang eased my fears and helped me make an appointment as soon as possible. after the appointment, i left feeling safe and confident now that i had all worries addressed.

i was able to schedule an appointment for the next day. the staff were professional, prompt, and thorough. 
tests for strep and flu were taken and the results were given to me in a few minutes. 

i received advice on how to deal with the virus that was causing my cough and sore throat. 

glad that i made the appointment.

i'm torn between five stars and one star, so i felt that two was sufficient for my wife's experience. i'm a proud father of a new baby girl who came into this world over one month early!! 

the labor & delivery staff were great except when it came to having my wife's food delivered. at first i thought it was the dietary staff but i later learned that the food trays are left at the nursing station. why? i have no idea but i can tell you that the trays sit for at least a minimum of one hour before the trays are delivered. i'm sure it's not the nursing staff's job to deliver food but why continue this practice if it's a problem?? 

as i mentioned before the staff are great when it comes to patient care but this one little detail of not delivering a pregnant patient's food is truly a horrible practice!! what makes it the absolute worst is that my wife spent one week at the hospital dealing with a difficult labor and now she has to eat cold food that has been sitting out for over an hour... 

after being transferred to the postpartum unit, it was extremely noticeable how much more attentive and helpful the staff is. everyone from the nurses to the unit secretary were beyond helpful. the dietary staff delivered breakfast, lunch and dinner to the room every single day!! the few days spent there were great!! the young man who conducted the hearing test was very professional and handled our baby with such care. i don't know his name but he definitely deserves recognition!! 

overall, our experience was good up until we were discharged... as we were being transported out we passed the security staff. there were three black male guards hanging out at the desk in the er lobby area. as my wife was being rolled out on a wheelchair one guard shouts out "what did you have"? i nicely replied "we had a baby girl" and i smiled because it's our first child and had been trying to have a baby for several years. as we reach the automated doors the guard yells out "good luck" in a sarcastic manner! 

this is exactly what i needed after spending an entire week in the hospital watching my wife struggle with a difficult birth, every meal being served cold and possibly bordering on bacteria contamination; all to be topped off with some contract security guard expressing his personal feelings on how he feels about having a baby girl. this is what you have to look forward if you're a patient here!!

i remember when this health center was run by the sister of charity of leavenworth. it was as professional as you could ever expect but for whatever reason it has lowered its values and you'll probably get a similar experience or worse!!

allied security is the contract company providing your sarcasm and er hangouts. i was informed that it's managed by the dietary department, not even sure how that makes sense?? when i inquired i was also told the dietary department also manages the valet parking operations. maybe it's downsizing at its best or worst??

i do want to thank;

marcel loh - chief executive
paul makarewicz - director - mission
carol o'dea, administrative director - quality and patient safety 

for not doing your jobs and especially for allowing these experiences!!

i was seen by a doctor named sameh, sawires, md for  complaints of sore throat, green thick mucus, cold, body aches, fatigue. after being assessed by this doctor i was told that i have a virus and no treatment was indicated and i should follow up with my pcp. i asked for antibiotics (azithromycin) because bacterial and viral colds tend to have the same symptoms and i would prefer to treat it then have these symptoms linger for days. he refused and told me again to follow up with my pcp. in the past whenever i have a cold that progressed to body aches, fatigue and green mucus i'm treated with an antibiotic and these symptoms go away within a day or so after starting antibiotics. it's unfair to pay a $50 co-pay for service and treatment and not be given the treatment i requested given that bacterial and viral colds have the same symptoms. don't go there if this doctor is on duty!

my husband has been a patient at mj several times. the first time, mj was an independent facility. therapists and nursing staff were both wonderful; efficient, well-trained and competent, very caring, and seemingly happy in their positions. in 2018 northwestern bought the facility. the facility has become very "corporate." while the therapy is still top-notch, the staff has taken on a different attitude toward their patients and their jobs. they are no longer caring and friendly; those traits enhance the patient and family experience and speed the healing process - lack of those traits make the patient want to get out of there before they are actually ready. the nursing staff, particularly the night shift, are "businesslike" to the point of being rude. the medical staff is also poor, at best, in communicating with patients and family and seem incompetent in following the discharge orders of the hospital from which the patient came, even to the point of simply ignoring the medication orders without informing the ordering physician or the patient/family. 
i am so disappointed that a superior facility like marianjoy would "sell out" to the corporate world which is taking over so much of medicine today. i would still return to mj strictly for the therapy, but i am certainly not happy about the new atmosphere and i honestly don't know if i would blanketly recommend the facility as i once did. 
i find that outpatient therapy at a dupage medical group facility is as good if the patient is capable of doing op therapy.
of course, there are still several staff members who maintain the old fashioned bedside manner and at least try to go above and beyond in patient care, but even those seem to be "afraid of breaking corporate protocol."

i have been using this practice for 10 years now. because i am pre-diabetic i see dr. calder on a yearly basis to check for diabetic retinopathy.  i also had west nile virus in 2018 with encephalitis that caused pressure on the retina of my right eye. i was seeing white blood cell floaters in my right eye for 3 months. i was followed closely by dr. bronner to resolve this issue. i visited dr. horst last week to be fitted for variable focal contact lenses. the contact lens in my left eye was bothering me and i called today. even though dr. horst was on vacation, they gave me an appointment with dr. pierce this afternoon. he wanted to be sure i did not have a corneal infection.  it turns out the soft contact lens had some fibers imbedded in the lens and this was causing the irritation. they gave me a new lens and now the irritation is gone. having seen many of the physicians and optometrist, i highly recommend this team. they have a comprehensive team to help with all eye care problems.

this is a terrible a place.  you see a doctor via video.

basically it's a blood draw lab (think quest labs) with a "doctor" front end to authorize tests.  you go in, there's no receptionist, there is no patient intake.  one door is for the lab where they process blood samples.  behind a sliding door on the other side of the office is where you see the doctor, via video!  there is no active reception or intake. there is only one person seeing patients- an ma or nurse.  we  arrived and after about 20 min. she came out from beyond the thin sliding door (where we could overhear parts of her conversation with another patient) and seemed surprised to see us, despite our having made an appointment.   

so finally we go in, and she says, "hang on let me wipe everything down...."   it's just a drab office with carpet and cloth arm chairs.  ew.  big tv on the wall.  she donned her mask and we started talking.

they don't take medicare, we found out there- so don't take older folks there.  probably don't take medical either.  this is not stated on their cool looking website.  it's $100 out of pocket to "see" a doctor.  and during this time of global pandemic, who is this doctor?  makes you think of that old joke, "what do you call a medical student who graduated last in his class...?"  the ma/nurse showed me on her phone a photo of their price list that seemed to be handwritten.  really class act.

this is a place where capitalism and health care conspire to create this awful, substandard place for "care."  not to mention that sick people are coming in and out of en effin' safeway.  and to be sure, the ma/nurse was doing her best, so i don't blame her in the least.  

this model should be outlawed.  #medicare4all

i've been a patient here for years. the doctors i saw were always reason enough for me to stick around, through some very serious medical problems i've had going on for the last several years. that's how much i liked the doctors i saw. i was willing to put up with always waiting past my appointment time because they were behind schedule. i was willing to deal with the incompetent front office staff who change on what seems to be a monthly basis. i guess they can't keep employees. i even stayed when they literally stopped answering phone calls and started doing all communication through their messaging app. that right there is one of the most frustrating things about this place. do you know how hard it is to get anything resolved or addressed when you can't physically speak to someone and instead have to wait hours or days in between messages, usually from someone different than whoever sent the previous message. it took months to get a bill sorted out for an appointment i rescheduled but that they forgot to change in their system, resulting in a no show fee.

now though, i'm pretty much through with them. i have several chronic conditions and knowing this, my job suggested i get a doctors note that would allow me to work from home during the ongoing coronavirus outbreak. i sent the office a message and first i was told i had to schedule a virtual consult, which costs money by the way, just to get this note. i questioned this and then i was told, by someone else who also isn't my actual doctor, that my chart was reviewed and i would have to come in for an appointment since it had been 6 months since my last appointment, and because they hadn't performed the apparently very essential annual physical and routine bloodwork. i was there in the office 6 months ago. whose fault is it that the "annual" testing and exam wasn't done? and the reason i haven't yet scheduled my 6 month follow up visit is because i want to avoid concentrations of sick people during this outbreak.

so in essence, they claim in order to provide a note simply stating that i have chronic health conditions and should work from home, as suggested by my boss herself, first i need to come into a cramped office full of sick people, risk exposure to the same virus i'm trying to avoid, and have routine bloodwork done. and of course this conversation is occurring via glorified text messages. needless to say, the great doctors here are no longer enough to convince me to stay with this practice.

review:
https://wharflifedc.com/glo30-at-wharf-dc-for-a-fresher-cleaner-face/

go to shahin! a year with her has transformed my skin.

facials are a level of self care that i had never taken seriously before i lived at the wharf dc. living aboard a boat means i am outside most of the day. (hello, sunshine!) living in dc means i walk everywhere and the grit of the city ends up on my face. (hello, city life!) 

glo 30welcome to glo30, a boutique right here at the wharf offering all the products we are looking for to care for our skin these days - clean, exfoliate, tone, hydrate, and protect. we've all heard that we need to take care of our skin, and perhaps you buy your skin products online without much thought, like i did. glo30 offers a line of skin care products to match your skin's needs. 

i first stopped into glo30 looking for sunscreens without oxybenzone since my sunscreen had run out. i found sunscreen and was surprised by how much more they offer. their products have a unique combination of anti-aging antioxidants, an effective sunblock and a replenishing moisturizer!  the staff at glo30 are easy to chat with and gave no pressure to buy or sign up for anything, but i did pick up a brochure and asked about their facials.  

after chatting with the staff, i convinced myself to sign up for a monthly facial membership. there are three levels of membership to choose glo30from, but my favorite is the freshglo membership.  at $79 per month, it's more than fair for an hour long session of treatments including an upper body massage with a bonus of 10% off all products in the store. it's easy to book your session in the store or online, and a massage of your neck, face, arms, and hands as well as multiple skin treatments designed just for you after they analyze and photograph your skin, are absolutely delicious.

glo30after each session, my skin really does feel refreshed and rejuvenated. treatments here range from feeling like a light mask you might put on at home, through microdermabrasion, which is like a tiny tiny sander, a mildly abrasive instrument the technician uses to gently sand your skin, removing any uneven outer layers. it's used for reducing the appearance of scars, or freckles and dark spots. depending upon what your skin needs, they might use chemical peels or light therapy as well as masks with medical-grade ingredients to reduce wrinkles, boost vitamins, and volumize through hydration. i never ever thought i'd want any of this, but our life here in dc is busier, and dirtier than i could have imagined. a facial has become part of my monthly routine for health and wellness.

a friend of mine suggested this place as she's been a customer for about a few years now. i learned about the monthly subscription and figured i would give it a try since it's a different facial every month. 

background - i never got facials from a professional  before but always tried home remedies and face masks. i have t zones and very old acne scars. i started the subscription  in the fall and my acne scars have gotten lighter and my skin tone is more even. it's made the biggest difference  of my life! 

my go to lady shahin also suggested a humidifier and one of the best scrubs. she's super knowledgeable and the one hour spent at glo30 goes by way too fast. i wish it was longer! oh and one of my favorite things is that they switch up the treatment every month based on the weather or how you're  skin is. 

highly recommend this place and you can cancel the subscription anytime which is a win win.

my mom was who went to an appointment. she questioned the hygiene of the assistant using only 1 1" by 2" wipe and with a lackadaisical effort to wipe all the equipment. the doctor then questioned what was the best method and cleaners to use. umm dude you are supposed to be the professional here. this lowers one's sense security at the time of the corona virus issue. shouldn't there be updates in they hygiene and husbandry of the equipment. 
at the end of the appointment with her eyes dilated she was not issued or suggested to ask about some form of shade on the eyes. for crying out loud she arrived alone and addressed the issue of having to drive home. regular glasses will definitely not do the the trick and has to go back to ask for a set.

avoid like the plague!
