the waiting room is very open so you don't have to sit next to people if you don't want to. the 2 different receptionist i encountered were very friendly. they had mask available, lollipop, hand sanitizer and water. the tv was set to a kids movie which was great because i had kids with me for both visits. the waiting room was very clean however, i would say it was pretty warm in the waiting room compared to the back area.

once we were taken into the back. all vital signs were taken and the nurse was very friendly making sure to get all the information before the doctor came in to see us that's all i'll wait time was about 10 minutes. we were able to see the doctor, he was able to give directions about what needed to be done. then we were given discharge papers and we are out the door.

at check out i was given the option to pay my deductible or to wait to be billed which was kind of nice. especially when you're feeling sick and you can't concentrate or make a decision. all in all everyone was very friendly the facility was very clean and i would recommend this location to anyone that was feeling under the weather. adults or children.

i knew i had a sinus infection and wanted to be seen by a doctor by monday.
i arrived at carenow on rainbow and warm springs with my magazine knowing i had to probably wait awhile and tissues in hand.
the facility was very clean and and the front desk was very welcoming and customer service oriented.
although the wait was long, everyone had their masks to not cough or breath on each other and there was enough room to not have to sit next to each other.  they also had a movie on to watch.
the nurse and doctor were also professional and did spend the time needed to get your vitals, talk to you about your illness.  there was no sense of a rush to get you out.  
the staff were all truly happy, again high customer service oriented and it also helped that the tunes they were playing rocked the place.
good job carenow!

i gave one star because i couldn't give fewer. this company is far from dependable. they send the wrong orders, drop calls and that's if you can even get someone to answer. i have found that i can find most of what i want/need on amazon and then submit the bill to insurance for reimbursement. it sounds like extra work, but the reality is that i spend less time ordering there than i do just calling and hoping for an answer at preferred. plus i am not frustrated at all like i am when i deal with this understaffed/untrained company.

this outstanding service was a savior! 
i came down with a nasty cold in january and after 2 weeks of coughing and blowing my nose to the point of bleeding i called them for the first time -- the doctor who saw me was thorough and set my mind at ease - after the consult, which included taking my vitals by a an accompanying medical assistant,  i was instructed to just keep doing what i was doing. 

then in early february my husband came home with the flu  -  very sudden onset - had them come out again to see him given the coughing and fever - didn't think it was prudent to go to a doctors office like that and two days after his visit i was deep in the throes of high fever and all the  nasty symptoms the flu comes with -- so i called upon them yet again and we were both prescribed tamiflu and told to continue our self-imposed quarantine and palliative stuff until we had one 24-hour period without fever or the help of analgesics for said fever. 

the three doctors we saw in those three visits were all great -- most especially dr. robert kakehashi, who saw us last. the medical assistant that accompanied dr. kakehashi was excellent as well.

when i received my first eob i realized had made an insurance mistake and called them so they could please bill medicare first for my two visits - they were very helpful  and accommodating and since then my error has been corrected. 

i will definitely continue using this outstanding service when necessary -- it's a definite plus to be able to be seen by a doctor in the comfort of your home - especially with all the stuff going on now with the covid-19 and the flu and also if you're feeling so under the weather that driving is not an option or a dangerous one. this is also a much more prudent option than going to a doctor's office and possibly shedding virus on everyone there or being around other possibly contagious sick people yourself. plus the peace of mind of knowing you can get a doctor to see you the same day or the next day. you're offered many options by heal. all the medical professionals we saw arrived on time during the 2-hour window that we were given when we set up the appointment.
  
i definitely recommend this service! congratulations for a wonderful alternative in healthcare.

besides the food being awesome, there customer service is top-notch!  i've needed assistance 3 times now when ordering, and within minutes they respond and go out of their way to help me.  ordering from them had helped make my hectic days do-able in more ways than one.  may god continue to bless your business and the people you serve!

review:
rushed my mother to williamson medical at 1 am this morning hoping to get relief from the writhing pain she was experiencing related to bladder cancer. despite having only one other patient, the er team was cold, harsh, thoughtless and entirely lacking in empathy. they were also mistaken in key parts of their diagnosis and their treatment. 

based on my experience today, i would never send a relative or a friend to williamson medical under any circumstance imaginable. 

why do these "healthcare professionals" feel they are serving their patients if they allow interminable delays (we were left for 2 hours without getting pain medication of any kind - the very reason we went in the first place) and brutish bedside manners (being moved from bed to gurney like a sack of potatoes, my mother getting screamed at during insertion of a catheter, blaming the patient for difficulty finding a vein {it took 3 tries and 3 pokes} in which to insert an iv, etc.).  10-minutes into the nurse screaming catheter insertion i heard the head nurse, amy, finally ask my mother what her name was. think about that. 

i found medical trash strewn all over the room we were in. this is 3rd world treatment and 3rd world quality care. 

i have great reverence for those who commit their lives to the serving and healing of strangers. i revere and feel hfriends who are er doctors, social workers, cancer scientists. these people serve mankind and they have empathy somehow baked into their dna. the er team at williamson medical should seriously consider why they chose to serve the public. i wouldn't hire any of the nurses or the doctor we dealt with to deliver my mail - they'd find a way to screw it up. they might, however, be just right to pick up our trash curbside.

to be fair, i should note we had generally positive experiences from the er check-in staff. also had acceptable treatment and care after getting my mother checked into the main hospital. but by the time we were upstairs, we had lost faith in the entire place, so we were watching/prodding them closely to be sure they attended properly to our mom. no one should need to do that. 

later in the day i spoke to an emt who said he wouldn't allow his friends or family to get taken to williamson medical er, that they have an awful reputation as a dumping ground for patients who have no advocacy and no close family oversight. his quote was "tell them to take you farther north to vandy, st. thomas etc. ". he also said, "even if you arrive at williamson medical without an infection, you'll surely leave with one". yikes.  wish i'd known. that's why i've labored over this review. beware. 

and my heart goes out to anyone reading this who has a loved one suffering like my mother has. god bless.

before i share my personal experience (publicly), i wanted to express a heartfelt thank you to dr. t and staff. while i think it is imperative to provide feedback to a business regarding long wait time, i also feel it is worth noting and i stand strong to my beliefs that patience is so critical. if you feel you have found the right and noteworthy surgeon (not just a doctor) who you have confidence in giving you the ultimate results and capitalizing on time, the surgeon should be worth your money and time spent. i had initially heard of dr. taneja from a friend and i gave him a chance. after receiving 2 other consults from (also) noteworthy surgeons, i knew he was my guy. 

it's true, you may be experiencing some delays during your consult or your follow up, but it is because he takes his time with patients and really listens to each one. he not only cares for them as individuals, as human beings, but it takes time to develop that trust. so i get it. he gets me. 

to anyone with concerns about waiting, i recommend to get to your appointment on time, maybe smart to add some cushion for after your appointment so you are not feeling rushed trying to get to your next stop. i can assure you, he is the best in his field. 

a huuuuge thank you to each one of you, at mylook, who have taken part in my transformation journey. 

in addition to dr. taneja, i have met with elxy more than once regarding my care and she was always more than happy and willing to chat. about anything - my medical concerns, what's on my mind and heart. on the day of my surgery, nancy was my nurse. and just by the caring and reassuring look in her eyes behind her mask, i was confident she would take care of me while i was awake and asleep. i also got the chance to meet my anesthesiologist on the day of my surgery. he explained the process of how the anesthesia would be administered and the effects to my body. i was always afraid of being half asleep or awake when going under - pretty sure i'm not the only one. he explained it thoroughly and educated me to help me understand and didn't just assume that i knew it all. thankful for that. 

i would be remiss if i didn't mention the rest of the business and clerical staff back stage. little nancy is new to the team, so it seems, but she is very friendly and is attentive to details; with the hundreds of patients that call or visit, she remembered me!

personal experience - dr. taneja is the only other person i would allow to touch my body. he is an expert in his field and has seen hundreds of patients (male and female). why do i trust him? for 21 years i always had concerns about loose skin in my abdominal area, and no matter how much running and exercise i did, it just wouldn't go away. time after time and again and again, i would become my worst critic and over judging my appearance, leading me to become depress with how i looked - through my 20s and 30s. even as a marathoner, it was bothersome, running races with excess weight. i came to dr. t with my concerns and not just once but i came back for my final consult, for self-reassurance because i had fear of going under anesthesia. he reassured me i was the perfect candidate. on my 40th birthday, it was the ultimate gift! with my husband's support, i was able to book my appointment. 

fast forward, i am currently 8 months post op, and i am very happy with my experience, as well as my appearance. i trusted dr. t and staff with my life and i also trusted the process. my only regret is i waited 20 years. i should've done it earlier! 40 looks good on me.

i have been to this hospital several times over the years, in different units, when it was winthrop, during the nyu affiliation years, and recently post-nyu acquisition.  overall, i have had positive experiences.  care, staff, facility, etc.

the following is based on recent visit to the er.

background: busy flu season.  hospital had been on diversion recently.  ip beds full.  er very crowded.  placed in area outside main er.

first, the positives.  these er staff were excellent:

barry zou, rn (triage nurse) - awesome; demeanor, thoroughness
"mo", rn
s. datta, md
grace, rn
christine cirillo, rn
dr. lori katinas, md internist
eugene sullivan, do, gi = no ego; easy to talk with; gave us great ideas, hope
odette thomas, do, hospitalist medicine and her pa laura zaveski. - both so compassionate and patient-centered
n. hussain, do, endocrinology - easy to talk to; listened
tray - environmental/aid - great manner with patients, families, colleagues
firenze b - very understanding
ben, rn

management/professionalism:

felt like there was very little physician or rn oversight or presence in the er. no sense of leadership presence. this erodes patient/family confidence in staff ability to provide appropriate care, competently and timely.  this is heightened by fact that a lot of staff only a few years out of school.  

staff were observed discussing personal issues, staff-staff issues/gossip, other patients, vacation plans, "crazy people", etc.  discussing patients in areas where others (everyone) could hear.

staff need coaching: e.g., christopher d., rn - did not treat patients with respect and dignity (despite patients being challenging); i observed his demeanor with one challenging patient in particular; it is never ok for any staff member to be rude, argumentative, dismissive, and poke fun at a patient - or anyone for that matter; terrible. this rn threatened to withhold meds "next time i won't give it to you." laughing, rn said, "it's almost entertaining...you have to laugh at it" referring to the patient.  another rn had to take over caring for the patient.

lack of attention to patients - hours would go by w/out staff attending to a patient.  what is rounding protocol?

noisy - staff loud and boisterous in late evening and early morning hours - disruptive and not at all conducive to healing 

upon arrival to er check in - rn kelly wore mask but later had it pulled down below chin.  rn in nearby room celebrated he had just seen his "last patient" before his shift ends, but noted unfortunately he had to fill out some sort of paperwork; he held up a folder with a pink sheet of paper

masks - lackadaisical approach by many staff with respect to wearing flu mask - either pulled fully off face or wore half on - below nose.

musical chairs - patients left in chairs (not enough beds); moved several times within the same ancillary/accessory side area: why?

cramped spaces - er berths only as wide as a bed, with flimsy partitions that would not always stay in position.  very little (no) privacy.

providers (resident? and student) - using patient spouse for medical (clinical) translation to get medical history, document symptoms.  staff knew little or no spanish.

while the hospital was extremely busy (flu season), there is never any excuse for staff to act in the ways described.  this behavior is unsafe, provides a poor patient experience, and undercuts the work of team overall.  i encountered many (named above) excellent, caring team members.

i hope this feedback improves care and environment at nyu winthrop.  i want this hospital to thrive in our community.  we have much need for healthcare access.

review:
my husband and i have seen dr. lin for almost 10 years.  we really appreciate his care and upfront honest manner and importantly his knowledge and experience.  last year upon return from a foreign trip, my husband developed harsh cough and fever, friday morning we called his office, no vacancy, but later his staff called and said doctor can see him after hour at 5:30pm.  soon as he listened to my husband's lung and measured his temperature, he immediately gave him a shot for pneumonia, and sent him to take an xray.  later xray result showed clear sign of pneumonia, he saved my husband having to go to er that weekend.
last week we came back from a cruise to hawaii, i suffered symptoms of cough, mild fever, sore throat, running nose, etc.  in the fear of crononavirus, dr. lin agreed to squeezed me in to the after hour appointment at 6:00pm.  i wore mask, gloves everything needed to prevent spreading.  he carefully asked questions and checked my lung, throat, ears, eyes, and legs, then said there is no sign of pneumonia, no worry, just a terrible bad cold virus.  he sent me home with prescriptions of nasal spray, cough syrup, that's all, not even any antibiotics. 

to me, dr. lin is a great doctor, not only because his extensive medical knowledge and experience, but also he really cares about his patients, he    treats you like his old friends/neighbors, he wants you to be well not just treating the illness you come in for, but for an overall living habit.  we always treasure his advice and suggestions.

i came here with a long history of snoring (according to my family), sleepiness during the day, tired, weight gain, and feeling depressed.  my sleep study revealed severe sleep apnea, and i knew myself well enough to know that i would/could not tolerate a cpap mask.  in fact, the reason i came here was because they offered options to cpap.

i was fitted with a dental appliance that made a huge difference in not only how i sleep, but also in how i feel. dr. joe explained what sleep apnea is and how it affects all parts/systems of the body - the brain, the stress hormones, the weight gain, mental fogginess/forgetfulness.  before long, i started "feeling like my old self", better than i had in at least a decade!  i began to have more energy because my body was able to get restorative sleep.  the clouds lifted, my mental clarity improved, and i began losing weight.  with my energy level improved,  i actually felt like exercising again!   my stress hormones went down because i wasn't struggling so hard to breathe in my sleep.  because of the severity of my sleep apnea, i also got a supplemental nasal device called bongo which has been a great complement to my oral device.  my followup sleep study was greatly improved!  i still snore sometimes, but my family says the difference is night and day from how it was before i got treatment.  the best part is no confining mask, no tubes, and no machine.

every single interaction i have had with every single person at sleep medicine group has been professional and courteous.  i cannot think of one negative.  they handled all the insurance for me and there have been no surprises.  

if you snore or are chronically tired, i strongly encourage you to get checked out here.  treating sleep apnea has never been easier.  you do not need a referral - you can refer yourself.  sleep medicine group is state of the art and cutting edge and the pnw is very fortunate to have such a great resource here!

i called dr. helton's office interested in scheduling an appt for a facial.  i was told that melissa was the esthetician and the basic treatment was $100. never was i told this was for 30 minutes only.  i've had numerous facials, all a minimum of 50-60 minutes for the same price with the total treatment, steam , extractions, massage, and a general well being experience.
first of all, melissa, the esthetician,  was sniffling and seemed like she had a cold, no mask or anything to prevent germs as she worked on my skin.  the light was totally bright the entire time,  no soft and soothing music, no dim lighting, and no soothing eye pads were provided when extractions were made.  

she kept asking me if i had an questions, which i had and did ask,and continued to let her know as i had them i would let her know. little did i know this inquiry was because the procedure was soon coming to an end.  i was in disbelief when she told me we were done.  she said her facials were more medically based and therefore the face massage and all the other facets of a traditional massages were not what they provided.  really?  ok but let someone know when they book an appointment that it is only 30 minutes and this is what it includes. 

she did an adequate job on the extractions, but when i pointed out a major bump on my skin that she blatantly missed, she took care of this, but only after i had to bring it to her attention.   in my opinion, a total lack of precision and perfection.   

i was sent to the front desk to pay, and realized i was bleeding from this extraction.  she never bothered to give me anything to contain the slight bleeding.  the front desk girls were even more inept.  i told them i thought i was bleeding.  one of the gals was processing my credit card while talking to the other 2 attendants with no regard to me, the client.  i finally had to walk into their space for a kleenex.

overall, dr. helton has a good reputation i am told.  but he has to know that a client should never feel like i did, ripped off for paying $100 for a 30 minute facial, when there are so may competitors, many just as good as what he has to offer at a more competitive price and value.  i could justify this is i felt a warm and fuzzy from his staff including  melissa to the front desk, but unfortunately not.  sorry but just can't recommend them for facials.

i was required to perform drug screening/testing as a part of routine employment checks.   their check in process is actually fairly straightforward and efficient.  also i like that they allow you to schedule appointments online as well as come in for drop in appointments.    that's where the quality of the front office and personnel ends.  

i was brought back to the testing area as routine.  since it's drug testing, there are particular about a lot of things (emptying pockets, etc) to help ensure the validity of the tests.  i was told to hang my jacket and place wallet/keys/phone into a lock box.   then i was given instructions on how to fill the cup and they marked it with a red line.   you are not allowed to use the sink while in the bathroom (this is important below). 

i was able to get mostly to the red line and toward the end of the urine stream i realized i didn't quite have enough urine.  as such, i gave a squeeze and got some out of the cup onto my hands (ugh, i can't believe i just pissed on myself).   so i get some paper towel to open the door handle and take the sample out.   i let the guy know and move to wash my hands at another sink, he says i'm not allowed to do that until i go through a procedure check (i have to watch him pour the urine and seal the sample).  this is pretty standard stuff, so no big deal.   

then he asks me to sign paperwork.  i started to walk to another sink to wash my hands which had a small amount of urine on them and he says i need to stop otherwise "i've refused the test and it's now invalid".  i clarify with him that i will be touching the pen with urine on my hands, he said not to worry (presumably since they will wipe the pen).   after going through several more steps, i am able to wash my hands.   i do so, and am instructed to now collect my things.  

now this is the part that gets unusual/confusing to me.  i collect my belongings and let him know that there's still urine on the pen that he had me use.   urine is usually sterile (unless you have a uti), but still ... i recommended that he wipe it down.  he actually said "it's ok, we've got gloves and we're safe".    i said it's not for your safety, it's for the next person who's now touching the pen with piss on it.   he had no comment but went to get the next person for testing.   he also didn't change his gloves between people.   it's for this reason i think they deserve a low rating. 

i am surprised that a testing facility has such sloppy sanitary procedures.  even after pointing out the deficiency, the person seemed ambivalent to the issue.  seems like this could be a good opportunity to help train and educate the staff on better and more meticulous specimen handling procedures.   anyhow, i thought i would pass this on in the hopes that anyone using this facility understands that they do not as a matter of routine follow minimum standards for handling.  this is certainly more acutely important given the recent infection and pandemic concerns, etc.  

good luck peeps and i hope the review helps!

2019 was a very tough year for me indeed, being told you need a multi-level fusion was my worst nightmare. * weeks ago, on november 20, 2019 dr. serge obukhoff changed my life forever, this is my story. 11 years ago, i was involved in a car accident that damaged disc c4 and c5. a year after the accident it was determined that the brachial plexus nerves had been compromised and i began to lose function in my right arm. a kaiser surgeon then recommended i undergo a laminectomy to relive pressure on the brachial plexus to regain function of my arm. surgery was simply not an option for me as i had several friends and former athletes that had undergone various spine surgeries and the results were terrible. i found a great chiropractor and started yoga and other homeopathic remedies.

my symptoms were masked for the next 10 years and i enjoyed regular fitness and sporting activities. i played in several basketball and volleyball leagues as well maintained my regular gym regiment. i felt good for the most part but still dealt with numbness in my right arm. in 2019 that same numbness became worse and i also started to feel numbness in my left hand. headaches and dizziness also became regular symptoms as clearly something was not going well for me neurologically. i visited a neurosurgeon local to me and another mri was performed. the results of this scan were terrible as now the damaged disc included c4, c5, c6 and c7. the herniation of these disc had now begun to bruise my spinal cord and images on the mri showed a potential for significant paralysis if any additional damage occurred. 

this doctor said my only option was a multi-level (3 level) fusion and that he also wanted to perform a laminectomy to relieve pressure on my spinal cord. the surgery needed to be performed immediately and he wanted me in the hospital asap. after another consultation it seemed a fusion was my only option and my prognosis seemed bleak. as an athlete a 3-level fusion is game changer and my activities post-surgery would certainly be limited. thank god that one night late i spent time on the internet doing research on artificial disc for spine injuries. i found incredible videos on the mobi-c device by zimmer biomet. this device was successfully being used for multi-level spine injuries as an effective treatment option. through more research i was able to locate dr. serge obukhoff and my life has been completely transformed. he spent so much time with me in his beverly hills office going over my injury and explaining exactly what my options were. with great care we put together a plan to attack my injury and still maintain mobility in my neck to continue my active lifestyle. 

the surgery lasted 4 hours and the moment i woke up for the first time in 10 years i could feel my right arm. all the numbness was gone, and i can say i got extremely emotional being able to feel my son hold my right hand in the recovery room. the last 8 weeks i have made incredible strides and i can proudly say i am pain free for the first time in years! i am getting stronger every day and should be cleared to full activity in the next few weeks. let me say again i am pain free and have full feeling in my right and left arm. i have been able to walk at least 4 miles every day for the last 3 weeks and i am dying to start running and lifting soon. dr. serge obukhoff is an incredibly gifted surgeon who gave me my life back and for that i am forever grateful. i would highly recommend him for any procedure but especially recommend him for complex multi-level procedures. there is simply no one better!

i was then seen by the medical assistant which went fine, then he brought me to the patient room where i would wait to be seen by the provider. i was not asked to remove clothing or change, so i was fully clothed. the pa walked in, and it happened to be the same woman who sat behind the desk with an unpleasant look on her face. her name was omolara olasimbo. her affect was pretty normal, and she asked me a couple questions related to my uti symptoms. we were standing 5 feet apart and again i was fully clothed when she asked me "do you have vaginal odor?" as she asked the question, she lifted up a mask she had sitting on her neck and used it to cover her nose! again, we are standing 5 feet apart and i'm fully clothed. i was so surprised that a physician would be so insensitive, i replied uncomfortably that it had been a long day but i did not have any strong odor. i was so taken aback that i chose not to address her behavior, but she then informed me that i would need to take my own vaginal swabs when she left the room. i have never been asked to swab myself before, and she also gave me a swab to test for bacterial vaginosis even though i said i did not have any unusual odor. as expected, the test came back negative.

fast forward to the next morning, i wake up with the same horrific body aches but now with a terrifying full body rash and hives. my hands had also swollen up and became hot and painful to the touch. i run to urgent care again. this time, i see dr. carty. dr. carty takes his time listening to me and after a lengthy consult and work up, determines i am allergic to z packs and that i do in fact, have the flu. he gave me a dose of steroids in the office to help with my allergic reaction, clear aftercare instructions, and a script for tamiflu. after my second dose, i am already feeling significantly better. 

now, i'm not upset about my allergic reaction since no one can really anticipate that. i just wish my concerns were listened to with more concern the first time - and we might've been able to avoid me looking like i had hulk hands. 

thank you dr. carty for taking the time and being a grade a doctor.

i am generally against the solicitation of a public review. if i were a business owner or manager, i would prefer hearing feedback inhouse first. i had some comments i was too weak to share during my visit, and they will be heard here, since providence sent a feedback solicitation link to this site:
* parking/check-in: excellent, as usual
* triage nurse: she rocks, is attentive and observant as she gets patients ready prior to appointment.
* person who brought me to the exam room: obviously hates her job or life or just didn't eat her cheerios this morning. she is in a position to educate or calm the patient. instead, here's what happened: she escorts me into room. as soon as the door is closed and she cannot be overheard by coworkers, she snarls "wear a mask. you don't want to make everyone here sick." now, you see what i am getting at? if i didn't know about masks, i don't believe that approach would have won me over. in fact, i already had a mask on. i took it before even checking in, and without being asked. occasionally, needing to breathe more oxygen, i would pull it down. suggestion: she could wear a mask. 
* doctor: whether he was a doctor or pa, i do not recall, but ken obviously knows what he is doing, and made me comfortable. he is warm, knowledgeable, thorough, and decisive. a great communicator, he made a point of asking me to be in touch if nec.

review:

these people are a waste of space. completely empty waiting room, i checked in online and i still had to wait over 2 hours to be seen by a pa. this is literally the last place you should go unless you want to die waiting to see an actual dr. filthy, expensive, incapable and unqualified staff. this place is like the 7th layer of hell. it is inexcusable to have waits this long when you're empty (except one guy with a hurt wrist who walked in after i was ther for 40 minutes). loser staff sits around and chats instead of helping patients, i hope this place closes and all these morons lose their jobs.

i'm 40. never a smoker, full-time employee with a master's degree. i'm not grifting. i have work to do. family, coworkers, people count on me.

practitioner (no doctor on site) ordered chest x ray but no radiologist to interpret result. sill waiting to see if they call me.

practitioner wanted to prescribe a second round of tamiflu, which had caused double vision and hallucinations. i refused.

"because as usual i don't feel heard by old white men who don't listen to me."

well meaning husband held my hand and told me to stop crying.

i lost a child to a medical mistake. i've had flu a twice in my life, and both times spent weeks in the hospital, months recovering from secondary pneumonia infection. i get vaccinated every year. i have a primary immune deficiency and see an immunologist for treatment.

lastly, none of practitioners nor patients wore masks while coughing.

i'm afraid of hospitals, full ptsd.

who will take care of my special needs nursing preemie son if i end up in hospital again?

so glad that i could find lysol & chlorox spray and wipes here today as some places are limited or shelves are wiped out.  heard b&b doesn't have hand sanitizers in stores and on line.  plus many stores are out of rubbing alcohol.

in one movie i watched many moons ago, a greek family's father always said windex serves all purposes but at a glance i didn't see it labeled  kills bacteria or viruses.

also found some good snacks to bring home in case everyone becomes home bound.

take care everybody.

dr. reddy is a stand out great internal medicine doctor.

in addition, dr. reddy is proactive about her patients' health--she reviewed my full physical with me and provided lots of information about my health and bloodwork, and explained recommendations for going from good health to excellent. when i have a cold or flu, i never have a problem getting a fast appointment (even the same day), yet i never feel like i'm being rushed out the door when i'm there. one thing that always makes me hesitate is how germy doctors' offices can be, but the front desk takes extra precautions with possibly contagious patients in waiting areas, including providing masks, tissues, and hand sanitizer for people who have coughs or fevers.

dr. reddy is knowledgeable about certain more holistic approaches to resolving health issues than most doctors who just push prescriptions. she has been the long-time doctor of my father who also feels she is an excellent doctor for our whole family.

to all the complaints about the front desk, i understand it's a bit difficult at times but the complaints are not fair. this practice has an online system for making and cancelling appointments which is far better than trying to call in to a staff dealing with incredible high volume. i don't even use the online system, and i've never had a problem cancelling an appointment. as a business owner who also receives a high volume of calls - you just have to stay on hold or call back later.

by not giving internal medicine associates a chance, you're really missing out on a great doctor/patient relationship you might have with a wonderful doctor like reddy. she's helped my dad out so much and over time through proactive health changes, my dad has reduced his prescription medicine intake dramatically with her coaching.

i've had to because of employer reasons switch back to kaiser and also due to moving to the south bay, san mateo is not very convenient when i have a kaiser clinic in walking distance from my home. i've switched doctors and i think i've been very lucky in my life to have several good doctors including reddy on my side.

give them a shot!

review:
the urgent care i am reviewing is at the corner of katella and knott in cypress.  i see there are different areas reviewed here and that isn't really fair.  reviews need to state which urgent care they are talking about at the start of their review.

a problem with shortness of breath led me to this facility.  the receptionist could have been friendlier but she appeared efficient and helpful when my pad wouldn't take my information.

i was called in within a reasonable length of time and during my wait in the reception area noted a woman who was coughing and sneezing almost constantly had availed herself of one of the masks provided at the reception table.  a tv was provided with a generic program to distract you while you waited.

the dr or pa looked worn out but she gave a thorough exam and gave me a "cocktail" of medication for a problem i'd had with my respiratory system for sometime that helped immensely.  all tests were done and evaluated with the only problem the ekg machine balking and not taking the reading until some adjustments were made.

appropriate advise was given and i left feeling relieved and better from the visit.  

a good place to go in an emergency or just for help when ill.

the check in process is so stupid. most elderly people do not have a cell phone. when i ask the receptionist...what if no phone????? she shrugged it off. the receptionist wasn't rude but she also wasn't overly friendly and needs  help on her customer service. i didn't hear her say bye or thank you at the end of calls either. she needs to learn to say, i dont speak spanish, in spanish. also, needs to learn to look at a people when she's speaking to them, not act like she's bothered when asked a question. tell the people coughing in the waiting room to wear a mask. how stupid and irresponsible that there are no masks available and that sick people aren't told to wear one in a small waiting room. also dumb and selfish on the sick persons part. i would have put one on had the cheap owner of this place had masks available. the chairs are filthy and horrible. 

we waited a long time, they need more doctors. 

the nurse and doctor were great though, both were polite and knowledgeable. 5 stars for them

so i walk in and i'm already annoyed. i brought both my kids in to get seen and the lady at the front desk is checking us in. one of the doctors come from the back and looks at the screen talking about food next door! so i'm like ummmm ok i give her my insurance information and she's  taking so loooooong i'm like wtf. finds out she's ordering food online instead of checking us in! we are on a time frame and it's 3-4 ppl behind me waiting like really your chili and sandwiches couldn't wait. havent been back since then.

review:
very impressed. this was my first time at a korean spa and first here at this specific location, but it won't be my last! 

for $19.00 (regular $25.00) on groupon, you can access general admission for the various sauna rooms and jacuzzis. however, my girlfriend and i opted for the 70 minutes - regular scrub and massage which exempts you from the entrance fee. 

once we paid, we went downstairs to the spa room. we first showered and soaked in one of the bathes before our service. the masseuse then called us in. i had joean, and my friend had summer. i started on my tummy, and she scrubbed my back head to toe, then turned me both on my left and right sides, and ended with me on my back. once the scrub was over, i showered and came back in. she put on a mask, massaged me, and lastly washed my hair. it was fabulous.

i ended my visit by soaking in the various jacuzzis and then enjoyed the saunas, charcoal mud clay room, himalayan salt room, infrared healing room, and negative ion balancing room. these all had their various purposes that you'd have to try yourself. 

they provide towels, robes, body lotion, and hair dryers! great details.

service was excellent, and i'd come back again!
who encourages a couple of 90 year olds to attend a non essential wellness check in the midst of covid19 outbreak? what an uncaring, ignorant person. not the first example of her lack of compassion.

so this place is a joke. waited over 3 hours to be seen. had 3 people ahead of us. once we got back the dr was very unprofessional. wouldn't listen to why we were there. kept interrupting my wife. didn't listen to anything she had to say. when a female says she thinks she has a uti might want to listen. they are pretty good about knowing that issue. instead he said it sounds like a virus going around. follow up with your primary in a couple of days or you gyn. no urine test nothing. not a go to hell, you suck get out of here nothing. spent less than 3 minutes and then wrote her a script for diarrhea. got in touch with our primary dr. by chance and he was at mt. view hospital. went down he checked her out and guess what. yep sports fans you are right she has a uti. got some meds and we are off to the races. next time you want to run a scam please just tell me so that you can take my money  and i can keep 3 hours of my life.

what i believe i have has me in excruciating pain and all the dr did was prescribe me a topical lotion.

review:
doctors are decent. front desk, office personnel and billing process are horrible. good place for employees to pass the buck to the next person when you have a question or complaint that's it's someone else's department. three previous visits only one was without incident.  had a 3:30 appt today and i'm still sitting here waiting after walk-ins and later appointments have been seen. no updates or contacts that i didn't have to ask myself. no common sense that if it's after hours for your workplace you're not going to get a call from them.  chastised for not giving information they didn't ask. won't see me apparently without talking to my employer when it's after business hours so i'm sitting in the middle of a flu season (their words) waiting room of coughing patients probably taking in the germs that will get me the flu where i will have to come back and go into the same crap routine as i've done twice before with no real assessment except i must have allergies for the first time in my life and for an injury i had an appt for two hours ago. today, if i could give them a zero, i would. and these people are actually taking care if people in an urgent care capacity that are depending on them to have some wits about them. i'm glad i'm not sitting here with something life or death because i'd probably be dead. oh, but they made sure i signed off on their coronavirus paperwork alright. probably to protect their own health. 

look at that one star in the review and think zero stars. don't be real sick because if you are pick a different place than the hunters creek loop advent centra care.

had a basket of groceries and was going to check out and all 4 lanes of self-checkouts were open and backed up? no lines for regular check out open.  wtf? all lights for regulate check out were turned off and the was a lady with a red vest on helping someone check out. there was another couple behind him that she told them that she wasn't open? i asked her why ? also, why are there only self check outs open? no reason given? i asked for the manager and while , i was waiting, she came over and said that she would now check us out. we were checked out and the manager came out latter to assist someone at the help desk. after he finished with him, i spoke with the store manager and he stated that the lady in the red vest was a manager and was suppose to open up a line when the self checkout was backed up or someone had a lot of groceries. well that employee was telling customers to go to the self checkout? is this sac and save? this self checkout stuff is really getting bad. the employee that was suppose to be at the self checkout desk wasn't there either? really, this it really troubling for a saturday evening. there were lots of employees walking around stocking and what not. let's take care of the kroger's shoppers. updated as of march 10, 2020 it's a mad house , due to coronavirus scare. geez people.

i have been coming here for everything. flu, virus, infection. you name it and i've been there for it. they don't have a lot of resources but they make due with what they have. x-ray machine, blood work, urine analysis, and can send away for cultures if need be. they will call back and see how you are after each visit. i have had the pleasure of knowing these amazing physicians and staff. dr. mihaela ille is an exceptional physician with much knowledge on an array of matters. she is very sweet and will work hard to help you.

we were a walk-in to triage the kid's high fever. initially, the receptionist told us she would have to consult the doctor to see if he would see a small child. he agreed.  so make sure you call ahead of time to see if they are taking children - this review would be a little different if they were not.
the intake process was pretty standard. we waited for about an hour on a sunday morning. there were about 5 to 6 people in front of us, so i didn't think 20 minutes per person was bad. then again, i wasn't the sick one so my patience was probably at a higher threshold. 
we were called back. they took the basic measurements - vitals, height, weight, etc. the medical assistant was very sympathetic to the kid. she listened to my concerns and triaged the kid appropriately. she was diagnosed appropriately and the medicine was her fever was administered in an appropriate amount of time.
shortly after the doctor came and did his assessment. no issues there - very gentle with the kid. i wasn't sure about the pharmacy i would use so he gave me the prescription and a note for school
overall i would go to this location again, although accepting not accepting kid thing is a little sketchy. 

my only vice is no visible hand hygiene. i can't say they did not do it, but i didn't see them do it. this aspect could have been improved by simply "gelling in" when entering and exiting the room. they had on mask given its cold and flu season, which was understandable, but you also have to protect the patients not just yourself.

dr. brandi jo was rude and didn't care at all. i came in for my scheduled appointment at 7:20 when they close at 8, so she was just annoyed to be seeing me. she ended up telling me i might have a virus or maybe the flu or maybe allergies and there was nothing she could do. she gave me over the counter suggestions and i went home. she never said she was going to prescribe anything. today, i got a text from a pharmacy saying my prescription was filled. not sure why she had me buy a specific nasal spray over the counter if she was going to prescribe one anyway... waste of time and $

this is the worst hospital i have ever visited. to start my visit to the er i had to park in a parking garage no where close to the emergency room or use "vallet parking" which i'm sure was their plan to help make an extra couple bucks a day since the parking garage is so far. then i check in and the lady at the front desk refused to give me a face mask "because i was only there for abdominal pain not respiratory" when i explained i have been coughing and high fever she explain my papers only say abdominal pains so she wasn't required to give me one. i had to sit in the waiting room for 2 hours ! crying. and in pain. when asking the front desk how much longer that i was in a lot of pain she said she doesn't know to just sit down. 
i would not recc this hospital to anyone !

i came in with flu like symptoms, chest pain, shortness of breath blood shot eyes and dizziness. i was given a flu test and an ex ray that came up negative. dr came back saying i had a viral infection and although the symptoms were a match to that of covid-19 they would not test me. starting they only had 50 tests and those were reserved for the elderly. he said i may have it and need to quarantine myself but was not willing to test me. he also stated and within a few weeks they would be over run with cases. unless i was to the point of extreme sickness and high fever would they test. i can not afford to self quarantine as without income i will be homeless. i explained the business i do requires me to deliver groceries to the elderly. he said to keep the mask i had on lol and offered no other help care or concern. he blamed it on the government and said we needed to get trump out of office but would not assist in ensuring i'm not a risk to others by making sure i'm clean of this virus. i got up and walked out. i'm sure to get. $2,000 bill for nothing. do not go here if your think your sick with the corona virus unless your 70 or to the point of near death they don't care.

just so awesome. if they could be my kid's general pediatrician, that would be great. 

the place is spotless. clean and shiny, fresh smelling, and with like a fairytale castle theme going, which as a girl who grew up in the 90's on disney - i can get behind. like there's like knights everywhere and every examination room has disney jr playing on a tv from open to close. legit af. 

the staff is so nice. the receptionist dude was there both times we had to visit and he's just a straight up angel. he sets the whole tone for the place. calm, friendly, reassuring. 

we had to take our sweet baby jack to this place twice now, both times for bad viruses because children are gross cesspools. tonight we rushed jack in just before they closed at midnight (this is now what saturday night is for me and ned) because it was that or the hospital. and just like before - an epically great visit. the receptionist even made ned a cup of coffee. unreal service. 

the nurses and doctors are all amazing and they are also for some reason all hot. they're like hip, youthful, friendly smart hot people who all work at the same urgent care for kids. they are also - and this is equally as important as their hotness (obviously joking but not about them all being attractive) - incredibly thorough. they won't make you feel rushed or stupid for asking a bunch of questions. they explain what's going on in detail, give you options for treatment, tell you what to look for, and always send you home with a stapled packet of information about your little one and their gross diseases. 

honestly i can't imagine taking jack to another urgent care. there's just no way it will ever be as good as this one. 

thank you guys for being so amazing. hope to not see you for awhile but glad to know you're here. 

love always and always and always,

allie, ned and jack

while waiting to be seen, a woman walks in and asks for a mask because she had the flu. the front desk said they are out and "just can't keep them in stock". this is unacceptable, especially during this time of year. protect your patients from getting ill while waiting, please!!!

the first experience i had here went well dr. jones is great actually cares for her patients and really tries to figure out the root of every problem.  i went here yesterday because i have been super sick just with what i think is just a cold but i had some concerns about an ear infection. i call for an appointment and tell them why i am coming in and then about 10 minutes later i get a call and they are asking me questions as if i have the corona virus which is understandable with everything going on whatever. i get there and check in early and the wait time hasn't been too long for both times i've been there. i get called back and of course get asked to step on a scale which is obviously normal. i have been super sick so my appetite hasn't been great and on top of that i am a genuinely just a small person always have been! i step on the scale and my weight is lower than normal and the nurse goes " umm is your weight always that low" i didn't even think about it and i was just like no i am sick. then she said that about my blood pressure as well but when the doctor took it, my blood pressure was fine. i just thought about how if someone was bigger you would never say that to them about their weight would you? it's not what was said it was how it was said that makes a huge difference! also the doctor said i could pick up my prescription there but somehow the nurse got it sent to the walgreens and i even said something about it but when i went to walgreens they said the script was pulled so now i have to go back to the doctor and figure that out. i am still very pleased with the doctors but the weight thing definitely threw me off.

i've never neen to any urgent care before so i was dreading a long wait in a waiting room of sick people. had a mild sore throat and body aches over the weekend and my manager told me to stay away from work and go to a doctor. 

although kunia urgent care was a lot closer, i chose kapolei u.c. as the yelp reviews were better.  it is literally next to the kapolei movie theaters, lots of parking.  co-payment with my hmsa insurance only $12. cool! i was expecting to pay er prices.  

upon entering there was a sign that if you had flu symptoms to ask for a mask, which i did. but there were several other people wearing masks. the waiting room had 4 or 5 people for a monday morning. i filled out paperwork not too bad and waited less then 5 min to be seen. staff was pleasant and professional. the doctor was nice and informative. got a swab up my nose to test for flu, negative. no signs of strep either. i mentioned coronavirus and she assured me i didn't have it. besides, they don't have test kits anyway. 

got a work note for 3 days. i feel fine. time to go shopping and get my nails done mini vacation!

i checked in at the emergency room at south shore hospital at 2pm. its 715pm now and still waiting. 3 other patients waiting with me. nobody can give answer as to what the delay is. and why aren't they passing out face masks to these patients who are coughing up their lungs? just spray the flu virus all over the hospital why don't you? i should have made the trip to hammond st. margaret or south suburban. never coming back to ssh ever again except to visit someone i may know

as washington state declared state of emergency over coronavirus, everyone was very cautious about anyone showing symptoms around them. i had an appointment with dr. hyman, and when i was waiting in the waiting area, i heard someone coughing every 3-5 minutes inside the clinic for about 23 minutes. there was no one in the clinic who wore a face mask, and that included staffs at reception, doctors, nurses, and patients. out of abundance of caution, i asked the nurse to reschedule our appointment and walked out of the clinic.

afterwards, the clinic called, and told me that it was a staff recovering from an illness, and they can ask her to wear a face mask if i'm so concerned, or they can give a face mask to me. i was shocked that they let a sick staff work in the clinic without wearing any protective gear, and politely asked to be rescheduled. however, the clinic still wants to charge me re-scheduling fee. i tried to ask them to forfeit due to coronavirus fears and they wouldn't.

later, i wrote an email to the clinic again to ask them to forfeit the fee because they had a sick staff showing symptoms. then dr. hyman replied, saying that the staff drank from a bad pipe of water and wasn't sick. dr. hyman's explanation didn't match what i observed while i waited in the waiting area, and didn't match what his front desk initially said. 

initially he gave me the choice on whether i'd like to insist to forfeit the fee or not, and i said i already made the request to forfeit, but can understand if he wants to enforce. in the end, he insisted on charging me the rescheduling fee for his own careless clinical practice.

mandy is the best!  i had my second microcurrent treatment with her & my skin looks & feels amazing.   first of all, with the coronavirus panic, mandy keeps a very sterile environment.  she lines the bed with a disposable mesh-like fabric and she works with a mask & gloves.  she is knowledgeable, caring & not pushy at all.  i highly recommend mandy for any skin care needs.

i've had a horrible experience with your medical assistant (alicia) and the front desk. this started before my travels to the dominican republic as they would not return my phone calls on the vaccines i've received. now this week, they're not responsive about allowing me to schedule an appointment. i've been waiting for 3 days to try and schedule an appointment and they pass me through call after call voicemail after voicemail. when i finally do get to someone, they pass me off to another voicemail. not only that, i've been hung up on by alicia and many members of the front desk. they're treating every potential cough as the same situation and have not asked about any additional symptoms or places people have travelled to. so now, in the middle of winter, everyone who has a cough has the coronavirus? that is a ridiculous triage process. i've explained to them that my initial symptoms were gone within a week, but that was completely ignored. i'm coming in purely to get my skin checked out. they will not even allow me to speak with the doctor, who communicated with me through private email that we should meet!

however, throughout the 5 years of care, dr. lee has been impeccable. he is very attention detailed and has explained symptoms with me. i am really sad to have to post this, but this front desk and support staff needs to change. the people who are complaining about the same things are right, all of this is happening.

this is a joke. since i have been coming to northwestern emergency room from 2013 -2015. i would be septic and shaking and have to sit that way for 4+ hours.  one time i waited so long that i had to straight to icu. my blood pressure was way past the low point, like one step away from all my organs shutting down.

with so much going on in these days in the medical field and overworked nurses and staff at hospitals. the st. joseph hospital admitting staff, nurses, and techs have been so nice, attentive and helpful. 

i was worried in getting my surgery done here with corona virus going on, i thought they would be tired rude because they are overworked but that wasn't the case. my stay has need pleasant and i would definitely recommend this hospital more than others i've been to.

yes , that's right a total disaster. they just waste your time, wrong diagnosis. bill insurance twice. don't find proper complaint box.

i've been a patient of this office for around 3 years. the initial appointment was with dr. gowda who concluded i should have a sleep study based on our preliminary review of symptoms. the sleep study was comprehensive, convenient and professional. the results were undeniable. i needed a cpap machine.

all equipment, the study, and all subsequent replacement supplies have been 100% covered by medicare (with supplemental insurance). all follow-up appointments have been with the doctor's nurse practitioner, monique mulvany, and have been completely satisfactory. she carefully reviews ongoing progress and is ready to modify equipment orders at my request when improved masks become available. i've changed face mask several times to improve my comfort, and this office has made the process remarkably easy. 

it's useful to understand that after the initial study, the equipment prescription for medicare patients (and probably other insurance providers) needs to be handed off to an approved equipment supplier. that supplier, in turn, needs to receive all the appropriate forms from the medicare (or other insurer) system. the time lag is weeks. it can be frustrating. once the approvals are completed, a visit is scheduled with the supplier (xmed) which can add more time. welcome to the world of insurance and "medicare approved" suppliers. none of this takes away from what i believe was a very positive, professional experience with a very busy sleep disorder practice. i'm sleeping perfectly and the follow-up experience has been great. even that equipment supplier has proven to be reliable and thoroughly helpful, even if the initial experience was maddening.

review:
an absolute horror show, travesty of medical care, and a lawsuit waiting to happen. 

my mom fell this week (fragile, dementia, history of stroke, and a hip replacement). i called 911 and on scene the paramedics asked which hospital we preferred- i chose mercy general as her pcp and records are all at dignity health. 

worst decision ever. 
how the hospital is run: 
a doctor saw my mom for a total of 1 minute at arrival and 30 seconds at exit. no supervision or accountability. lots of people here seemed "checked out" working in an untenable environment. 

medical assistants and one rn is on duty, one pa or doctor for what seemed to be 50 or more patients. there are lots of guys in green outfits doing, apparently, nothing that i noticed for the five hours we were there. my mom was parked on a gurney for the whole time in a busy hallway. people, patients, staff, gurneys, paramedics, security guards, and random people coming and going nonstop. 

she had imaging of her hip, elbow, and arm. there were good people doing the imaging. i repeated that her head hurt- mom chimed in- and then that was related to the doctor and a ct was ordered. too bad the doctor refused to talk to the patient and just felt  her bones for minute and didn't ask one question to her "patient" aka just a number.  props to the imaging team for maintaining a system and compassion for patients in a totally chaotic situation. 

she was offered a tylenol and glass of water. no updates on what was happening...i assumed a room would be provided eventually.  other patients parked in hallway, including a man and his wife- he begged to have someone help her use the restroom- for an hour. 

at about 8:30 pm the medical assistant popped by and said no broken bones, mom had to get up and prove she could walk before being released. i stepped in when mom got upright on the gurney and said she felt dizzy. 

medical assistant said she would have a chair behind mom as she walks. my dad was helping. honest to god, this was the plan. my mom fell, said she's dizzy, and they want her to walk in a busy hallway with people crashing around pell-mell. 

i spoke up loudly, said you need to get an orderly and she said, this is how we do it do you have a better suggestion? 

this could have been solved by having my mom move to a room- (literally across the hall an empty room with three hospital beds) for a safe environment for a trial run. 

we worked with situation at hand with me guarding the hall like a pit bull behind mom and blocking people and gurneys from coming through....and dad ready to catch mom. and then medical assistant tells mom to get back to 
the gurney after a successful trial run. mom has lymphedema and her swollen legs would be hitting metal. i said no get a wheelchair. then a guy in green shows up. apparently ready to catch mom if she falls. thanks, perfect timing. 

so, end of story- doctor comes by for 30 seconds to tell us no broken bones and runs off, totally masked  to protect herself from coronavirus. brava. medical assistant turned out to be a nice person and she stood by us while my dad got car. she was smart and empathetic once she was freed from caring for 50 people simultaneously with no tangible support. 

literally the worst er i have ever been in. train wreck, third world care. danger. no info. a few decent people trying to do their best in a disaster scene. never again. they should close their doors if they can't serve patients and provide a baseline of medical care. our east sac family has been born cared for. and died at mercy for three generations. sadly, switching care to sutter asap. 

every person who walks out of these doors should get a t-shirt that says, "i survived mercy er."

suggestion: hire some nuns to get this place shipshape. someone needs to be slapping a ruler.

in this time of the pandemic covid-19, it is important to acknowledge the good work and the good people we encounter.  yesterday was friday, march 19, 2020, after the official declaration of the pandemic a day or so ago, i felt it necessary to stock up on some provisions just in case.  i had the fortune of having this particular friday off.  

when i arrived at this vons location (store #2107), the parking lot was abuzz with the hums of cars and people filing into vons like many trails of ants returning to the colony.  i grabbed a shopping cart from the parking lot, expecting there would be none available just outside the sliding door.  

as i stepped through the door, the organized chaos hit me like jam onto peanut butter onto a slice of warm toast.  lots of buzzing activities with carts pushed in all directions by like minded people as myself.  i was pleased that despite the urgency in the air, shoppers and staff at this vons were pleasant to each other, but quiet. it felt like shopping for an upcoming fun holiday, but today, there was a serious undertone that permeated throughout the store.  

i pushed my cart from aisles to aisles, window shopping and wondering what i should stock up on.  i hit the main sections of frozen food, can foods, waters, can soup, cookies and snacks, but not the paper towels or toilet papers, those we already tackled at the big boy costco store last week.  

at all aisles i visited, i noticed that there was tremendous mark down in prices, offering abundance of savings. i was both surprise and happy to save on my needed supplies. 

in this time of potential crisis, vons could have easily taken advantage of their patrons like other businesses i have seen.  people are on heightened alerts for themselves and their families.  the vendors and businesses that take advantage of the pandemonium should be ashamed, and i will document those businesses for myself, and never to return in fair times.  

i stocked up on essentials such as; frozen prep meals from hungry man, marie calendars, stouffer french breads, birds eye frozen stir fry vegetables, pastas, corns, peas, can soup, water, and grapes.  this has got to go down as one of the largest single day purchase at a grocery store for me.  and at check out, my billed came out to $110.51, with a saving of $48.02. that's 30% savings.

within the coming weeks, the media will inevitably deliver alarming warning news.  it is important to be prepared, but not to hoard so that others may also get their needed foods and supplies.  our family has 10 days worth of food should san diego encounters covid-19 conditions similar to washington state and new york.  

in sharing my story, again i wanted to complement vons store #2107 and the staff for being good community members.  it is super busy at the store and the staffs are working hard to stock shelves and to get customers checked out as efficiently as possible. 

i just want to say to all members of my community, please be safe.  wash our hands thoroughly with hand soap and apply hand moisturizer (no need to pay a king's ransom for purell hand-sanitizer) , avoid touching our faces, exercise to stay healthy, get plenty of sleep, keep an eye on the children and elders in the community, be respectful to others, be calm, and do not over stress.  

we are a great community and we will weather this storm together.  god bless you and your family.  

thank you vons store #2107.

my experience with dr. ransom was excellent. i've waited to post this review for over a year (my procedure was performed in november, 2018). often times final results can take up to a year and i wanted my review to be complete.   

dr. ransom and his staff are top notch.  they were with me every step of the way - answering questions and/or  quelling fears/concerns. i felt completely supported, which is key while going through something that can be very scary.  certainly for me it was.  i spent a year researching and having consultations  with several well known facial plastic surgeons on both coasts before deciding to go with dr. ransom. it's an important decision and imperative that one do due diligence.  i'm no stranger to cosmetic procedures - getting involved in my 20's with facials, retin a, peels, masks, ipl, you name it.  as i've gotten older i've consulted with surgeons regarding more invasive procedures, and this is where research is everything!  i've been diligently working on my skin and body for decades.  whatever i can do on my own with regards to health, wellness, and beauty - i do.  i work hard at it .  i'm an informed, pro-active, and some might say demanding patient.  dr. ransom took the time to listen to all of my concerns and answer every single question i had. certainly dr. ransom's resume is outstanding, as were all the plastic surgeons i visited.  the difference for me was his manner.  not once during our multiple consults did i feel rushed or like i was being given a sales pitch.  dr. ransom and the staff at his office combine professionalism and pleasant bedside manner seamlessly.  i want to make special mention here of jillian lamberg, dr. ransom's medical assistant -  her wonderful energy combined with her expertise makes her a pleasure to work with.  i felt completely at ease and confident in her care. 

the results? i couldn't be happier.  it's exactly what i hoped for.  exactly what dr. ransom and i discussed in detail. a very natural result.  

our follow ups have been great.  the care and attention don't end once the surgery is over.  i was at the office quite routinely this last year, at no extra charge.  it is his pleasure and professionalism that he keeps up on the progress of his patients.

dr. ransom is an outstanding and talented facial plastic surgeon. i appreciate his attention to detail and his patient-centered focus. without reservation, i recommend him to anyone considering having any procedures done to their face.

review:
the main reason for this post is that the er staff mishandled information that caused them to break hipaa and i now have the personal information of a previous patient of this hospital. i do not believe this was intentional, but was a very careless mistake. there were several instances where this could have been caught prior to myself noticing it at the end of our visit. 

on tuesday morning 2/18 my boyfriend was not well and asked to be taken to the er and we went to broward hospital imperial point. due to his level of pain he was distracted and asked if i could handle the signing in and provided at check in with his driver's license and completed the intake form. 

after maybe 10 minutes the nurses came in to set my boyfriend up with an iv drip, etc. we were seen by the er doctor/pa (john marini), who came in to talk to my boyfriend who was in a lot of pain so i was assisting with some of the questions. due to where the pain was located the doctor ordered for an ultrasound of his abdomen and morphine for the pain. 

question #1: why are basic questions not being asked prior to ordering expensive tests? it is the middle of flu season and patient comes in with abdominal pain after vomiting for 5 hours. no pain over mcburney's point. at no time during the entire visit did anyone ask about if he had the flu shot, would he like a flu shot, or do any kind of test swabs for the flue.  immediately they went for more expensive tests. 

the er doctor/pa came to discuss that it looked like from the ultrasound that something with his gallbladder and pancreas, and that he wanted to order a ct scan. at this time another girl, administrative, rolled in a cart with a computer and began to go over basic patient information, much of what i had literally just filled out on the intake form or could be found on his license. doctor/pa was still present, as well as another nurse. 

the girl went through the list - name, birthday, address, emergency contact, etc. none of the information that they had on file was what i had filled out and we didn't recognize anything...

question #2: is it not protocol to ask the patients for their birthday and then the patient provides it? this girl was literally reading off what was on file, and each item we had no idea where that information was coming from. they had the wrong address, wrong birthday, we had never heard of the person that was the emergency contact. at no point during this initial confirmation of information did anyone ask him for his ssn, or i'm sure this would have been caught immediately. 

they took my boyfriend for a ct and he eventually returned. the doctor/pa returned to let us know that it didn't show any issues, that his gallbladder was contracted and nothing wrong with his pancreas (not shocking, ordered an expensive test for nothing without checking off all of the other things that it could be first). he would get us set up to be discharged. he also made some kind of comment that my boyfriend had been to the er back in 2015, which my boyfriend has never been there. 

while we continued to wait and i was holding my boyfriend's hand, at that point i noticed that the birthday on his wristband was incorrect. and that was when it clicked in my head that they 100% had some other patient's information and did not have the right patient. 

i went up to the girl who had been confirming all the information before and told her "the birthday on his wristband is wrong. when we were going over information before, we didn't know the emergency contact, you had the wrong address and phone number, are you sure  you have the right person?". she looked concerned and rolled her computer back in. now, finally, one of the first questions that she asked was for him to confirm the last 4 digits of his ssn. when he did, her eyes got wide with an 'oh s***' kind of look. so i directly asked her "is what i think is happening actually happening?" and she quietly said that she thought that i was right. i asked if that changed anything that had just happened here today, and she said "it doesn't change anything for you guys but it changes a lot for me" and rolled her little cart out. i have no idea if she fixed it or if she reported it.

after all of that, somehow the prescriptions and the documents that have personal information written on them still have the wrong birthday, wrong phone number wrong address. they are someone else's, whoever was there in 2015 apparently. searching the address on google i find that it was associated with someone who has the same first and last name as my boyfriend (different middle initial) and the name of the person that they had originally told us was his listed emergency contact. i can literally google map image their home. i could call this person's phone number if i wanted to because i have it due to the hospital's mistakes.

check in was quick and the front desk receptionist seemed organized.

also, the nurse who saw me was not wearing gloves when he took my vitals. this the last thing you want to see amidst the detrimental covid19 viral outbreak!

lots of co-workers were raving about this place that just moved into the neighborhood, and of course i was interested in checking them out. migrating from crescent heights/sunset, next health has a nice new location in a prime spot. 

cryotherapy is what everyone seems to be getting, and i was curious after checking out their site to see what it's about. since i'm not from here, the cold doesn't bother me too much since i grew up with it, so intentionally putting myself into this didn't seem like such a crazy idea. after filling out an intake form, i was led back around a opaque glass wall to a dressing room where i changed into socks/slippers, gloves/mittens, and a face mask along with a towel. i didn't have a particular song in mind this time around so for three minutes and thirty seconds, some sort of whitney houston collaboration filled my ears*. seeing flurries flying around made me think of home, and the time was up super quick. there is also a large digital countdown clock within view and the attendant is around the corner in case you need them. i guess some people tend to bow out much earlier than the allotted time but this didn't bother me in the least. i did feel a little more energized afterwards. 

next experience was the infrared jade sauna which was pretty much opposite of the cryo where one is laying down, it lasts thirty minutes as opposed to three+, and you are able to completely relax. your head sticks out so it was nice to get a cool breeze, and it was a 'pleasant' sweat where you didn't realize you were until about 15-20 minutes in. there are towels lining the jade stones, and you definitely should not have direct contact with them as they obviously become very hot. i think you can wear undergarments or a swimsuit but they recommend being completely undressed. my first time was great, second time okay, as the guy forgot to provide a towel for me after, but i just hunted through the drawers to find one myself. hopefully they'll be more prepared with that next time (and i'll check myself beforehand). my outcome with this is that i felt very pleasantly relaxed, and being in this sauna was nice since it's currently 'la winter'.

finally tried the hyperbaric chamber! this is sometimes out of service so i was happy i finally had the opportunity. you spend about 50 minutes in a 'pod', and there is plenty of room to either read, be on your laptop, or sleep/rest (as i did). there is consistent noise though, and the machine itself sounded as though it was breathing, which was really cool. you kind of feel as though you're in outer space until you look out the window and see someone going to the restroom. one of my favorite things was changing the color of the mirror frame (i chose to keep it at a white violet). honestly, i really didn't feel any different after this; it was an interesting experience though, and probably something i would do every few months.
