review:
i had a stomachache virus and the urgent care was not open so i was sent to the emergency part of the hospital. everything from the intake was good, once i moved to the room it went downhill from there. it was 6am and i was told nurses and doctors shifts were changing. i spoke with what seemed like ten different people and i kept having to repeat my symptoms, which was becoming alarming. 

1.) i had an emt come take my blood and start poking my arm a couple time. then she stated that my vain popped and took off, she didn't explain what that meant.

2.) then the first male nurse, while nice, came and poked my veins again. that did not go so well for me. apparently, i look over and my whole arm and sheet is covered in blood. the nurse apologized and changed the sheets. but the kicker is that he set up my iv. he left and  never set up the iv to flow. i was just sitting there for 30 mins, with an iv im my arm which wasn't flowing anything.

3.) the new nurse team comes in and fixes the issue by flowing the iv and apologizes. i explain my frustration with the two incidents from the emt and nurse and how i'm really concerned about the delivery of services. 

4.) the second nurse tries to put another bag of fluid and this time it's super painful and my arm has blood underneath the taping. i express my discomfort and he advises he would would bring me water instead. some time passed, and i was never given said water, and i was discharged. at this point i'm just tired and want to go home and rest. 

overall, i was very alarmed at the services and the process and efficiency in the delivery. i now have this big bruise on my arm to remind me of my visit to the emergency room. everyone was extremely nice and friendly, which i really appreciate, but i need professionals to be on their a game. explain to the patient what you are doing, introduce yourself and if you don't know how to draw blood then request training. don't let patients feel like test patients. and lastly, i think a little more work needs to go into coordinating staff once they've been assigned a bed. i may have gotten there when shifts were ending, but i must have spoken to 8 to 10 people and had to restate what was happening and my symptoms, which i think could have been evaded.

so far so good. went to the er during my first trimester. was worried i'd be there all day but considering the severity and treatment i was out in about 3 hours which was far less than i planned. the obgyn department is also very efficient. they always have a full house but tries to honor everyone's time. i've gotten blood work and visited the pharmacy at this location its all been pretty decent. i would say to anyone skeptical abt coming over here 1.) know where you are going as far as the building and floors 2.) try to arrive early to allow for parking and walking 3.) grab a face mask to decrease your anxiety 4.) check in on your kp app and keep a your phone charged in case its a busy day. 5.) always treat ppl on the job with respect. it comes with perks.

this is regarding the er. i was incredibly disappointed with the care received. my little sister fainted while in the shower during her period. she had a small gash on her head-- because it was on her face we wanted to make sure there was no scarring and thus took her to the er. when we got there, they checked us in... and called us to the back for an ekg and blood work (excessive, yes, but it is the er). they took us back to the front, and called us back again for a chest x-ray. the np was walking by so we inquired as to why a chest x-ray was needed for someone who fainted (with known cause) after an ekg was already done.  the np proceeded to tell us that football players have fainted and died (completely irrelevant). i asked her if the ekg was normal, and her response was that there was syncope and we needed to find the cause of the syncope. then she asked my 18 yr old sister if she felt a vagal response. i looked up what syncope was on my phone- "fainting"? why is a medical professional using these terms when talking to patients? terrible bedside manner. my sister had to ask what she meant, and she still was unable to explain properly. i asked if my sister needed all these tests as she has been acting completely normal- she just has a cut on her forehead and i wasn't sure if it'd scar. np asked when the fall occured and i told her it was 10 am (this was about 11 hours later), and she responded she didn't realize. i asked if they would give my sister treatment without all these diagnostics tests and the np said that they would not! we felt stuck at that point, because the stitches needed to be done within a certain time frame. after all of this, we to the front and get called back again-they decided to finally take vitals/check the blood pressure of the girl who fainted! they also said they needed to take do a cat scan of her head! at this point, we refused treatment to the tech and said we needed to see an md/physician. the ct tech said okay and said we could go back out front. over an hour later, we were called back so more blood could be drawn; i asked if there was something wrong with the first draw, and was told no- they simply have to draw blood for the particular test over a period of six hours. we inquired as to why this was necessary and where the doctor was and why this was all needed for some stitches! the np came and said she was waiting on the cat scan results before she did stitches. we asked her who was ordering all these tests, and we absolutely refuse to have a cat scan. she said the doctor ordered them and we'd have to sign a waiver saying we decline treatment. we said we would like to see the doctor who is ordering these tests, because why is he/she doing so without even seeing the patient. she said she was ordering on behalf of the doctor. we proceeded to sternly say we need to see a doctor, and her response was, "well i see patients all the time by myself." we replied that was fine but we need to see a doctor. in the meantime, she went back to her office and we heard her talking to the doctor on speakerphone who said that we did not need to sign anything, but simply make sure it was noted in the chart. after some time we were put in a room, and then waited for the doctor.

i was a new patient of dr. armstrong's when the incident i am writing about occurred.  i had previously been a patient of dr. sire's (another doctor at that office).  i had dermaplane treatments by the nurse at that facility when dr. sire was part of it.  my entire family of three generations had gone to dr. sire for over 40 years and loved him.the later part of 2019  dr. armstrong relocated by herself to another office in fullerton.  the nurse who did this procedure did not go with dr. armstrong.  when i called to make an appointment (not knowing about the relocation and sale of the business,i was told that dr. armstrong still did this procedure).  when i went for my procedure i signed in and said i did not know the person now doing this procedure.  i was told, "dr. armstrong will be doing this."  a very young hispanic male came into the room, told me to go the restroom and wash my makeup off and then without even putting anything on my head to hold my hair back started to use the small instrument on my face.  i jumped up and said, "are you the doctor?" i had never seen dr. armstrong but i knew that he couldn't possibly be named jennifer.  he said, "no."  i asked him, "are you a nurse?"  he again said, "no."  i said, "well, what are you?" he said, "i am the physician's assistant."   i then asked him, "how long have you been doing this?"  he said, ""4 years and i do this on my wife."    by this time i saw that i was going to be late for my next appointment. (i was delayed about 15 minutes for my treatment because of some sort of verbal altercation between the receptionist and the wife of the patient before).   also i had to go to a restroom (no washroom in the office where the procedure was to take place) and wash my own makeup off).  i was by now almost late for another doctor appointment.  the pa (or so he claimed) said i could ask the doctor to come in if i wanted but i was late and by then completely upset that i told him to go ahead.  he did nick me and i told him and he said, "no nicks here."  but i went home and took a picture of the nick which was obvious.  after the procedure he asked me if i wanted the "free treatment"  mask and i said okay.  he wore a pair of what looked like pink rubbermade gloves that were so big and clumsy and proceeded to apply this mask.   the gloves were so abrasive on what was already a tender skin because of the dermaplane.  i was so upset by the time i left the office.  i had come to the conclusion that this person probably should not be doing this procedure.  i went from there to another doctor's office nearby and told them of my experience.  i was told that only a doctor or nurse is allowed to do this procedure.  i went  home and looked this up on multiple web-sites and yes that is true.  i was so upset they gave me some juice to calm down and i spilled the juice on their counter.  i realized that dr. armstrong allowed an unauthorized person to perform this procedure.  i called the state board and was told that yes that was true.  i called dr. armstrong's office and complained about what happened and told the "office manager" that it was against california rules and regulations for cosmetic procedures to be performed by a medical assistant (i later found out this person doing the procedure on me was not a pa but a medical assistant) i told dr. armstrong's office that they needed to stop this immediately or i would report them.  i was asked, "how can we make this right."  i told them i certainly did not want to go back to their practice but that i would like to be refunded my fee for the procedure since i suffered a good deal of trauma because of that.  they were apologetic and promised to send me a refund.  it was  two months and i called again.  since they did not seem even cooperative or take my call seriously then perhaps they are still ignoring this state regulation. they did not even have the courtesy of refunding me the money.  this isn't even about the money, it is about blatantly breaking the law and not concerned about any consequences.  i hope other people are willing to come forward and admit that this happened to them.

i did not want to cause a ruckus while there were people waiting for their surgery. when i was alone with the coughing women i went over to her and asked if she would please wash her hands after she blew her nose, and dispose of the tissue in the trash 2 ft away, and to keep the mask over her nose. she just said no and closed her eyes. 
i went over to the receptionist and told her, she said she could not ask the lady to do that. so, i said , can you ask the lady to wait outside or in her car. she said no. i gave her my phone number and said i would be in my car to call me, which she did. 
this is the flu season, people who are coughing , sneezing , blowing nose, should  not be exposing their germs to anyone, especially those waiting to go into a surgical suite!  take care if going there. the  receptionists need some education about infection control at this facility.

warning!!!  do not go if you have any problems with breathing or want to be in a clean environment!

one thing i am thrilled about is that for the longest time there was a person at the meat case in the back that had a serious attitude problem along with a lack of eye contact, lack of greeting, mumbling and seemed to actually dislike helping customers and getting meats and such.

my friend spent close to half a million dollars going here for 6 weeks in the end of 2019. i went with her, and rather than people receiving her and giving her a comprehensive program, she would say what she felt like that day - acupuncture, an infusion - it was like ordering off a menu. the treatments themselves were so aggressive, she almost couldn't make it home. finally when we were able to fly her home for christmas, we called antara needing to talk to someone about the state she was in, and know what were we supposed to do. was it normal? was it expected? in san francisco they told her her migraines and swelling were because cancer cells were dying. no one called back us for over a week, finally we took her to the er. then we got a call from the antara doctor saying ambiguous "positive thinking" things like he has seen "dozens and dozens" of cases like hers where people recovered. no medical advice at all. no one else in the world would accept my friend when she went there, so maybe her health was too dire - but antara accepted her money - she died february 20th. save your money and your dignity, this place is just peddling hope to desperate people.

i have had nothing but problems with cvs. the final straw was the lie they are now telling about getting free delivery of prescriptions for high risk patients during this covid 19 time. you must sign up on their app and pay $5 for extra care to access their free delivery process! that's not free!

review:

i had lasik mono-vision done approx. 3 wks ago. i love dr. siems, his staff is horrible in my opinion!  both my husband & dad had lasik w/ dr. siems, so i decided to go w/ him even though lasik was available at other locations for less. 
i had my prescreening a month prior no problem, paid up front & was given 3 prescriptions that i needed to fill. i turned my rx's in on a friday, 1 wk before my surgery. i went to pick up my rx on saturday, only 1 was ready, the 2nd would be ready on monday. the 3rd one the pharmacy said they can't get & need to see if there was a generic or other option. they said they called dr. siems office to generic option or alternative, but had not heard back. so monday morning i called them. i spoke to ashley. she said she'd call the pharmacy. tuesday i called the pharmacy & they said they'd not heard from them. when i called on siems on tuesday afternoon a resa answered. i asked for ashley, & was told she was busy. i explained why i was calling.  she told me to hold on & then she came back on the phone & said "we are too busy right now we'll handle it later this afternoon & call you back." click. that was it.  i did not hear anything back from them. so on wednesday morning i called the office. i asked for an office manager. when asked for my name & why i was calling i told them. next thing ashley picks up the phone & asked how she could help me. i told her i was waiting to talk to the office manager. about 5 minutes later the office manager picks up the line. i didn't get her name. i started to explain why i was calling & she cut me off saying "well ashley faxed the rx on monday, so she did what you asked her to." i asked what rx did she fax over? i was told prolensa. i told her that i didn't need the rx for prolensa faxed over, & then had to explain that the pharmacy is asking if there is a generic version or substitution for that since they can't get it. which is the same thing i'd been telling ashley in all my conversations. very frustrating. i tried to tell her about my conversation from the day b4, & she again started to cut me off. i said i know your're busy but please just bear w/ me for 2 minutes & listen. i told her i didn't think it was good customer service for her staff to be telling people that " we're too busy right now so we'll handle it later." she asked who told me that. i told her & she did apologize. they did end up handling the rx situation & it was taken care of by friday. 
my surgery was scheduled for 12pm w/ an 11:30am arrival. we actually got there early- at 11. we walked in & one of the 2 girls standing that the desk looked at my husband & said robert? he said no its for my wife . the other girl stated my full name & said "have a seat, we'll get you checked in." we went & had a seat. it was very busy in the office, we sat in chairs along the hallway. by 12:30pm we'd still not been called back & i asked my husband to check & see what was taking so long. when he asked they said "i don't see that she's checked in." he told them (the same 2 girls) that you guys are the one that repeated our name told us to have a seat & you'd get us checked in.  again, just dumb founded by the lack of organization of the staff.  at 12:45pm someone came over to me w/ a glass of water & pill to take before my surgery. at 1pm i was having my eyes re-checked. & by 1:30pm i was done. i made my follow up appt for 10am 3 wks later & put it on my calendar. however, in the instructions they gave us it said to sleep w/ the eye patches that were being provided. we asked for them before we left & were handed another pair of the flimsy eye glasses that the put on you when you leave... not ideal for sleeping in... i know b/c i tried. when i went back the next day, on saturday for my follow up appt i asked again & was told that they were out of them, but they'd call me when they were in. i ended up ordering a pair off of amazon & having them overnighted.
now as far as my surgery. easy. i love dr. siems. the surgery was quick, no pain during or after. the next day things were a little hazy. 3 wks later i'm still having some haziness, here & there. the halos around bright lights have lessened.
 however, i work on computers in a very bright office. so every morning my eyes water non- stop for the first 20-30 minutes. i can see when i drive at night now, but am having trouble seeing things up close, like on my phone. i was supposed to have my 3 wk eye appt tomorrow but when they called for a reminder i said yep i'll see you tomorrow at 10am. they said "oh we have you for 12:30". i wouldnt have made my appt for 12:30pm i have to pick up my kids from school at 1pm, so there's no way i'd ever have made my appt for that time. i told them i'd have to reschedule then. 
in my opinion, the young girls that are working the front counter & representing your offices need some phones skills & customer service training. i would not recommend siems based on my experiences over the last month solely b/c of them

on saturday 2/15 i visited the henderson - galleria location for a 60 minute facial.i had no pimples or bumps of any kind prior to my service. i was treated to the facial as a valentine's day gift and wanted to use it as soon as possible.  my appointment was going smoothly and my esthetician was very friendly. she asked what my skincare regimen was like and i told her that i cleanse, tone, and moisturizer with a 30 spf. she applied one mask on my face and maybe 30 seconds into the application process, it began to burn. i told her immediately that it was burning. she explained that the burning/tingling sensation was normal and said that it should stop soon. after another minute she asked if the sensation had stopped and i told her that it had not. she completed the mask and removed it once she was done. she continued the facial with a hydrating mask and finally applied a retinol serum/mask. when i left the clerk commented on how shiny i was. i checked out and left my esthetician a tip, as i was pleased at this time. i did not wash my face that night, as i have been taught that it's best to let the product "sit in" the skin, especially when you've been treated by "professionals." on sunday, i felt some raised skin behind my ear but didn't think much of it. by monday night i had a full blown rash all over my face, ears, and neck. i took benadryl thinking that it should help. by tuesday the rash was more pronounced and raised. i called your massage envy location and was told by regina alvarez that there was a product or two that should be able to expedite the healing process of the rash immediately. i asked if she recommended that i go to urgent care and she replied, "if you go to urgent care, there's nothing that we will be able to do for you. "i work with children and parents and would not want them to be concerned that something was wrong with me. regina asked that i email pictures and i did. she said that she would try to contact the head esthetician and give me a call back. she sent an email listing the products that were used on my skin. after not receiving a call back, i drove to massage envy - henderson/galleria. i spoke with regina in person and another manager or esthetician on speakerphone. i believe her name was barbara. they informed me that they could not give me the products that regina mentioned over the phone, as they contain fragrance and they didn't recommend that i use anything with fragrance. i then began to panic and asked what should i do??? my face is a wreck. i came to receive the service to be proactive about my skin and now i have a million bumps on my face. she said that there's really nothing that could be done and then went on to say the most preposterous thing: dark skin is more sensitive so this reaction could be from that. my skin was dark before my service. if a professional and are aware of this, wouldn't you be more cautious when choosing products? wouldn't you at least tell me that there's more of a risk because of my skin color. would you violate the retinol policy knowing that my skin is more sensitive??? had this been communicated initially, i would have waited to receive a facial from a  spa that is equipped to work with all skin types. regina then said that i could try an aloe vera plant to my skin but reiterated that there was nothing that could be done. i explained that this is my face and that wasn't an acceptable response. she coldly asked, "well what do you want?" all i wanted was for my face to be back to like it was or at least steps i could take to get it going back in the right direction. i left the spa at this point. i am livid with that lack of expertise, professionalism, and compassion that i received and will never receive another service from any massage envy location.

dr. marsh is a competent physician, with good people skills and a highly personable manner in dealing with patients. he is also entirely about the money, and has created a fast-food, "mcmedicine"-type practice.

a while, he started relying on physician assistants, nurse practitioners, and contractors with various specialties who he brought in on-site at his practice that would use doctor marsh's practice to funnel patients into their own. 

after i a heart attack, and was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and congestive heart failure, he insisted on treating my recurring chf symptoms medically himself, ordering tests for heart failure that both my cardiologist and hmo regarded as unreliable (and would not pay for.)

my symptom's escalated within a month. when dr. marsh went on vacation, his colleague, dr. jose hernandez treated me for asthma, instead of heart failure, and put me in a number of steroidal medications that are contra-indicated for congestive heart failure, without checking the chart, my cardiologist, or dr. marsh. 

i wound up relying heavily on nitroglycerin tablets until i had to check into the hospital and had a major heart attack, arrested in the catholic lab, and was close to being pronounced dead before my heart started beating again. 

when marsh returned from vacation, he began a major gaslighting campaign, pitting my near death on poor self care for weight management and dianetes. 

for the next year he was very capricious about writing scrips for various kinds of opioid pain medication for my various orthopedic problems. and channeled me to pa/np staff for care. 

all the while i was complaining about the treatment from his administrative staff who were rude, abusive, and generally impossible to deal with. 

finally, after months of requesting a meeting or phone call with dr. marsh to discuss my issues with the mistreatment by his office staff and the general issues i was encountering with his mom-medical personal, i was diverted from an appointment with my regular provider to a meeting with dr. hernandez who told me i was being "discharged" from the practice, and that they had documented this (retroactively) due to my attitude towards his more problematic employees as being perceived as "threatening".

this was obviously done to discourage and discredit me should i attempt to file complaints with the appropriate state agencies. 

bottom line: marsh moved and downsized his practice, but my perception remains that he mainly concerned with pumping a volume of patients through his practice,relying on lower cost, non-md providers, low cost administrative help with poor attitudes and even worse people skills, and contract providers to maximize profits to his practice at the expense of quality patient care. 

i would not recommend dr. marsh or his practice.

review:
i am completely shocked and disappointed with their unprofessionalism. i have had strong symptoms of covid-19 and right now i'm on day 7 of shown symptoms. when it started i had extreme fatigue, which led to heavy post-nasal drip down the throat, no runny nose, no sneezing, just thick postnasal that would make me cough a bit. on day 2 i felt a fullness in neck and throat which evolved into a full and forceful dry cough along with a fever which i took ibuprofen for. day 3 the cough just worsened and i started to feel shortness of breath, chest tightness, and pain and getting winded going up and downstairs. day 4 i went to soundview. i was wheezing, short of breath, coughing, and unable to take a deep breath. dr diagnosed me as uri even though i had symptoms of lower respiratory difficulties. dr told me because i didn't have a fever i would not get a test for covid-19. and told me if i didn't directly contact someone who traveled recently i likely would not have the virus. meanwhile, the news has reported "community spread" in our area. yes, i suppose there are limited tests but the dr was not honest about that fact and simply told me to take cough med, pain med, and inhaler and sent me on my way. no recommendation to avoid social gatherings etc. i did so anyway, i canceled all plans and tried to keep a distance from other parents at school drop-offs and pick-ups throughout the week. i have had other concerns about this practice before this, but this clearly has me looking for a completely different practice. i'm giving two stars because the dr was very nice and personable. 

the night after the appointment was the worst night of all. i was sitting on the couch, coughing fit, after coughing fit, and just had the feeling like i could not get any air. that my windpipes in my lungs were completely constricted and not opening, i was seriously needing air. i had taken inhaler but yet was at this level of breathing trouble only a couple of hours later. i went up to the shower and turned on the steam with the hope of it relieving the issue and opening up the airways, which it did for a bit. 
when i was ready to go to sleep laying down in the bed i still was struggling for air. any position made me cough like crazy. any relief i got was sitting up and leaning forward or completely standing up straight. this is no way to fall asleep. i wrestled with the symptoms for a good two hours until finally, things subsided enough to drift off. but i was woken up many times overnight with the breathing struggle. i have had bronchitis before and this seemed to be on another level. the next day, more coughing fits and a nap interrupted with them yet again. coughing fits caused intense headaches over the day. i went to sleep day 5 with the same symptoms. day 6 coughing fits over and over, the same breathing issues. day 7, symptoms are easing just a little bit but i'm still experiencing shortness of breath and coughing and not being able to breathe in deep. still winded walking up and down flights and around the house. i still feel like someone should test me properly. i am convinced i have this virus in my body. and i have no clue if i definitely have this virus and if i should avoid going to work this weekend. 

the two mildest of the symptoms: my voice is different, the whole throat lining is irritated from all the coughing and slightly sore, but it's not a seriously sore throat and doesn't hurt to talk or eat or move. i also only have had a slight fever since the second day and mostly no fever- but the issue is definitely in the lungs - lower area of lungs.

i'm not the type of person that take my anger out through breaking things but my boyfriend is. i'm more of the fixer upper type. i like the art behind the breakables and the things you can build with it. my boyfriend enjoys tuning his anger out through breaking glass or hitting things, like boxing. with that said, i decided to surprise my boyfriend with this fun and benefiting experience. 

the place is small but just enough room to rage, just really be cautious for things flying. there's different packages, different weapons of your choice, no age limit to participate (but of course enter your youngins at own risk) and also painting for cool down which i thought was pretty neat but we didn't get to do it. after your rage, they let you write your anger or anything on the wall which i find real comforting for those with lots of anger and/or trauma who are scared to be heard.

we were provided with the gloves, helmet, mask, suit and weapon of our choice. we got to play our own music as loud as we wanted while we raged! we were able to break all kinds of things from toys to glass. it wasn't my thing but i still enjoyed myself. my boyfriend would've spent the whole day in there if he could though. 

staff was very friendly, informative and really showed us the beauty in all of what they have to offer. they really focus not on what they have but the benefits of what they have. it's therapeutic and there's no judgement on whatever you're raging about even if it's just a for fun rage. for your cool down, you can throw paint on a paper they provide in a whole other room. a lot of the times, your anger/trauma creates the most beautiful art pieces without you knowing it so test that out. 

i got the deal from groupon because i honestly wouldn't pay the regular price. i found it expensive, hence the four stars, but i do understand business is business.

there are staff members positively reviewing this place on multiple sites. you'll also notice a lot of positive reviews on google reviews from folks that have only submitted that one review. red flags that their rating is being purposefully skewed. anyways...

most of us know what to expect when you visit an emergency room, now add the scare of coronavirus... fun... yes the wait was long, yes the nurses were lacking in communication, and yes you could cut the tension with a knife. 3 hours in the waiting room, then another 2 in an actual room to speak to a doctor but it was all worth it. my sister has been in and out of hospitals for years without ever receiving an answer to what was causing her illness. dr. richard weintraub was such a pleasant surprise. he was polite and professional, but most importantly asked my sister the right questions to help diagnose what was causing her to be sick. his people skills are impeccable. i am writing this in hopes that it reaches dr. weintraub to simply express my gratitude. thank you,  my family and i sincerely appreciated your advice and sincere concern to help my sister.

avoid. read the reviews. it takes two hours for everyone. i don't see why they don't just tell people to come two hours late.

this place has many reviews, many of them bad, all about the same item that they fail to address over time. if you have a vision issue, maybe they'll be good at fixing it. there certainly seem to be plenty of people who go there.

we went based on a pediatrician referral. we will not be back, regardless of what our pediatrician suggests. 

first, we were booked for february and my wife and i made arrangements because we had doctor appointments for two kids on the same day and needed to split the duties. thomas eye group called two days prior and canceled due to overbooking our time slot. i shudder to even think what "overbooking" means to them.

i'll also note that our family eye history is strong, so we don't carry vision insurance. when the pediatrician recommended that we book an appointment for our little one, i picked up vision for open enrollment. thomas eye group books to medical, not vision, so i now pay for vision for no reason. i'm going to see if i can cancel it. and i can't help but think a regular checkup through vision is covered, but through medical it's not. 

so after being overbooked, we went to the office on the day they chose. they're only open week days. this means you can only go here if you don't work or are willing to miss a half day. i read some of these reviews and figure i didn't have the worst of it, but i was one of the first appointments on a monday, brand new week, and i arrived at 8:40. i wasn't out until 10:35. guess how long the procedure part of my visit took. go ahead, guess. less. no, still less than that. four minutes. i was texting my wife that i have to leave because i've been waiting an hour and a half and i was standing in a long line to ask why this is taking so long with a bunch of grumbling parents who weren't there when i started waiting when they finally called our name. so i know i wasn't called until 10:20. i texted her "done." at 10:24. i'd argue the doc meeting took less time because i wasn't on my phone at that moment. 

remember, they canceled my prior appointment because it was overbooked and this early morning appointment took two hours of my day, plus commute time, just for a 4-minute appointment. what is "overbooked"?

they have updated technology with check-in terminals, but you have to check out with a person. and that line is another 10-15+ minutes to wait.

so in summary, they don't value your time. they maximize your out of pocket expense. they really don't value your time. they don't seem to want to get better (almost 100% of the reviews say waits are hours long).

if in a few weeks i get a bill for these "services", i might get really angry.

bonus: everyone seemed to be waiting a long time that morning. this is at the height of the covid-19 scare and there was a family with a 1 week old who asked why they'd been waiting over an hour, concerned about being with a bunch of flu-ish kids in a doc waiting room, trying not to touch anything. kids were getting bored with the tv shows and asking when they could go home. one guy left before having his daughter seen. one couple was told that they're next, but they were waiting for a room to open up -- maybe they shouldn't book 20 people for the same time if they have six rooms...

clarification: apparently there are multiple locations. this review is for suwanee. the only positive review on this thread is for midtown, so drive there, come back, and you'll still be seen faster.

to the owner: if my kids need glasses, we won't be back. we will be bringing a complaint to our pediatrician about the referral and will ask her not to refer patients to teg in the future. we will be talking with our insurance about why we are being billed through medical rather than vision insurance for a routine eye check, if we are billed for these services. we will tell family and friends to avoid this place. you have a lot of work to do if you care about your patients or your business.

i do not recommend this place at all. i was told there was nothing that could be done for a virus. when i went in i had a fever and cough. the pa who is not a doctor prescribed me a gel pill for cough called tessalon perles.
five days later i was able to get in and see my doctor, my cough was so bad they took xrays and found out i had the beginning stages of pneumonia and still had a low grade fever. i was able to get on a antibiotic, cough medicine and given a breathing treatment.
when my doctor found out the prescription given to me, she laughed, she said maybe that works in about 1-25 people! save your money, if you don't have a doctor, definitely go somewhere else!

when i read the terrible reviews on yelp (they're better on google), i was afraid to go here for my brain mri. i don't understand the bad reviews. this place was wonderful! i had a great experience. front reception put me right at ease. i didn't wait very long. the woman who took my insurance info was efficient, courteous, and knowledgable. i had a full on screaming, flailing panic attack in the mri machine before they even started scanning and kenneth, the technician, helped me through it-- he problem solved, gave me more room in the machine and a sleeping mask, and was patient, encouraging and genuinely excited for me when i made it through the imaging. they made a copy of the scan for me before i left, which took no time at all. the results were ready and available the next day and my doctor called me with them. all of these reviewers who are looking at the patient portal for their results need to call their doctors. book an early morning appt if you're worried about waiting. thank you, lenox hill radiation at e 77th.
fac_name: Lenox Hill Radiology and Medical Imaging Associates PC

review: i had a horrible experience with this practice. i was already in crisis with symptoms all over the place. severe skin irritation, scalp with hard discs forming under the skin and hair loss. my primary prescribed antifungal that didn't work and sent me to a specialist. i told the office staff what an emergency it was and asked if the have any protocol to get me in faster than 2 weeks. the rude office staff said no. in that waiting time i went to urgent care once and then the emergency room. prescribed a high predisone for symptom relief. it was that bad. predisone masks the symptom but doesn't cure problem. she refused to address it because symptoms weren't present after i explained what happened. i am still not diagnosed on day 3 off the predisone and i get to wait and see if it's going to happen again. they've only addressed the hair loss and diagnosed alapecia (means hair loss) which my primary already had diagnosed. omg this was an emotional  exhausting and expensive ride to have someone tell me i have hair loss that had no known cause. i am stunned at the lack of professionalism and the atrocious attitudes of the office staff to someone in so much need of help and compassion

i've been coming to this location, since they open. i knew they no longer take my sons insurance, i decided to switch his insurance to the one  if the insurance,/ they accept. my son has asthma, and he run out of medication, pcp can't see him until april. i decided to go to afc ,i explained to the lady in the front desk that my son run out of medicine and can't be seeing by pcp, lady told me she didn't know if they can see him and need it to ask manager. she comes back to tell me that manger said i need to go to er. didn't even allowed the dr to see him. the er is for emergency. specially with the corona virus. i'm sad to know that this place no longer care for patients

after working with quality dme for a few years, i need to downgrade my rating. they're still helpful for someone new to cpap treatment, because they walk you through all the setup, but the billing company they use, vgm homelink, is awful.

the last straw for me was that they doublebilled me for my last order. they won't ship an order without payment upfront, and i have a credit card statement and an emailed receipt from vgm homelink showing payment for an october 2019 order, but they sent me another bill at the end of january for the exact same amount. after 3 different phone calls, vgm told that the payment i made in october was for an order in september 2018. even though the october payment was made on the exact same day my order shipped, and the order number on my receipt matches up, vgm insists i owe them more money. i paid again, but i will no longer order from quality dme.

other annoying things:
-at least in my experience, you have no choice over what equipment you get. they (or my doctor) picked a machine and mask, and i never got the option to try anything different. when reorder time comes around, they just send an email asking if you need more, but i haven't seen any way to try new masks.

-vgm homelink insists on doing everything by phone, no email or web portal, and it's not fast. you place an order through quality dme, then a few days later, vmg calls you, tells you how much it is, and asks for a credit card to charge. in spite of repeated directions not to call me and do everything over email (they keep your credit card on file), they called me every single time. on top of that, they call to see if you got your order, usually a day or two before it shows up (they could just check ups tracking). i ended up blocking their phone number.

-there's a huge insurance upcharge on everything. for example, they were billing my insurance $300 for a mask and headgear, and i was paying $80. i discovered i could send my prescription to any of several online cpap suppliers, and order supplies for the same price as quality dme, without going through my insurance.

after being diagnosed with sleep apnea, i obviously needed relief. quality dme was awesome. they were fast, friendly and efficient. jim, who fit my mask, made the experience great. he has such a great personality and made it fun to get my mask fitting done. i look forward to continuing working with quality dme. thanks jim for being so bubbly!

i am very unhappy with the lack of accountability and poor customer service i experienced with this company.  

a couple of months ago i received a new mask and machine and attempted to use it despite the poor fit that caused me to wake up during the night.  i called the company and explained that the mask caused me discomfort and my need to get a different mask.  luckily, i had the model name of a previous mask i used a few years ago and requested to get that mask instead.  

the agent said that i could indeed get the mask but i would need to wait some weeks to order it if i wanted my insurance to cover it.  i wasn't so happy with that since i wasn't the one who ordered the ill fitting mask to begin with but ok.

fast forward to today and i call to order my new mask.  i haven't been using my machine so i am happy that i can get back on track with some deep sleep once again.  well, now i am told that the mask is "too old of a model" and "they won't bill insurance for it" so i must pay out of pocket full price if i want this particular mask.  

when i made it clear that i was specifically told i could get this mask after jan 11 and even told how much it would cost with my insurance, the person on the phone repeatedly said, "there may have been a miscommunication"  i was flat out told something that was wrong and this company is not willing to remedy the situation in any way that is favorable to me as a customer.

the only options given to me are to pay full price for the mask i know will fit or go with some other mask option (my insurance will cover) that may or may not fit.  and if the new mask doesn't fit, then i must wait again for months to pass before i can get a new mask that they can bill my insurance for.  

this doesn't seem right to me and i ask why they won't cover this mask.  i was told it's very old and they won't bill my insurance for it and it's a decision of the "higher ups".  i don't see why i would do business with a company that is irreverent and lacks accountability with their customers.

customers beware.

update:  i was pleasantly surprised this morning when quality dme reached out to me to offer a resolution to my sleep mask issue.  they have surpassed my expectations and have shown me that they do indeed value their customers.  thank you quality dme.

my entire experience with quality dme was absolutely great. from the initial intake/ordering by kamille, shipment, and invoicing/payment, everything was smooth without any issues. additionally, the redesigned mask that kamille recommended is so much more comfortable than the old style i was using. from functionality (no more air leaks blowing into my eyes, yay!), to the improved aesthetics (less face redness/markings and hair matting), it's a much improved design. my old cpap dme provider never bothered to suggest this upgraded design to me and could never get insurance/billing straight. kamille also gave me a great option to repair the screen on my cpap. it was broken during air travel but i still otherwise really like the machine. i had no idea that getting it repaired was an option until she informed me. thanks kamille and quality dme!

excellent service.  they responded to my initial voicemail and email about insurance coverage within 24 hours.  within 3 days of my doctor transferring my cpap supply prescription over to them, quality dme had shipped my supplies out.  because of their 30 day mask guarantee, they replaced part of my cpap headgear when it wasn't the variety i preferred at no extra charge.  my only disappointment was they didn't carry the brand of chin strap i prefer.  special kudos to lauren pernell and kamille marks for making my new-patient experience as stress-free as possible.  i will be sticking with quality dme going forward.

we got referred here by my sons doctor. we were sent to the er and we were quickly in, my son had severe myositis due to a viral infection and was not able to walk. they brought a volunteer to us with a wheelchair and we were in a room within the hour with a bed for my son after them checking his vitals and symptoms in one of the triages. all the nurses were nice and extremely helpful. we stayed here 3 nights after also testing positive for coronavirus and other complications. they have someone bring the kids a tablet or bubbles to distract them while they get their blood drawn. 
dr. cooray was our doctor and he helped answer all my questions and concerns. the rns and staff was extremely attentive and they even brought my son toys, crayons and coloring worksheets and a tablet. the tv had plenty of kid movies and kept my little one entertained but he liked to watch netflix on the tablet instead. they brought a physical therapist for two days that we were there. they even had a playroom for the kids but unfortunately my son was quarantined due to his virus. they made sure we were well taken care off. today is week since we were discharged and i'm so happy to see my babyboy walking and jumping again! thank you millers children's hospital!
fac_name: MemorialCare Miller Children's & Women's Hospital Long Beach

review: the lady at window 1 is checking people in while coughing up a lung. she's sick. her words not mine. no mask either, and i see many elderly people here waiting. this is disgusting. just want to leave.

this place is definitely not "terrible."  my father is there now, getting some intense physical and occupational therapy. ozanam deserves at least 2 stars, maybe 2-1/2.  

in my short, recent experience checking out rehab centers for my dad, i've found that even the "best" of these places seem to be crappy in one way or another. our first choice, northwell stern, was not available to my dad since he was coming from a hospital out of the northwell network, and it's well known and generally accepted that they give first priority to patients who are staying at a northwell hospital, even though they denied this when i asked about it.  but even stern is an old building with its shortcomings. 

when i read some bad reviews about ozanam, i told myself that these people were just nit-picking on unimportant little things... that the most important thing is the pt and ot. well, let me tell you... i've changed my mind. pt and ot is central to why your loved ones are here, but the majority of their days will be spent in or around their rooms, not in pt/ot.

when i first visited, i was impressed that the place is basically run by a group of nuns, and the gal who gave us a tour was very impressive, and made it sound like they run a really tight ship. it's possible that she's just not aware of the nurses there who act like they're miserable with their jobs, or the ones who seem personable, but don't pass your messages or requests for medications on to doctors, and blow off the patients when they're able.  i realize that we were spoiled by the terrific, energetic, positive and friendly ways of the nurses at st. francis hospital, which we had spent about 4 weeks at, and left to go to ozanam.  some of the nurses here are good. still though, i saw one nurse who was on her break come back from break, and then just sit down on a bench in the hallway at about 9:30pm. even though someone claims to have told her that we were hoping to speak with her when she returned, she sat down for an extra break and i had to pursue her.

one day, my dad asked for a prescription laxative. it was not requested the first time he asked for it. when i spoke with someone nice at the nurse's station the next day, they finally ordered it. it arrived the very next day, and my dad requested it early in the day.  the nurse in the evening blew him off and told him "no" for some reason. finally, after he argued and plead with her for it, she gave it to him after 11pm.  as a result, he woke up after 1am needing to go in an emergency. the nurse who took over the shift was left cleaning up my dad's poo from the bathroom floor in a very big way.  he felt terribly about it, and embarrassed.

today, i asked someone at the nurse's station (i won't name names... i believe the problem is management, not entirely the fault of the individuals i'm complaining about) why it is that they don't wear masks when they enter a patient's room. she said that they're "not allowed to wear masks unless they're entering the room of someone who's in isolation, such as with tuberculosis."  not allowed?  that threw me off. i can see if maybe they let it be the nurse's option, but not allowed?  i asked to speak with the nursing supervisor on duty, and minutes later, the woman at the desk said that she called and spoke with her, but that the supervisor agreed with her that "they're not allowed" because of the low risk to them, or something like that. 

with my father's lung disease, if he were to contract the flu or a coronavirus like the now-famous covid-19, he'd be gone in days. he's a sitting duck in that place.  what's incredible to me is that my daughter wasn't allowed to visit her grandfather, because of their fairly new policy that no one under 16 y/o is allowed upstairs to the living quarters. she was confined to the parlor.  you know what?  that's a good idea. it's a shame, but schools are a mess of germs. we don't need to bombard the seniors at this place with that stuff.  but then why are we treating nurses so differently when they, too, are bombarded with germs?  are we really so naive as to believe that they have a "stronger resistance" to a new strain of coronavirus? as if nurses don't experience ups and downs with regards to their own immune systems... it's terribly insulting, or at best, it tells me that they misunderstand how a virus is spread, and the purpose of a mask with regards to spreading a virus.

finally, i asked who else i could speak with, and was told to "write a letter to the director of nursing."  i'm not fighting this war. if they don't want to inconvenience their employees with wearing a mask to protect the likes of my father and others there, then this is my letter to the director. on top of all this, you're not allowed to use cell phones there. bleh!

on the upside, of course, the pt and ot are very good, the place is kept clean, there are some adorable kitties and a rabbit that can be brought to visit patients, and the lobby and parlor are beautiful.
fac_name: Ozanam Hall of Queens Nursing Home

review: thank you to vons' staff for being so kind, professional, and calm during the coronavirus crisis. they were working so hard yesterday to keep up with super-increased activity, and they did a great job. thank you.

each time i have been to this urgent care facility, i had a very good experience. i was there yesterday in the midst of what was clearly a very hard day on all the staff bc of patients coming in with virus symptoms. 

despite the wait, all the staff was very professional and pleasant. the healthcare provider who treated me, named edward l., managed to care with kindness and efficiency. he was wearing a face mask (plastic mask that covered face entirely), underneath which he also wore a nose/mouth mask. he took the time to explain my diagnosis swiftly but with respect, and did not make me feel like he was in a rush, which i knew was the case bc there were many patients waiting. 

i would give a five star rating but i did feel some discomfort at the fact that the nurse who took my vitals had a cold, was sniffling a lot, and had a cough. she was wearing only a white face mask that covered her nose and mouth but it seemed loose and not covering in a snug way while she was examining my eyes and throat. i'm certain the day was hard on her too, though she seemed sick enough not to be working. i definitely appreciate the fact that we are in need of as many health care workers as possible in this time of crisis, so i do appreciate her commitment as i imagine she would have preferred not to be there either while feeling so under the weather!

all in all i believe the neighborhood is very fortunate to have such an outstanding urgent care facility.

my son was seen at this clinic for the first time on 1/21/2020 and definitely will be our last time ever. the nurse that checked us in was amazing! very caring, gentle, and genuine. then dr. paula schweich came and this is where my disappointment in care started. when she came into the room she sat right down and never got off that chair until she walked out of the room. she never once listened to my son, nothing! i explained to her all of his symptoms and how my youngest was diagnosed with the flu the day before all she had to say was my son has some type of virus and how tamiflu is this horrible drug which i have heard this and wasn't coming into get that. i just wanted to make sure that this was what he had. when i asked for them to do the flu swab i was told they were out. all she kept talking about was tamiflu this tamiflu that and i promise you we weren't coming into get that medicine for him! after we got into the car all my son kept saying was "mommy that dr was so mean and kept cutting you off". i will never come back here nor recommend this clinic.

final update: magda you pulled through, thank you for all your help. from one aries to another!

update: magda called back. says she is going to call the or to get a surgery date. let's see if she comes through. 

----------------------------------------------------

called wednesday and left a message on magda's voicemail. she has not returned my phone call. i'm attempting to find out the date or possible dates for my mother's upcoming surgery. 

it's ok if you haven't figured out the possible date of the surgery. it's completely understandable especially with the coronavirus affecting many things and closures of different offices. i'm a reasonable person. what's not ok, is to sit there and listen to a voicemail and just ignore it with no follow up. meaning-if she called and said hey, we are still working on a surgery date and i will give you a call back-this review would be 5 stars. it's been more than 48 hours since i left the message. patients and their family members want to be kept informed.

in the meantime, i will wait until monday to make my next move. which will most likely be a phone call to the referring provider who referred her to this office to complain and to see if they can either help assist or refer us elsewhere.

again, this review is regarding the scheduling of surgery. this does not have anything to do with the front desk staff, who by the way were helpful to me when i was scheduling my mom for a consult. they get 5 stars. dr. lavotshkin deserves 10 stars according to my brother and mother.

what a great place -all the people were patient ,loving even with all the coronavirus scare they were calm collective and i felt very safe in a very clean professional environment for a back procedure with dr. meyer. my nurse marion and dr tang we're fabulous as well- the girls in admitting, recovery, pre-op etc. i choose this hospital- free parking too!

i went to the optometrist close to 2 weeks ago, i ordered my glasses with in few days. when i went to select which ones i want it the optitician ashley arreola did not tell me to go and pay, she just told me when ready i will get a text to come and pick them up. so yesterday i called just to check the status and 2 of the receptionist were so rude to me that she said well, you have not pay. i told her i know. i did not know if you pay once you pick them up or before. there was a poor communication from the optitician in not letting me know pay before ordering so i would get my glasses sooner. so now i got to wait longer which it was her fault. my point is here make sure you guys asked before ordering glasses so it won't happened to you. also stay away from lety and julie avila both receptionist are rude and have attitude, they even hanged up the call when asked to be transferred and asked if the supervisor is there they will tell you she is not there sure!. i complain to their bosses which they never want  it to give his name. but is better to expose the poor customer service they gave me, so others will know what to encounter in the future if you go to this facility.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Baldwin Park Medical Center

review: i am from out of town and i had to come to oklahoma due to the death of a family member.  over a period of 7 days i visited classen 3 times as i got a very very bad bug.  the staff here is fantastic.  they took time to really assess what was wrong.  took x-rays gave me blood and flu tests. etc etc.  isolated to a very bad virus.  wait times were good.  very very clean place.  other than the fact i was sick as a dog.  the experience here was fantastic

i've been going to collin county cryo for a few years now & they are just the best! last week i had an hour long facial with amanda & it was amazing. my face felt so soft & supple & the lemon smelling mask she uses is divine. did i mention i even got a hand & arm massage during this hour? i also had a full body massage with wanda & she is hands down the best around. the owner, holly, is a total gem! i highly recommend this place & their services!

if i could give this place negative stars i would.  the care, or lack there of, given to my girlfriend, who was brought in by ambulance, was shocking!!when the ambulance picked her up at her house they said they were taking her to sl hospital but she expressed concern so they said they'd take her to eden.  after sitting in front of her house for 15 minutes the ambulance driver advised me, with no explanation why, that they would be taking her to sl hospital.  upon arrival, we were advised they had no beds available.  after laying on the gurney in the hallway for about 15-20 minutes she was taken out to the filthy, disgusting emergency waiting room, moved to a single chair, and left to sit there for over 5 hours, five hours, without being seen.  at least 20 people walked in while we were sitting there and most of them were seen before my friend.  at one point we were told there were 3 people ahead of her and when we asked again  later there were 4-6 people ahead of her. they couldn't give us any idea of how long it would be before my friend would be seen and after waiting 5+ hours my friend just needed to lay down and rest comfortably so she had them remove the iv and we left.  the nurse that removed the iv did such a crappy job my friend bled the whole way out of the hospital!!  omg!!!  the guy sitting at the back desk was the biggest asshole in the world!!!  when my friend asked him why so many people were being taken in before her his reply was "please step out of my way".  wtf?!!!!  seriously?!   a woman came in while we were there with a bad migraine and sat moaning in pain in the waiting room.  she complained that the lights were hurting her eyes and that jerk wheeled her wheel chair directly into the brightest area of the room and left here there.  i told him she said the light hurt her eyes and he ignored me completely.  i assisted more patients while i was waiting with my friend than anyone that worked there did.  i'm still in shock at the way my friend and others were treated that came to this facility.  my husband and i made a pact that no matter what, we will never, ever, go to this hospital for any reason.  hopefully wearing the mask and gloves, while sitting in a waiting room full of sick people for 5+ hours, prevented us from contracting anything harmful.  my advise to anyone thinking of going to this hospital is "don't do it".

welcoming walk in care that can diagnose & treat multiple health issues by very good doctors.  you sign in electronically so no filling out a bunch of forms every time. theres coffee, tea, water and magazines available in the large waiting room. samples of antibacterial gel and masks for those germs too!! i have come here for "bugs" that we're going around and they even have ekgs, x-rays etc.  most insurance is taken and the staff here are very nice and empathetic! it's a go to when your primary is booked for a month!!

i have recently started coming to this location for adjustments and never fail to express my gratitude for the staff and dr. justin. although, after speaking with the front desk girls, i was fairly disappointed when i learned this location would remain open in the wake of the current covid-19 virus pandemic. with the amount of attention placed on "social distancing", one would expect a place that gets myriad inflow of people, which could produce a "petri dish" like feel, to close down -- like many businesses and schools are doing. i hope this does change and they take heed of the experts advice and protect those coming in and out of valley spinal care.

avoid if possible. i was sent there by my cardiologist, whom i've expressed my displeasure to as well. 
the doctor is fine. but you won't interact with him much. it's the office staff. they are mostly friendly, though one of the central people i had to deal with very difficult to deal with  she wasn't friendly or helpful in any way. 
and even the friendly people aren't very helpful since nothing gets done the right way anyways. i even had one of them get frustrated by her coworkers and work environment to the point where she even expressed regret that she worked there. 
my machine didn't come with a card. i told them. they said it's in there and not to worry about it. then, they were in a full panic when it came time fo read the card for compliance purposes. if it wasn't for the bluetooth app that gave reports, i don't even know what they'd do. 
then they wanted to refill my supplies. i asked if i could try a different mask, and they said another person would have to call me. it took two weeks. 
i told them to just take me off their active patient list. i'll find someone else to go through for supplies and office visits.
i don't know how they manage to keep the doors open other than new referrals from cardiologists like mine. 
stay away if you expect competence. this place is a disaster.

i definitely have at least a chest cold. i called the doctor's office to maybe get a covid-19 test or be told i don't need a test. the person on the phone told me to call the county. the county said, you can get a test if your doctor orders one from us. i called the doctor back, they said they didn't have the forms to order a test. and i asked why they don't call the county to get them or find out about the proper procedure. then they asked for my name, i gave it to them and they said since i haven't been to their office in over a year that i'm no longer their patient and hung up on me.

very unethical and unprofessional office.

this hospital used to be wonderful. since being taken over by nyu it's abundantly clear that it's profits over patients. the hospital is over run with interns and residents. they don't even read your chart when they come into the room and you have to tell the same story over and over and over again. 3 of them will come in and want to take turns checking your already upset toddler. my daughter came in with a stomach virus with dehydration and low blood sugar. the interns and residents treated her symptoms but had zero regard for anything else i was telling them. they dismiss the mothers who know their babies best. the nurses, child life specialists and other staff were wonderful but the "doctors" in the pediatric unit are terrible. i was told they wouldn't run anymore tests because it's a waste of hospital resources.  i will never return to winthrop again.

no question,dr wyman is one of the very few cardiologist, who can open totally occluded coronary arteries in the country. he opened my totally occluded left anterior descending artery, which had been occluded for more than ten years, there is no question ,he is the best in southern california.
the phlebotomist didn't change gloves between patients. with the corona virus , it seems dangerous. for the urine test, i didn't receive a wipe to use before urination, which is customary procedure.

well, the massage was good, but my therapist nathan kept talking about corona virus and how bad it is in china, really upsetting me with the stuff he's seen online and his opinion about how bad it is.  then even more when he talked about animals.  now i can't even go to sleep, i have no idea how i was supposed to relax while listening to that!!  i read another review about unprofessionalism here and i didn't think much of it, but i now i've seen it.  that was my first encounter, i will not become a member after that!

i've been a patient of this office for around 3 years. the initial appointment was with dr. gowda who concluded i should have a sleep study based on our preliminary review of symptoms. the sleep study was comprehensive, convenient and professional. the results were undeniable. i needed a cpap machine.

all equipment, the study, and all subsequent replacement supplies have been 100% covered by medicare (with supplemental insurance). all follow-up appointments have been with the doctor's nurse practitioner, monique mulvany, and have been completely satisfactory. she carefully reviews ongoing progress and is ready to modify equipment orders at my request when improved masks become available. i've changed face mask several times to improve my comfort, and this office has made the process remarkably easy. 

it's useful to understand that after the initial study, the equipment prescription for medicare patients (and probably other insurance providers) needs to be handed off to an approved equipment supplier. that supplier, in turn, needs to receive all the appropriate forms from the medicare (or other insurer) system. the time lag is weeks. it can be frustrating. once the approvals are completed, a visit is scheduled with the supplier (xmed) which can add more time. welcome to the world of insurance and "medicare approved" suppliers. none of this takes away from what i believe was a very positive, professional experience with a very busy sleep disorder practice. i'm sleeping perfectly and the follow-up experience has been great. even that equipment supplier has proven to be reliable and thoroughly helpful, even if the initial experience was maddening.
