my sweetheart needed an x-ray because she was feeling  icky with some onset fatigue and shortness of breath. we popped into our local urgent care for a look see. this was her first medical encounter of any kind since moving here and fortunately this facility is just down the road from us, takes our insurances and is open 24/7.

before i get into the specifics a little background is needed. i was a navy corpsman and worked in a navy er (emergency room) plus several dispensaries before working in a civilian trauma center for several years and also a paramedic driving ambulance on occasion. my sweetheart spent her college pre-med years in a catholic nursing home then 4 years in navy hospitals and 40* years in civilian hospitals (20+ at st jude) and she is a nd (doctor of naturopathic medicine) sooooo we know a little bit about urgent care and what to expect. with that said here's what happened .......   

first impressions were good with plenty of parking, large clean waiting room with masks and hand sanitizers everywhere and there's  wheelchairs available for the non-ambulatory, check. 

the receptionist ( not sure if she is the triage nurse ) is pleasant and immediately put a monitor on my honey's finger to get her o2 saturation, good. hands me some forms and they continue to take her story and assess the situation, competent triage, check.  you are informed that although this is called urgent care, they only bill your visit as an office visit. why is that important to you as a patient? they don't get into the weeds on the insurance implications but i can tell you from my years of experience that depending on your insurance carrier there could be some unexpected charges singling out individual lab test, x-rays or the physician, etc. that can also easily happen in an er today where you could be seen by several doctors (orthopedic, neurologists, radiologist, etc. and one or more might be out of network or all may be covered. it's kind of a crap shoot these days but for us we are well covered in this scenario but it's your choice, as always, whether you want to drive 20 minutes to an er and take your chances or give this place a shot.

moving on, our wait was less than 10 minutes and we went in to a small but comfortable exam room where the check-in nurse took vitals and after a few minutes the nurse practitioner arrives and takes a detailed history and orders an x-ray. without getting into personal stuff we only waited about another 20 minutes for the np comes back and tells us that the lungs and x-ray looked okay but the radiologist was backed up and that they'd call us with the official reading. she called in an antibiotic that we could opt to pick up if things got worse and we were on our way. overall it was a much more pleasant and timely experience that many er's and we feel confident with the results.    

bottom line: i am happy to report that everyone we encountered were professional and friendly and treated her with compassion and most importantly with respect. the result was exactly what we expected and we have confidence in our local urgent care facility. recommended!

zero stars should be an option. i seriously whether die from sickness than go back to this hell hole. eugene theibold is absolute trash. trash!  i have been in 2 times over 2 years and had to see his horrible self. the first time was with ear pain and a bulging eardrum, the second time was with fever and cold symptoms turned out to be phenomena. both times eugene theibold said, "this is a virus i can't do anything for you take ibuprofen and motrin". i had to go elsewhere after more than a week of being sick to get proper antibiotics. i'm not one to leave reviews but people need to know how awful this place is. the best thing they can do is tear down the building and fire eugene theibold. seriously do not go here if it's your last option.
fac_name: Wake Forest Baptist Health Urgent Care-Clemmons

review: raising price of the face masks to $80 for 50 masks. taking advantage of the virus and ripping off from the people.

the staff are always very kind and helpful when you are in the building. beautiful modern facilities. i saw dr.medley yesterday with pharyngitis. in and out in under 3 hours. my only issue is that the doc said he was ordering a throat numbing solution from walgreens and it did not appear on my discharge forms or at walgreensa day later. i was required to call 3 separate times with a voice that is very hard to communicate over the phone with. i called 3 separate times, spoke with a nurse who said they would call to get it started and 3 times it did not happen. not sure what the miscommunication is but it is so difficult to eat soup, drink water and talk with this throat condition and it seems very ridiculous i had to do all of that for something that should have been done yesterday. communication is key and it did not seem to happen between the nurses and walgreens. not naming names because i don't remember or care. just want to rest and eat comfortably

i walked in with severe back and hip pain after a fall - i wasn't looking for meds. i wanted to know if i should rest or stretch. i asked to go back to the room where i would be seen asap b/c sitting down and getting back up who hurt so much. they said no, so i say down and was in pain. then almost immediately someone came to get me and was clearly annoyed at how long it took me to get up and walk to the door. like...she rolled her eyes at me. again i was not looking for meds. we go back she continues to be sort of rude i tell her my symptoms and she takes my pulse and all that. 

a pa comes in. she takes all my info again. she watches me walk and presses in my spine. she tells me that they can't do anything for me b/c they are just an urgent care. i reiterate that i just want to know...rest or stretch? heat or cold. she tells me they can't give me meds. i reiterate rest or stretch? heat or cold. she tells me that she doesn't think it is my bones but they can do an x-ray, but i should go to the er for proper treatment, but she spend think anything is wrong.

at no point does she take her mask off. if she is sick she shouldn't be at work. if she isn't she should have on the damn mask. 

at no point do i see a doctor. at no point do they even offer me motrin. at no point does anyone tell me to stretch or rest. 

i paid $160 to be treated with zero sympathy and left with no medical advice. i didn't go to the er. i figured i'd i survived this bs i'd live. what a bunch of a$$h@)+*!!!

i woke up which i felt was super high blood pressure in somewhat of a panic and needed to see someone right away.  right now with all the caronavirus panic the last thing i wanted was to go into a walk in clinic and wait with a bunch of sick people! (no offence sick people)  super convenient location and when i walked in i was extremely surprised at the decor at the clinic. it's more like a spa feel then a medical clinic.  well not quite a spa, but close! super clean and nicely decorated.   a pleasant gal greeted me at the door and sign me in and i was seen right away by doctor johnson.  

because they are by appointment i was the only one in the clinic which was really nice. the dr never made me feel rushed as a matter of fact i think it's one of the most thorough visits i've had.  she took her time to help me figure out what was going on.

i left with a minor prescription which gave me instant relief.  she also made a couple other recommendations which i super appreciated.  

that was friday, today is saturday and i feel 100% better based on her recommendation.  to top it off she called me today to see how i was doing...really? yes, she did.

i am someone who likes to take care of my own health situation and make sure i understand what's happening typically i'll go see a naturopath and a doctor at the same time to make sure everything's okay and i super appreciated that doctor johnson was open to the naturopathic community as well.  some drs just roll thier eyes.  

i agree with another review in saying this is a brilliant franchise and i'm looking forward to seeing what the new one in bellevue is going to look like the doctor was telling me about how awesome it's going to be.

i would recommend this zoom clinic and dr. johnson to anyone who has an issue.  she's 22 years in practice which is hard to believe because she looks like she's about 35.  

the easy online scheduling is awesome!

i used to go this office all the time. as of this week i'll never be back. 
after they told me they tested me for coronavirus and told me the result came back negative i went to the hospital after symptoms didn't subside. 
the hospital told me there's no way the results could've happened so fast. we're supposed to be able to trust our doctors not be told lies in midst of a panic. still waiting on results from hospital as they said it takes days to get results back. 

i was also tested for strep and flu at dr paul's. flu came back positive and strep negative. when i went to the hospital my flu test was positive as well as my strep. i don't know what goes on in the dr paul office but i've never felt so let down by "healthcare professionals".

should be in the negatives if i could! the er and icu staff at this hospital is quite simply put: rude! even my husband who never says a bad word about anyone was disgusted with their behavior. nurse assistants who don't have time to make an 86-year old patient feel comfortable or assist in having him use a urinal over the side of the bed; nurses talking about visitors behind their back but in a very obvious manner; staff that doesn't introduce themselves or care to use/learn the patients name. disgusting, disgusting! there was only one rn in the er dept that actually got into nursing to help people, and she was an on-charge nurse who was covering for the main nurse while she took lunch; went above and beyond. icu should also work on their people skills when dealing with family members of individuals with serious health issues. upon arriving in the icu, i was basically kicked out while dropping my dad's bags of clothes off escorting him from the er. not hi! i'm your father's nurse, would you mind stepping out while we get him settled? that would be too much for them to utter. totally rude! oh and the kicker! when i call back to check on him, the nurse states: "are you the young lady who i kicked out earlier this evening?" awkwardly, "yes, that's me." "let me give you a code for when you call back because if i didn't know you were the woman i kicked out earlier, i would ask for it, too." like who talks like that? i had every right to curse him out, but let it go since my dad is under his care; insensitive jerk! for context, my dad is an 86-year old who has stage 4 kidney cancer in his lung, has one kidney, has had prostate cancer, eyelid/skin cancer, has diabetes, etc. and was admitted for a potential heart attack/inflamed heart. like i'm his daughter! have a little compassion. if not for me, certainly for him. at his age, the worst thing is being admitted to a hospital; you don't think you are going to come out. some people should really just not be nurses, etc. - in it for the wrong reasons. the majority at dover certainly didn't get involved in healthcare to help people, and if they did they lost their humanity along the way. if coronavirus hits this hospital, they will be ill-prepared to handle patient care - and certainly not prepared to do it in a respectful manner. get it together!

the woman at the front desk and nurse who brought me back to the exam room and took my info and vitals were both amazing. they know what they are doing. they are both great at their jobs. the pa i saw on the other hand i was not a fan of.  he stood far away from me(at a full arms length) to exam me. never looked in my nose. barely looked in my throat. i get that he did not want to get sick, however how can you give someone a complete exam to help them if you are afraid to go near them. there weren't any masks in the waiting room. i looked. he should have worn a mask if that was the case. i could tell he was uncomfortable being in the room. i work in healthcare and i pray i never made any of my patients feel this way especially when they were sick and feeling so horrible.

the worst hospital ever!! other patient families coming to your side of the room and looking at you as if they don't understand huge asian community!!! i would of never came here knowing what i do now, unsanitary i hate it here
nobody wears a mask and everyone is coughing

review: i received a gift card for christmas from my daughter.  the morning of my scheduled massage i had the stomach flu and called at 6 in the morning to cancel.  i was pretty sure they would appreciate me staying home and not throwing up on my therapist but they did not appreciate it at all!  i was charged $42.50 because i didn't cancel 24 hours before my appointment.  i have tried with no positive result to get my money back.  i would think because of health concerns they wouldn't have wanted me to come in but i now wish i had gone.  with the coronavirus going around you can't be too careful.  all they seem to care about is the money.  i will never go to this place again!!!

it's flu season! we returned from vacation in europe just to be welcomed by the cold/flu virus. the minute we got home, son complained about his throat. nervous about our contact with people from countries affected by the coronavirus, off we went to this location because in the past, we had been treated well.

the front desk staff: exceedingly pleasant and helpful these days. they had always been in the past but recently there has been a slight uptick/change, especially today, friday, february 21st. very noticeable.

staff member taking vitals: excellent bedside manner and very engaging with my son. she spoke to him every step of the way. she checked his throat and swabbed for strep, which tested negative. she continued to ensure that he was comfortable and relaxed.
.
physician's assistant: she was nice but meant business. she discovered that he had an ear inflammation but no fever. we caught it before it became worse. she prescribed an antibiotic and prescription ibuprofen and we were good to go.

overall, this took 40 minutes between waiting and paying (copay $35). i highly recommend this location.

within 24 hours, my son eventually reached a 102 fever and vomitted. thank goodness we had our medication and lots of rest.

horrible.  the receptionist are so concerned about the coronavirus they're not even doing their job, yet getting paid.  before they even asked what's wrong, they said it will be an hour wait and all are rooms are booked.  i chopped my finger and bleeding and, me a tax paying, medical insurance having american couldn't even see a doctor.  train your receptionist to at least ask the patient what's wring before they go on about an hour wait.

review:
my daughter, after getting back from miami, was feeling horrible.  immediately went to this establishment for care and was mistreated horribly by one of their doctor's.   she was ridiculed for getting on an airplane feeling the way she was feeling, yet provided no assistance.  she was informed that they don't test for cornavirus unless she was recently overseas.  the doctor then proceeded to take a throat culture to test for strep, yelling at her and and belittling her the entire time, while horribly stabbing her in the throat for the throat culture, then did the same in her nose for a flu testing, stabbing her so horribly in the nose that he caused her a horrible bloody nose right their on the table.  he then just up and left, without even giving her a towel to help stop the bleeding.  at that point a different doctor came into the room and was astonished by what had happened and provided her with paper towels to help stop the bleeding.
this is absolutely the most horrifying and inexcusable actions from a health care provider.  people come to you for help, when they are at their worst, and this is how they are treated?  your a doctor, your supposed to care for your patients, not insult and assault them.  unbelievable.

i understand the frustration that so many people are asking for surgical face-masks due to the recent outbreak of the coronavirus.  but what i don't understand is why your cashier had such attitude and annoyance with a simple inquiry - ' do you have the face masks in stock'. 

sorry cvs that i asked.  and sorry that i called.  sorry that i drove in after your website said you have them in stock.   it is ok that you don't have them in stock due to the high demand.  it is ok and a good idea that you put a one box limit per customer. what i don't understand is why your cashier is so annoyed that people are asking for help.  we are simply trying to find them and buy them one box at a time  so we can ship them to our family back home. 

and if you are tired of talking to us, leave it on your voicemail or post a sign.  it is ok.  just don't get annoyed. 

for those who don't like to help the sick or the ones in need, perhaps try and work at a different place.  

the staff in escondido and other locations have been more than helpful.   shame on you scripps ranch cvs. shame on you for being in such a nice neighborhood.  wish i do not share the same zip code as you.  even i live in the same neighborhood, i will make sure i drive  farther away just so i don't bother you again. 

february 10,2020 at 2pm.

i love this place. i am currently doing laser hair removal treatment and i look forward to my appointments. ziggy the owner is my laser specialist. she is helpful, easy to talk to and knowledgeable. i actually found this place by accident. i was ordering food next door and saw this place and decided to go. i'm glad i did! the place has nice decor, clean and inviting. the service is superb and simply the best. i highly recommend ziggy and green valley aesthetics.

a really quick & easy process to get blood work done. sign in at the kiosk, a few moments of a wait to confirm your identity & then your escorted back to one of the phlebotomy rooms.  tracy checked me in, star took my blood & it took all of 12 minutes before i left. 

the waiting room is clean & organized with tv's, complimentary water & protective masks.  although i called to make an appointment, i was told appointments are not needed & to just walk-in. yet, if you listen to the automated message when you call your preferred location, it states you can make an appointment online. 

on saturdays all locations are open from 8a - 11a...this location's door locked at 10:59a. 

a couple of blocks from the friendship heights metro station - red line.

i just took my mother to this "club"...(r&b music so loud that you could hardly concentrate and god forbid if you're actually not feeling well- the loudness would make you feel worse!). so/ my mother is 72 yo and post-stroke and it took forever to get this appointment- stay with me...this is important. given the current known covid situation, we wore our protective masks, as generally there can actually be sick people (flu, colds, etc) waiting in the waiting area. as my mom is completing the paperwork, the front desk lady calls us up and says: dr oso would like for you to reschedule because you are scaring patients..." let that marinate for one second!  there were at least two people in that room hacking/coughing and we are scaring patients! i offered to remove our masks and explained our reason for being there is for a post-stroke primary care visit...she returns and says: yeah, the dr would like for you to reschedule.  
me: i took off work to help my mother who is not ill!! i am not ill! we can remove the masks!!!!!
front desk lady: i'm sorry. you'll need to reschedule. 
do. not. go. here. period. no proper assessment whatsoever and they turned away a 72 yo woman who just had a stroke. clearly, they care less about real health care. 
ps- i am a nurse!!!

idk about the rest of the hospital or their staff but the emergency department needs to get their act together. the staff was extremely rude and multiple nurses tried to use the scare tactics on my 4 year old daughter who was already upset and not feeling well for the last five days. we got here because my daughter has been very sick and i explained to them that she hasn't been eating or drinking in days and i literally felt like i've been watching my child just dying in front of my eyes. we had already been discharged from another hospital because they said she had a small virus... well this wasn't true. im so damn sick of hospitals treating patients like we are just another number in the damn book. we are people who have feeling and real symptoms and need help. 

for three hours in the waiting room they were treating us literally in the waiting room. administrating medication, taking vitals, no privacy, super uncomfortable environment. this was horrible. when they finally brought us back to our own room hours later... the nurse asked me if they told me that my daughter finally got a diagnosis of the flu. i told her that the nurses didn't tell me anything. she was like oh well she tested positive for the flu... and they finally gave her iv fluids like i was trying to explain to them for hours is what she needed...  but honestly to use the horrible scare tactic on my 4 year old daughter and traumatize her even more about getting poked and having to stay in the hospital and not be able to go home is not how a health care should be talking to a young sick scared child... let alone anyone who is sick and in need of medical treatment. so much for a good bedside manner! i'll be calling the er manager tomorrow to speak to them personally about our horrible traumatizing experience. not sure if anything will change but i need to speak up for my 4 year old daughter because the way she was treated was absolutely unacceptable!!!

oh, furthermore, the first positive corvid 19 infection is from a nurse traveling from iran with her husband who is also an er nurse. they were all whispering and said not to tell anything about it. figures. i blame dr. david l. reich for all this hush hush. he is no better than his predecessor. they do not care about the staff and in turn they do not care about the community.

i just want to warn everybody to stay away from this place, they deliberately over medicated me to keep me compliant,  i was their for 20 days, and i had to fight to get out, they tried to intimidate my family members/and friends who showed interest in picking me up, the nurse lilly lied to me by telling me that if i left i would be responsible monetarily  for the 20 days i was there, so i called medicare, and they told me that was not true, and i was free to leave, that they could not hold me against my will. the dr. was ordering medications and charging my prescription drug company for drugs i wasn't even receiving!  when a person is recovering from an incident, the first road to recovery is good/healthy food-you will not receive that at fairmont. i had to wait hours for someone to clean my commode, you practically have to beg to get it done and that's a health hazard too. all i can say is if you truly care and love someone- do not send them to fairmont rehabilitation center you'll regret it!!!

amazing. i was picturing hell on earth going to an urgent care with a two year old on a sunday morning, but mvp goes above and beyond to make your visit relatively painless. tons to do in the immaculate waiting room--on demand tv, photo booth, coffee, crayons and coloring books, lollipops, etc. the kind staff makes you feel seen and heard, and move things along quickly yet thoroughly. the doctor was super nice and patched my eye before my daughter's so she wouldn't be scared, then gave us the eye flush tube when he was done so she could play with it. she got a popsicle and a beach ball too. made me so so happy to know this place existed should we have another "oops". 

the only thing i wish they had was a separate waiting area for kids who are sick. they have masks in the waiting room, and at least once, i saw a nurse disinfect the whole waiting area (yay!), but that did nothing to stop my daughter from picking up the used face mask of a kid who turned out having strep from the desk where he left his mask. good one, parents! maaaybe get off your phone and pay attention to your coughing, listless child.

i have never liked urgent care & i just gave this 5 stars!

for starters, i came in with a cranky 3yr old who couldn't breathe (chronic asthma got really bad). he was frustrated & crying. we walk in & we looked like we were at a beachside cafe. it resembled nothing like a doctors office. the entire place had beach decor. 

there was a selfie machine where we could take silly pictures with emoji facial hair/masks. awesome distraction!!! my son keeps asking to see the pictures again. 

there is a tv in the waiting area as well as every room with netflix so there's something for everyone to watch. 

they had coloring sheets & crayons (personal fave). 

it was early in the morning & i hadn't had my coffee. they had a nice coffee selection for the parents. just what i needed! made it much easier on me. 

the staff doesn't wear traditional scrubs. they looked like lifeguards on duty with lifeguard shirts. 

we had to be there for 3 hrs for course of treatment & they were so kind & loving to us   they brought my son a popsicle to make his treatment not as awful. 

on our way out they let my son pick a prize from the treasure  chest. 

i have never seen anything like it before. i am completely amazed with all the  distractions from making it feel like a drs office. well done!

(addition the next day) : i just got a check in call from mvp asking how our son is doing. this is unheard of from any other urgent care. wow! 

they just wowed us even more!

how messed up is our healthcare system in the us that we choose medical care by number of stars on yelp? 
came down with something awful while traveling and was immediately fearful of coronavirus.  found hellomed on yelp and there was no wait even though they were short-staffed themselves, due to staff illness. 
i've never been so happy to receive a flu diagnosis in my life.  
extremely thorough, communicative and professional.  
i'm grateful for the great care they provided me and i'm the mend.

i am so upset right now.  i was given a mask that makes me feel claustrophobic, irritates my skin, poorly sealed, and was constantly coming undone all night (magnets coming loose).  i called the next day after i got it to see about exchanging it and was told i couldn't because i didn't buy it with my insurance (insurance wouldn't cover the mask because i already owned a machine). any where else i was looking at buying a mask had a 30 day return/exchange policy. i spent $264 on a mask that i can't use, that i could've tried from an online company (and paid less than $150 for). the fine print says unopened masks are charged a 15% restocking fee, but the package was opened in the office, not by me.  seems like they should've been able to take it back or at the very least exchanged it.

usually when i come here the nurses, doctors and staff are all very professional. however, not so much today. my complaint is specifically the nurses who came in on 7 am. there is one really sick nurse constantly blowing her nose, loudly clearing her throat, and making very some very odd loud noises. she keeps walking around with her mask pulled down, which has to be a health violation. she should be at home, not risking the health of the patients and staff. a nurse keeps playfully warning her to keep her germs away from her, you think someone would actually enforce it. 
 
the fire alarm has been beeping for twenty minutes and i actually prefer that sound to the bickering and bantering of the nurses. the loud speaker called "code red",and they were rejoicing loudly that the hospital might be on fire so they  can go home! my jaw dropped in disbelief, i don't want to hear this garbage. what nurse says tickle tickle to another nurse in front of patients. 

the nurse practitioner was great, professional, and patient. this is what i'm used to when i come to loma linda. i have a lot of respect and appreciation for both the nurses and doctors, i hate to make a complaint but this needs to be addressed and remedied. when you come to urgent care you shouldn't have to deal with this.

cafeteria germs i ate at the cafeteria at kaiser morse sac hospital and all the tables were unwiped, covered with crumbs and bits of food which means they were loaded with germs. it was not busy at all so they could have cleaned them. avoid infection by avoiding this cafeteria. many hospital personnel eat there so if you touch a cafe table you will be in contact with ever infectious virus in the hospital. this is not to mention how disgusting is the reheated and prepackaged food they offer.

review: 3 months ago i was diagnosed with bells palsy.  the right side of my face from my eye brow to my mouth was paralyzed and drooped. i couldn't even close my eyelid. the cause is unknown but research has shown viral infection is most likely the cause ( the virus that causes chicken pox and shingles). my neurologist recommenced dr. dryer. he handed me a paper with dr. dryers name and address on it and his exact words were go to this guy he can help you ....don't wait go asap.  so i did.  within 72 hours of diagnoses!  thank god i did.  dr. dryer knows his stuff!  he is patient, caring and knowledgeable.   i was very nervous, scared and anxious because of what i had been through.  he calmed me down and explained his treatment plan for me.  he talked me and my husband through every treatment, adjustment and massage he performed prior to the actual procedure.  he only adjusted my neck when i was comfortable doing so - he didn't push me but at the same time he knew the terrible nerve pain i was in and told me i would be better in 2 days after he did the adjustment in my head/neck.  he was right...he adjusted me on a friday and by monday my pain was better and 4 days after that it was gone!  i went from a level 10 pain to 0.  there is a lot of nerve pain in the face, neck and behind the ear  with bells palsy.  he did ultra sound electrical stimulation also to my face and this therapy helped the nerves and muscles in my face wake up.  he also showed me different facial exercises to do to strengthen the muscles in my face.  i am happy to say that 3 months and 5 days later i am about 95% recovered with almost full muscle movements back.  my eye closes 100% now.  i highly recommend dr. dryer and i will continue my therapy with him until i reach 100% recovery.  after that ...my family and i will continue to use dr. dryer as our chiropractor regularly.

i have been extremely pleased with my experience at dr corona's office. when i say that  dr partida and all the other employees at pardita corona center made me feel that i was in safe hands and provided customized individual care, then you can believe they are the best. i am truly grateful for all their continued help. they've been especially helpful throughout my pregnancy. a big thank you to all of them.

sleep data was great! i hardly even had to wait. the rt fit me with my mask-4th one. i was out of there so quickly. the only reason why i didn't give all 5 stars is that i was hoping to get some extra nasal cushions but i guess i'll have to call the warehouse number she gave me kind of a bummer that part

despite coronavirus and all the crazy people coming to the hospital. i came in for surgery.

so my doctors all knew i was in the er. but it was slammed. anyway got seen got a pressure bandage put on my stomach and went on my merry way.

in may of 2019, my doctor had me do some routine labwork.  when the results came back she said, "your blood sugar and lipids are waaaaay off, i'm ordering you to go to a dietician/nutritionist immediately and have them go over your diet with a fine-toothed comb."  despite not previously knowing about any blood sugar issues, i had shot past pre-diabetic and was well into diabetic numbers.  my triglycerides were off the charts.

i asked my friends at the gym and many of them recommended mv nutrition.  additionally, my partner had used mv nutrition several years ago and had an excellent experience with them.

manuel at mv nutrition explained to me all about metabolic syndrome, and what he would do for me to get it and my numbers under control.   6 months later all my numbers were perfect, i'd dropped 35 pounds, my bodyfat went from 28% to 19%, and i lost 7 inches on my waist.  my doctor was astonished at how i'd progressed, and called me her "poster boy".

the key components of the mv nutrition program are: they set a daily calorie target, you log everything you eat and drink, and you eat a certain number of servings that they set from 6 different food categories.  they identify "superfoods" in each category that they encourage you to choose from, but you have complete latitude in eating what you want as long as you hit the calorie and food category targets.  manuel is also a realist: he tells you to not worry about diet while on vacation, and if you are making good progress, you can take a cheat day every week.

logging all your food as accurately as possible is key, and mv nutrition has their own app that makes this easy.  just having the awareness of what you are actually eating makes a huge difference.

mv nutrition aims to help you make food choices that are healthy, but that are varied and enjoyable enough that they become lifestyle habits, so that you can maintain your healthier you.

i heartily endorse mv nutrition!

after our 95-year-old friend broke her hip and became bedbound, roze room hospice stepped in and took over her care. up to now, the healthcare from her insurer was mediocre at best and we all know how that goes. a parade of beleaguered lvns, nurses and doctors calling it in day in and day out, dealing with yet another patient and never really seeing the person beyond the body in front of them. 

roze room hospice was a breath of fresh air and our saviour. i don't know how we would have taken care of her without the tireless and loving care from them. from the get-go they knew exactly what to do, ordering a hospital bed and all the necessary accouterments for her comfort. they knew the drill--diapers and wipes, her meds, an over the bed table, bedrails, a nebulizer, even an air mattress to keep the bed sores away. within hours of roze room taking over, everything was delivered and put in place, setting the stage for her optimal care and comfort. 

the roze room staff was top notch. laura, joy, keith, dr. patel, eryn, gareth, irma, and libby were all ever so professional and had plenty of heart. like me, they became enamored by our friend and took the time to get to know her.  it showed in how she was treated-- with genuine kindness and heartfelt compassion from day one up until the day of her passing. after her passing, laura and some of the caregivers were kind enough to follow up with condolence texts and touching notes as if she were family.  laura even helped me with returning all of the medical equipment and instructed me on how to safely dispose of the unused medications. 

the one piece of  feedback i would give to roze room is that i wish we had better direct access to her care team via mobile phone and text. i can understand why patients have to go through the main number to get a hold of her caregivers, but direct access to them would have been so much better. that being said, the switchboard was extremely responsive and quick in getting our messages out to the caregivers and laura the rn was kind enough to give me her number so that i could call and text when i needed to. 

thank you roze room. so grateful that you were there for us!

jeff banas seemed quite nice, knowledgeable and professional when i spoke to him on the phone about my injury. i went to his office and was put in a private room for initial treatment. i was a bit dismayed at the cleanliness of the room, or lack there of, but i overlooked it. he had me lay down on the table without the typical paper on the table and used a paper towel so my face didn't touch it. he started with a tens unit and proceeded with a thorough adjustment. i was in tremendous pain and decided to return for subsequent visits because he seemed to be thorough, as i said, and i didn't want to delay treatment anymore to find another provider. 

on the next visit it was what i described above only the treatment following the tens session was seemingly rushed and less thorough. i have had many chiropractic treatments and am familiar with the process. but i thought that perhaps he was dealing with a tight schedule or something of that nature. again, i was in tremendous pain and was a bit desperate so i made another appointment. the room was still in the same condition with a dirty floor and dust. he still didn't put paper on the table and used a paper towel for my face. all i could think about was the fact that, since the rest of the room was dirty, what gross bacteria are lurking on that table where person after person lays down with their sweat, dirty clothes, and viruses. still desperate, i schedule two appointments for the following week. 

now for the third visit...i arrived at the appointment about 20 minutes early and the door was locked with the lights off. i thought that he would still arrive for the scheduled appointment and so i waited in my car for him to arrive. after waiting for 35 minutes i finally left. 

i went to the next appointment i had scheduled the week prior and asked him where he had been and he said that he thought he had notified me. seriously? clearly the same person who does the cleaning takes care of the administrative duties and they have zero regard for the pain the patients are in. 

and then there was the actual session; still dirty, still no paper. he had me lay down and put the tens unit on. it turned itself off after the specified time and i waited for him to come back in. after waiting about 15 minutes i pulled off the gel pads from my back. i was appalled to find that they were filthy and appeared to have been used probably dozens of times if not more. i had never considered the possibility that the pads he was placing on my back were not new. in all of my other chiropractic experiences new pads are used for each patient and then kept in an individual bag with the patient's name on it. i seriously wanted to vomit. how incredibly unsanitary! few things have disgusted me more than to imagine all of the people they had been stuck to and how dirty they must be to make the pads look so incredibly dirty. he probably bills every patient's insurance for pads on top of it. after i went outside the room to find him he came back in and did another half ass adjustment that took all of 60 seconds. 

so, if you don't mind a filthy environment, disgusting tools and being stood up for your appointment, jeff banas is your guy!!!

i got the fraxel laser package because i wanted to improve the acne scars and skin texture on my cheeks. this is my second laser treatment, but first time at spb. the staff is friendly and my laser tech, david, is great at his job. during my first consultation i bought some products from their own skincare line, pmd, because i was told they would really help with the recovery process after each laser treatment. here are the products i got:

-radiance brightening pads (kojic acid, arbutin, emblica). the pack comes with 60 pads and the solution was packaged separately for you to mix in. i really liked the idea of this product but it felt like there wasn't enough solution to adequately soak all the pads and that made me slightly disappointed.
-super hydrator hyaluronic acid/collagen. apparently this serum has a super high concentration of hyaluronic acid but it feels like any other hyaluronic acid serum to me. not impressed with this since i already have a similar product that would do just as well at hydrating. 
-coconut bio-cell mask. love this mask for post-laser procedure days. it's insanely soothing on my painful, red skin right after laser and it smells great too! please don't skip out on this sheet mask!

before each treatment, i have to come in an hour early to apply the numbing cream on my face. they give me two layers every 30 minutes for an hour, then it's laser time. on average i would say the entire time i spent at the clinic was about 3 hours. 

overall, i would recommend spb for cosmetic needs and david as a laser tech. :)

after many sleepless nights of researching treatments and questioning if they will work, i decided to give this place a try. i have acne scarring on my cheeks and temple area. i didn't know what to expect and i was nervous but the staff there made me feel good and wanted the best results for me. i've had 3 fraxel laser treatments so far and i'm so happy with the results. i also ended up switching to their skincare line. since my skin is so sensitive i thought i was going to breakout. but i didn't my skin looks healthy, moisturized, and hydrated. down below i'm going to lists everything i purchased and my fraxel experience. 

pre fraxel- i purchased there trinity line which i love it has a hydrate liquid, clarity moisturizer, and sunscreen.i  also bought brightening pads because my skin is a little tan. i would also recommend there coconut mask. i love this thing it makes my skin feel hydrated and glowing.  and it really helps my skin post treatments. it is pricey and you can buy other's elsewhere but for me i wanted to stick with their products. 

fraxel- the treatment is painful but tolerable, and after there done they put the coconut mask and ice packs on your face.  my advise stay there as long as possible after your treatment since there ice packs are free and they do help out with the swelling. 

post fraxel- my swelling went away after 3 days but the redness was there for about a 2 weeks. i was advised to hydrate 5 times a day so i had to take my bottle of liquid hydrate to work.  i also stayed out of the sun for about 3 weeks. stay our of the sun!! i remember my second treatment after a week and like 5 days i went to a dodger game and later that night my face was so red. i did feel like it broke up some collagen to. if you do go in the sun wear a hat and keep applying sunscreen. also i wouldn'trecommendgoing to the gym for about 3 weeks. i went a week after my first treatment and after my skin was really red. 

experience- i wish i would have gone sooner. this place is amazing and i feel good about my skin and comfortable. the staff is so good especially devin she was the one i was emailing with any of my concerns and questions. although my scars didn't go away completely i'm happy with my progress. i still have a bellafill to do so i'll update this review soon. thank you skinperfectbrothers.

ok i think it's time i finally wrote a review, i actually sometimes forget that i had surgery (its a good thing) so i forgot to write a review. i got my lasik surgery back in the summer of 2017. i had already done my research months prior before going in to get my free consultation. after the consultation and seeing that i qualified i right away decided to get it and set up my procedure for both eyes (they asked if i wanted to do one eye at a time, but i decided to go with both at once.) a week later i was dropped off by my brother, i filled out the paperwork and then dr. rouweyha came in and explained how the procedure was going to go (again i had already seen videos and simulations of the surgery so i had an idea of how it was going to be) i felt at ease. we got into the surgery room and i kid you not i was in there for no longer than 6 minutes tops. i felt no pain, the only discomfort i felt was if anything pressure in my eye at the beginning when they set up an assistant device so you don't blink. your eyes are numb so you don't feel anything other than pressure and that's only while they put the device on you. the laser was on each eye maybe for 10/15 seconds they didn't spend more than 2 minutes on each eye from preparation to actual laser usage. and i was pretty blind. i used to be a -5.25 prescription and by the time i got out of the surgery room i was already seeing better than i used to with no glasses/contacts. my brother picked me up (because due to sensitivity you can't drive yourself) they advise you to go home and sleep and that's exactly what i did. i had little sleep the night before (planned) so that i could get home after the surgery and sleep (my surgery was scheduled in the morning, first one of the day actually). i got home and slept for about 8 hrs...i did eat on my way home and took some type of night time medicine can't remember exactly what, might've been nyquil or night time tylenol. but by the time i woke up i could say that i was already seeing near perfect ! the following day i felt comfortable enough to drive myself to the follow up check up where everything came out perfect. i wasn't at 20/20 yet wasn't expected to be til about a month or so since the eyes had to heal and with the healing came the improvements in vision.  by about the 3rd follow up appointment i was at 20/20 and by the end of the follow ups one of my eyes was actually better than 20/20. everyone at the office was super nice and caring all throughout the first visit i had, for my consultation, to the post year follow ups....whenever anyone asks if it was worth the $$$$ i say without hesitation yes!!! worth every penny of it. and i tell all of my friends, family members and coworkers that wear glasses or contacts that they should get lasik if they qualify for it, they won't regret it. it's obviously vegas (a desert) here and it's already going to be 3 yrs since i had the surgery and i've yet to suffer from dry eyes which is one of the fears about getting lasik. no problems yet, as long as you follow their care directions for post surgery and use all the drops and take good care of your eyes by not rubbing them and by sleeping with the protective eye mask you'll be fine. i definitely recommend lasik for anyone that's considering it.

this is going to personally be the hardest review i've ever written. it is with a sad yet grateful heart, that i commend the doctors, nurses, and technicians of inova childrens hospital. the people who work here have the kindest and most loving of demeanors, absolutely care about kids and their parents who worry so much, and i can't think of many places that truly are as loving as this place right here. i absolutely with five stars recommend this facility, and want to give the staff here the biggest possible shout out of support that i can. all of us human beings suffer the mammalian struggle, it's what we do that matters, and my hope is that you'll embrace each day and others on the journey. yes my oldest son was pronounced dead here. he had already died of a massive angelman syndrome related seizure, that triggered cardiac arrest at age five. it is the worst experience a parent can go through, and i don't want your sorrow, but if you could donate blood to your fellow humans that will help. the staff here that night kept me, from literally destroying everything as this is a living nightmare that took years to get through. never over. through.

before that my oldest went here for everything from the nasty rotavirus to seizures. multiple visits and my youngest has been here for respiratory issues. he's a bigger boy now, but guess where i'd go if he had a medical emergency. here. with love to all paramedics, i'm going to insist here. the doctors and nurses do everything they can, and honestly i have no idea how they work here everyday, as it definitely takes a special breed. it's a very clean facility, and getting in and out of here is relatively easy. also they don't forget who you are. it is a sad but wonderful circle of life, that on the night all was crushed, the same nurse who helped my oldest multiple times held on to his brother and loved on him. that as tear inducing as it is, that is a love of the highest i've ever seen. definitely you're in great hands here! while no parent wants their kid in the hospital, i recommend inova children's for everything.

'nope, i don't believe that's good enough!' there's no 'across the board cleaning standard', nor testing done of these individual places, to assure that the public is truly safe.
